added_or_revised.reason: Extended tests are new. The old Annex 4 / 1 had no equivalent obligation.

added_or_revised.new_text: The reported information is not intended to be shared publicly.
added_or_revised.reason: New sentence with no equivalent in old 7.2.3.1. It adds a confidentiality constraint on the information reported.

added_or_revised.new_text: In the extended test for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (4.2.5.2.18.2), the test shall be executed at least with a static and pedestrian target of a different type and/or size.
added_or_revised.reason: Old 4.2.5.2.9.2.1(a) only varied pedestrian size, in a plain crossing scenario. This variation covers both the static target and the pedestrian target, and applies to the newly introduced drive around scenario 4.2.5.2.18.

added_or_revised.new_text: The driver shall be deemed to have insufficient engagement when this leads to one DCA following a system-initiated manoeuvre performed when the driver is deemed to be disengaged (as per paragraph 5.3.7.2.4.10.). Counting is reset when the system is no longer disabled.
added_or_revised.reason: Criterion (d) is new. It is tied to the new collision-mitigation manoeuvre provision in 5.3.7.2.4.10 and has no old counterpart. The reset rule that applies to it is repeated here.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. Old and new 6.2.4.1(a) are verbatim identical: 1.4 s after the start of lateral movement. However, the new 6.2.4.1 adds a closing paragraph, absent in the old text, that lets the system deviate from this assessment at speeds up to 60 km/h. It is conditional on the manufacturer explaining distances and timings to the Type Approval Authority and providing controllability evidence. That paragraph qualifies the assessment this requirement mandates, so the old unconditional wording is no longer accurate, and the previous 'unchanged' decision is overturned. The 1.4 s assumption itself is retained and is not replaced by the neighbouring 6.2.4.1(b) timings. The neighbouring clauses 6.2.4.2 to 6.2.4.4 are textually unchanged and refer to 6.2.4.1, so they do not alter the obligation. The new text is cited from the supplied new 6.2.4.1, spanning pages 26-27.
added_or_revised.new_text: The DCAS shall perform the assessment of the approaching vehicle's deceleration with the assumption that the approaching vehicle begins its deceleration 1.4 seconds after the system starts the lateral movement of the lane change procedure. At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from this assessment; in these cases the manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the distances and timings for an approaching vehicle under which a lane change manoeuvre can be started, and provide evidence that those situations are deemed controllable for other road users.

In the base test for the longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the VUT shall approach the impact point with the cyclist target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test.
added_or_revised.reason: Repeated wording from the stationary bicycle test (4.2.5.2.8.1.2) now applies to the newly introduced longitudinally moving bicycle target scenario (4.2.5.2.16). The new procedure scope creates a separately applicable obligation, so it is not a modification or duplicate of an old requirement.

added_or_revised.new_text: Base Test: the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a cut-out of the lead M1 category vehicle when other vehicles are fully or partially blocking the lane.
added_or_revised.reason: New scenario 4.2.5.2.17 'Cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle'. The old 4.2.5.2.5.1 base test covers cut-out of the lead M1 vehicle without blocking vehicles. The blocking-vehicle condition extends the test scope, so this is a separate, newly scoped test obligation and not a renumbering.

added_or_revised.new_text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs, if the driver is deemed, as per the strategy, not to be in an appropriate position to operate the vehicle controls for 10 seconds, an HOR shall be given.
added_or_revised.reason: New trigger (driver not in an appropriate position for 10 s) producing an HOR, within the HOR-withholding mode with system-initiated manoeuvres. The old HOR rules are tied to motoric disengagement (5.5.4.2.6.1.1) and to boundary conditions (5.5.4.2.6.5.1/.2). None of them covers this trigger, so it is not a restatement.

added_or_revised.new_text: At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from the 6.2.4.1 assessment of the approaching vehicle's deceleration.
added_or_revised.reason: New permission absent from old 6.2.4.1, which had no speed-based deviation.

added_or_revised.new_text: For the extended test in Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist; demonstrating that the system does not unreasonably change its control strategy for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection), the test shall be executed at least with different target vehicle types or categories.
added_or_revised.reason: New scenario 4.2.5.2.20 (oncoming vehicle and cyclist). The same wording in the old 4.2.5.2.13.2.1(a) applies to a different scenario without a cyclist, so this is a separately scoped obligation.

added_or_revised.new_text: If the driver remains disengaged, the system shall initiate a driver unavailability response at the latest 10 seconds after it has detected to be beyond a system boundary.
added_or_revised.reason: New 10-second timing obligation not in old clause.

added_or_revised.new_text: Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall continue to grant extensions of existing approvals to any preceding series of amendments to this Regulation.
added_or_revised.reason: Old 16.7 required continuing to grant extensions of existing approvals to the original version (00 series) only. New 16.3.2 applies the same obligation to any preceding series of amendments, which widens the scope. No base requirement R-ID represents old 16.7, so existing_id is null.

added_or_revised.new_text: For the extended test in Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the test shall be executed at least with different lane positions of the vehicles and target.
added_or_revised.reason: Separately scoped test variation for the new scenario. The old lane-position items apply to other scenarios (4.2.5.2.13 and 4.2.5.2.14).

Track B handoff (R-013, modified_existing) resolved as modified. The old 5.3.5.1 required the system to transition into 'stand-by' mode when a boundary was exceeded. The new 5.3.5.1 (page 9) requires the system or applicable feature to leave 'active' mode, with an exception for the driver unavailability response. This changes the target mode and adds the exception, so the old obligation is replaced rather than unchanged. Evidence: the new clause applies when DCAS or a feature is in 'on' mode, and the old text was a direct counterpart of the same sentence. Neighboring 5.3.5.1.1 and 5.5.3.3.3 still reference 'stand-by' transitions, but they are separate obligations and do not restore the old rule. The new clause's additional rules on disengaged-driver behaviour, the 10 s driver unavailability response and assistance termination are separate obligations. They are not folded into R-013; only the boundary-exceeded mode-exit obligation is carried here. The 'stand-by' wording is no longer mandated for this trigger, so the change is substantive.
added_or_revised.new_text: If the system identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded while DCAS or a DCAS feature is in 'on' mode, the system or the applicable feature shall leave the 'active' mode, with the exception of the driver unavailability response, and shall immediately notify the driver in accordance with the manufacturer's strategies (paragraph 5.3.5.2) and the HMI requirements of paragraph 5.5.4.1.

added_or_revised.reason: The previous 'unchanged' decision is not supported. The 3.0 m/s² and 1-second-distance sentence in 6.2.4.1 is verbatim identical in old and new text. However, the new 6.2.4.1 (pages 26-27) adds a sentence: 'At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from this assessment', with manufacturer explanation and evidence obligations. This sentence sits inside the same paragraph and directly modifies how the old obligation is assessed and applied, so it is a change to the applicability and conditions of R-089, not a separate procedure. The old text states the obligation without exception, and the new text introduces an exception for speeds up to 60 km/h with documentation duties. The neighbouring clauses 6.2.4, 6.2.4.2, 6.2.4.3 and 6.2.4.4 are textually unchanged. They still refer to 6.2.4.1, so they need no separate modification. No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs list is empty), so none needed resolution. The new_text keeps the original obligation and adds the 60 km/h deviation condition, citing new paragraph 6.2.4.1.
added_or_revised.new_text: When there is an approaching vehicle during a lane change, the DCAS system shall be designed to not make the approaching vehicle decelerate at a higher level than 3.0 m/s² in order to ensure that the distance between the two vehicles is never less than that which the DCAS vehicle travels in 1 second, assessed assuming the approaching vehicle begins its deceleration 1.4 s after the system starts the lateral movement of the lane change and either 0.4 s after the lane change manoeuvre starts (if the approaching vehicle was detected for at least 1.0 s immediately before the manoeuvre starts) or 1.4 s after the manoeuvre starts. At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from this assessment; in that case the manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the distances and timings for an approaching vehicle under which a lane change can be started, and provide evidence that those situations are deemed controllable for other road users.

added_or_revised.reason: Handoff resolved as modified (modified_existing, R-021). The same obligation, paragraph 5.3.7.2.1.1, is in both versions (old p.10, new p.11), so it is not a new procedure and not removed. The old gate was 'driver is not detected to be disengaged'. The new text uses 'not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start'. That adds a 2-second time qualifier and a changed criterion with cross-references to the deeming rules. Conditions (a)-(c) by manoeuvre type are unchanged. The final sentence, that motoric disengagement may not be considered when HORs are withheld, is retained in the new clause, and the previous decision's new_text kept it as well. The handoff obligation text omitted this sentence, but the clause text includes it, so it is retained here as an applicability condition. Neighbouring clauses 5.3.7.2.1.2 (detection range) and 5.5.4.2.5.x (visual disengagement) are different obligations and are not substituted. 5.5.4.2.4 does not appear in the supplied new context. This is not evidence of removal, since the clause itself still cites it.
added_or_revised.new_text: A manoeuvre shall only be initiated if the driver is not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start, and the driver: (a) has commanded the system to perform the manoeuvre for a driver-initiated manoeuvre; or (b) has acknowledged the system's intention as needed for a driver-confirmed manoeuvre; or (c) is given sufficient notice to react for a system-initiated manoeuvre. Motoric disengagement may not be considered when HORs are being withheld by the system.

added_or_revised.reason: Track B handoff resolved as modified (modified_existing, R-028). The supplied clause 5.3.7.2.1.13 (page 11) restates the old 5.3.7.2.4.3 duty almost verbatim: describe in the safety concept the system behaviour when the driver is detected disengaged during a manoeuvre. The clause sits under 5.3.7.2.1 General Requirements, so its scope is wider than the old duty, which sat under 5.3.7.2.4 (system-initiated manoeuvres). The word 'also' is dropped. The examples change from risk mitigation function, full execution and stop the vehicle to aborting, fully executing and safe stop. The duty is the same and is not replaced by a different obligation, so it is modified, not removed. The new 5.3.7.2.4.x numbering contains no counterpart, which is consistent with relocation. Related provisions are different obligations and do not substitute for R-028: 5.3.5.1 covers disengagement beyond a system boundary, 5.5.3.4.1.5 and 5.3.6.2 cover controllability. The new_text preserves the carried-over duty and adds the wider applicability.
added_or_revised.new_text: The manufacturer shall describe in the safety concept the system behaviour in case the driver is detected to be disengaged during a manoeuvre (e.g., aborting the manoeuvre, fully executing a manoeuvre, bringing the vehicle to a safe stop). This applies to all manoeuvres covered by the General Requirements for manoeuvres, not only system-initiated ones.
The manufacturer shall describe and justify to the Type Approval Authority the circumstances in which a system-initiated manoeuvre is performed as part of the driver unavailability response.
added_or_revised.reason: New documentation and justification duty for this scope. Existing documentation duties such as R-028 and R-030 concern different manoeuvre situations.

added_or_revised.new_text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different overlaps.
added_or_revised.reason: Independent variation item for the new partially obstructed intersection scenario. The old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1(b) is scoped to the unobstructed scenario.

added_or_revised.new_text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manouvres, the manufacturer's evidence of controllability of system operation (Annex 3, Appendix 2, paragraphs 5.2.1 and 5.2.2) shall include situations where the driver is aborting an ongoing manouvre.
added_or_revised.reason: This is a separate operating case from cancelling before the start. It is a distinct evidence scenario under the same inherited scope of system-initiated manoeuvres. No old base requirement covers evidence of controllability when the driver aborts an ongoing manoeuvre.

added_or_revised.new_text: The manufacturer shall establish processes to manage safety during the operation phase of the product lifecycle, including carrying out monitoring of DCAS operation and taking remedial actions when necessary.
added_or_revised.reason: New Annex 3 / 3.5.5 sets a process-establishment duty for operation-phase safety management. It covers monitoring of DCAS operation and remedial actions. Old 3.5.1 only required the manufacturer to demonstrate effective processes across the lifecycle, including operation. Old 7.1.1 (R-098) covers only monitoring of safety-critical occurrences. Neither old provision requires processes to manage operation-phase safety with remedial actions. Old 3.5.5 (periodic audits) moved to new 3.5.6.

added_or_revised.new_text: Following completion of a system-initiated manoeuvre performed to mitigate the risk of an imminent collision, and once the situation is controllable for the driver, a DCA shall be given.
added_or_revised.reason: New mandatory action: a DCA after an imminent-collision mitigation manoeuvre, once the situation is controllable. No old provision contained this.

added_or_revised.new_text: In the extended test for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (4.2.5.2.18.2), the test shall be executed at least with a pedestrian target moving at a different, but constant speed.
added_or_revised.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.9.2.1(b), but the scope is the newly introduced drive around scenario 4.2.5.2.18, so it is a separate obligation.

obligation.text: If the system identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded, the system or the applicable feature shall leave the 'active' mode, with the exception of the driver unavailability response.
obligation.reason: Old text required transition into 'stand-by' mode; new text requires leaving 'active' mode and adds an exception for the driver unavailability response.

clause.text:
5.3.5.1. The system shall aim to detect the applicable system boundaries when DCAS or a feature of DCAS is in
‘on’ mode. If the system identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded, the system or the applicable
feature shall leave the ‘active’ mode, with the exception of the driver unavailability response, and immediately
notify the driver in accordance to the strategies described by the manufacturer as outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2.
and according to the HMI requirements defined in paragraph 5.5.4.1.
If the driver is detected to be disengaged while the system or feature boundary is detected to be exceeded, the
system shall continue providing lateral and longitudinal assistance to the extent possible or terminate assistance
gradually in a controllable way, as outlined in the safety concept of the vehicle manufacturer.
The driver state monitoring system shall continue to monitor driver disengagement until the driver is motorically
and visually reengaged. The system shall initiate a driver unavailability response at the latest 10 seconds after it
has detected to be beyond a system boundary, if the driver remains disengaged.
The system shall terminate assistance to the driver provided by the affected feature or the system in a controllable
way. The assistance termination strategy shall be described by the vehicle manufacturer and assessed according to
Annex 3.

obligation.text: A manoeuvre shall only be initiated if the driver is not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start, and the driver: (a) has commanded the system to perform the manoeuvre for a driver-initiated manoeuvre; or (b) has acknowledged the system's intention as needed for a driver-confirmed manoeuvre; or (c) is given sufficient notice to react for a system-initiated manoeuvre.
obligation.reason: Substantive change from old 5.3.7.2.1.1: the old gate was 'driver is not detected to be disengaged'. The new gate is 'not deemed disengaged (per 5.5.4.2.4 and 5.5.4.2.5) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start', which adds a 2-second time qualifier and cross-references to the deeming rules. Conditions (a)-(c) per manoeuvre type are unchanged.

clause.text:
5.3.7.2.1.1. A manoeuvre shall only be initiated if the driver is not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in
paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start, and:
(a) Has commanded the system to perform the manoeuvre for a driver-initiated manoeuvre; or
(b) Has acknowledged the system’s intention as needed for a driver-confirmed manoeuvre; or
(c) Is given sufficient notice to react for a system-initiated manoeuvre.
Motoric disengagement may not be considered when HORs are being withheld by the system.

obligation.text: The manufacturer shall describe in the safety concept the system behaviour in case the driver is detected to be disengaged during a manoeuvre (e.g., aborting the manoeuvre, fully executing a manoeuvre, bringing the vehicle to a safe stop).
obligation.reason: The old 5.3.7.2.4.3 duty (R-028) is carried into the General Requirements in 5.3.7.2.1.13, so it now applies to all manoeuvre types, not only driver-initiated ones. The word 'also' is dropped. The examples change from risk mitigation function, full execution and stop the vehicle, to aborting, fully executing and bringing the vehicle to a safe stop. The duty itself is unchanged, so this is a modification of R-028.

clause.text:
5.3.7.2.1.13. The manufacturer shall describe in the safety concept the system behaviour in case the driver is
detected to be disengaged during a manoeuvre (e.g., aborting the manoeuvre, fully executing a manoeuvre,
bringing the vehicle to a safe stop).

obligation.text: For features capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of the manoeuvre.
obligation.reason: Old 5.3.7.2.4.2.1 required 'further strategies' to ensure driver engagement prior to initiation, in addition to the 7-second EOR lockout. New 5.3.7.2.4.2 drops 'In addition, further' and refers to 'The strategies'. The obligation is no longer framed as additional strategies, and the EOR lockout it supplemented is gone.

clause.text:
5.3.7.2.4.2. The strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of
the manoeuvre, which shall be documented and explained.

obligation.text: For highway or highway-like road operation, the system shall aim to respond to work zones, lane reductions, lane closures, toll stations and end of highways (e.g., by notifying the driver, issuing a DCA, or continuing operation if capable).
obligation.reason: Old 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 (R-041) applied only to 'highway operation'. The new text widens the operating-scope condition to 'highway or highway-like road operation'. The actor (system), the 'aim to respond' action and the listed situations are unchanged, so this is one modified obligation and not a new addition.

clause.text:
5.3.7.2.5.3.1. For highway or highway-like road operation, the system shall aim to respond to work zones, lane
reductions, lane closures, toll stations and end of highways (e.g., by notifying the driver, issuing a DCA, or
continuing operation if capable).

obligation.text: The system’s driver unavailability response shall comply with the technical requirements and transitional provisions of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79 with respect to the Risk Mitigation Function (RMF).
obligation.reason: The subject narrows from 'the system' to 'the system’s driver unavailability response'. The R79 04 series RMF reference is unchanged.

clause.text:
5.3.7.3.1. The system’s driver unavailability response shall comply with the technical requirements and
transitional provisions of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79 with respect to the Risk
Mitigation Function (RMF). In the event that the driver has been determined to be unavailable following a driver
disengagement warning escalation sequence as defined in paragraph 5.5.4.2.6., the system shall come to a safe
stop in accordance with the RMF requirements.

obligation.text: In the event that the driver has been determined to be unavailable following a driver disengagement warning escalation sequence as defined in paragraph 5.5.4.2.6., the system shall come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements.
obligation.reason: The trigger is unchanged. The action changes from 'appropriately activate the Risk Mitigation Function in order to come to a safe stop' to 'come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements'.

clause.text:
5.3.7.3.1. The system’s driver unavailability response shall comply with the technical requirements and
transitional provisions of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79 with respect to the Risk
Mitigation Function (RMF). In the event that the driver has been determined to be unavailable following a driver
disengagement warning escalation sequence as defined in paragraph 5.5.4.2.6., the system shall come to a safe
stop in accordance with the RMF requirements.

obligation.text: Where the system is equipped with a driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane change feature, the system shall be capable of performing lane changes during the driver unavailability response, in compliance with the technical requirements for RMF capable of bringing the vehicle to a safe stop outside its own lane of travel of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79, during an intervention on a highway to bring the vehicle towards a target stop area in a slower or emergency lane.
obligation.reason: Old 5.3.7.3.3 (R-045) required the RMF to be capable of performing lane changes on a highway towards a slower or emergency lane. The new text makes the system the actor, limits the capability to the driver unavailability response, and rewords the R79 reference from 'systems with the purpose of' to 'RMF capable of'. The trigger (lane change feature fitted), the highway scope and the target stop area are unchanged. This is a modification of R-045, not a new obligation.

clause.text:
5.3.7.3.3. Where the system is equipped with a driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane change feature, the
system shall be capable of performing lane changes during the driver unavailability response, in compliance with
the technical requirements for RMF capable of bringing the vehicle to a safe stop outside its own lane of travel of
the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79, during an intervention on a highway to bring the
vehicle towards a target stop area in a slower or emergency lane.

obligation.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall aim to provide the visual information at least 3 seconds ahead of the initiation of a relevant intended manoeuvre or with sufficient notice to allow the driver to comprehend the manoeuvre and the traffic situation, taking into account the complexity of the manoeuvre and amount of other road users present.
obligation.reason: Old R-064 required information ahead of the manoeuvre with sufficient notice. The new text specifies the information as visual and adds an 'at least 3 seconds ahead' target as an alternative to sufficient notice. This is a substantive change to the same obligation.

clause.text:
5.5.4.1.9.2. The system shall aim to provide the visual information at least 3 seconds ahead of the initiation of a
relevant intended manoeuvre or with sufficient notice to allow the driver to comprehend the manoeuvre and the
traffic situation, taking into account the complexity of the manoeuvre and amount of other road users present. If
there is a risk of imminent collision or it would conflict with the information about an ongoing manoeuvre, the
time may be reduced and system shall visually inform the driver as far in advance as possible. Where the notice is
less than 3 seconds ahead of initiation, the manufacturer shall provide evidence to the satisfaction of the Type
Approval Authority that the timing at which this information is provided ensures an appropriate driver response
and the strategies employed ensure the drivers notice the information without undue delay.

obligation.text: For the purpose of the assessment of visual disengagement, the dashboard and instrument panel may be considered as a driving task relevant area only while manoeuvre relevant information (as detailed in paragraph 5.5.4.1.8.1. or 5.5.4.1.9.4.) is displayed, for a maximum duration of 3 seconds.
obligation.reason: Old text said the dashboard and instrument panel shall not be considered a driving task relevant area. The new text reverses this to a limited permission, only while manoeuvre relevant information is displayed and for at most 3 seconds.

clause.text:
5.5.4.2.5.2. The driver shall be deemed to be visually disengaged when the driver’s eye gaze and/or head posture,
as relevant, is directed away from any currently driving task relevant area.
An outline of the driving task relevant areas, and when they are relevant, shall be specified by the manufacturer in
the documentation provided to the Type Approval Authority. For the purpose of the assessment of visual
disengagement, the dashboard and instrument panel may be considered as a driving task relevant area only while
manoeuvre relevant information (as detailed in paragraph 5.5.4.1.8.1. or 5.5.4.1.9.4.) is displayed for a maximum
duration of 3 seconds.
The EOR warning time shall not be extended with the time the drivers gaze is directed towards the dashboard or
instrument panel.

obligation.text: The driver shall be deemed to be visually reengaged following an aversion of eye gaze or head posture if either is re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area, with the exception of the dashboard and the instrument panel, for a sufficient duration depending on the situation.
obligation.reason: Old 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 (R-073) covered 'visually engaged or reengaged' and counted any driving task relevant area. The new text drops 'engaged or' so it covers reengagement only, and excludes the dashboard and instrument panel as re-direction targets.

clause.text:
5.5.4.2.5.2.1. The driver shall be deemed to be visually reengaged following an aversion of eye gaze or head
posture, if either are re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area with the exception of the
dashboard and the instrument panel for a sufficient duration depending on the situation. The duration shall be at
least 200 milliseconds.

obligation.text: The duration for which eye gaze or head posture must be re-directed towards a currently driving task relevant area (excluding the dashboard and instrument panel) for the driver to be deemed visually reengaged shall be at least 200 milliseconds.
obligation.reason: The 200 ms minimum is unchanged from R-074. The scope it applies to is now reengagement only and excludes the dashboard and instrument panel.

clause.text:
5.5.4.2.5.2.1. The driver shall be deemed to be visually reengaged following an aversion of eye gaze or head
posture, if either are re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area with the exception of the
dashboard and the instrument panel for a sufficient duration depending on the situation. The duration shall be at
least 200 milliseconds.

obligation.text: As outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2., the manufacturer shall describe in detail, as part of the documentation required for section 9, the boundary conditions under which HORs can be withheld (when the vehicle is on a "Highway" or "Highway-like" road at a speed up to 130 km/h).
obligation.reason: The documentation duty is retained but its scope is widened from Highway only to Highway or Highway-like roads, matching the R-077 modification.

clause.text:
5.5.4.2.6.5. Withholding of HORs
The system may withhold HORs when the vehicle is located on a “Highway” or a “Highway-like” road and is
operated at a speed up to 130 km/h. As outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2., the manufacturer shall describe in detail, as
part of the documentation required for section 9, the boundary conditions under which HORs can be withheld.
When the system is capable of withholding of HORs on highway-like roads it shall aim to avoid frequent
fluctuations between being able and not able to withhold HORs (e.g., not operating on discontinuous sections of
highway-like roads) and the following shall apply:
(a) The system shall aim to ensure a reasonable duration of being able to withhold HORs by verifying one or more
of the following before initiating withholding of HORs:
(i) The road ahead is deemed to have the necessary characteristics (as per paragraph 2.28.1.) for at least 500 m, or
(ii) The road ahead is deemed to have the necessary characteristics (as per paragraph 2.28.1.) for at least 30
seconds at the vehicle's current speed.
Alternatively, the system may implement other strategies which can reasonably be expected to result in at least an
equivalent duration as specified in items (i) and (ii). The manufacturer shall document such strategies and
demonstrate them to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority.








(b) The manufacturer shall demonstrate the system’s ability to safely operate in the presence of cyclists. This shall
be demonstrated by avoidance of a collision with a longitudinally travelling cyclist ahead in lane as outlined in
Annex 4, paragraph 4.2.5.2.16., taking into account the robustness criteria outlined in Appendix 4 of Annex 3;
(c) When the end of a highway-like road is expected to require a manoeuvre controlled by the driver an HOR shall
aim to be given at least 7 seconds prior the necessary manoeuvre needs to start.
While in this mode of operation, regardless if operated on a highway or a highway-like road, the following
subparagraphs shall apply:

obligation.text: The driver state monitoring system shall implement appropriate countermeasures in the event that no driver input has been determined over prolonged periods (e.g. through a negative determination of driver drowsiness or assessment of changes in gaze direction).
obligation.reason: Old 5.5.4.2.7 required implementing appropriate countermeasures under the same condition (R-082). This is a separate mandatory action from the assessment strategies, so it is kept as its own entry. The new text widens the illustrative examples of how no driver input is determined to include assessment of changes in gaze direction, which is a modest change in the condition's scope.

clause.text:
5.5.4.2.7.1. The driver state monitoring system shall have strategies to assess whether the driver is disengaged in
the event that no driver input has been determined over prolonged periods (e.g. through a negative determination
of driver drowsiness or assessment of changes in gaze direction), and implement appropriate countermeasures.

obligation.text: While the powertrain is active, when the driver is detected to have insufficient engagement, the system shall be disabled for a period of at least 30 minutes. The disablement shall happen once the driver has resumed control of the vehicle, or the vehicle has become stationary.
obligation.reason: The 30-minute disablement while the powertrain is active is carried over from old 5.5.4.2.8.1 (R-083). The new second sentence changes when the disablement takes effect, so this is one modified obligation and not a separate addition.

clause.text:
5.5.4.2.8.1. The system shall be disabled for a period of at least 30 minutes whilst the powertrain is active when
the driver is detected to have insufficient engagement. The disablement shall happen once the driver has resumed
control of the vehicle, or the vehicle has become stationary.

obligation.text: When the system is disabled due to insufficient engagement by the driver, the system shall only be re-enabled after the driver has confirmed by a deliberate action their understanding of their responsibilities and appropriate use of the system.
obligation.reason: Replaces old 5.5.4.2.8.4 (R-084), which required the system to request, at the latest upon powertrain deactivation, that the driver read the driver information material in paragraph 5.6. The trigger (system disabled due to insufficient engagement) is the same, but the obligation is now a re-enablement gate. The system may be re-enabled only after a deliberate driver action confirming understanding of responsibilities and appropriate use. The powertrain-deactivation timing and the reference to reading paragraph 5.6 material are dropped.

clause.text:
5.5.4.2.8.4. When the system is disabled due to insufficient engagement by the driver, the system shall only be re-
enabled after the driver has confirmed by a deliberate action their understanding of their responsibilities and
appropriate use of the system.

obligation.text: The manufacturer shall declare the system's ability to safely perform other system-initiated manoeuvres, or to respond to the target in non-highway environments without driver intervention, alternatively indicating 'Not Applicable'.
obligation.reason: The old declaration also covered driver-initiated manoeuvres; the new text is limited to system-initiated manoeuvres. The obligation to declare is retained with narrowed scope.

obligations.text: This UN Regulation applies to the type approval of vehicles of Categories M and N2 with regard to their Driver Control Assistance Systems (DCAS).
obligations.reason: Scope statement carried over unchanged from old paragraph 1.1. Actor, vehicle categories and object are identical. Only the footnote reference to R.E.3 changed (Rev.7 to Rev.8), which is a citation update and not a change in obligation. The base requirements contain no R-ID for this scope statement.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction has one obligation, and it is supported: the scope applicability of old 1.1 is unchanged. No base requirement corresponds to it, so existing_id is null; the old source is paragraph 1.1 on page 3 (o018). The footnote is a citation, not an obligation. The new exclusion of Categories X and Y is in the separate clause 1.2.2, not in this clause, so it is not added here.

obligations.text: This UN Regulation does not apply to the approval of vehicles with regard to their Automatically Commanded Steering Functions (ACSF) or Risk Mitigation Function (RMF) which have been approved to UN Regulation No. 79, even when a system is exercising longitudinal control at the same time.
obligations.reason: Same ACSF/RMF R79 exclusion as old 1.2 first sentence. It is only relocated under the new 1.2 lead-in 'This UN Regulation does not apply to:' as item 1.2.1. Actor, scope and conditions are unchanged, so this is not a substantive change.

obligations.text: If the manufacturer declares such ACSF or RMF (approved to UN Regulation No. 79) to be part of DCAS, this UN Regulation applies irrespective of whether it has also been approved to UN Regulation No. 79.
obligations.reason: Same exception as the 'However' sentence of old 1.2: a manufacturer declaration that the ACSF/RMF is part of DCAS makes the Regulation apply regardless of R79 approval. It is unchanged apart from relocation.

clause_reviews.explanation: Both sentences of new 1.2.1 are word-for-word identical to old 1.2 (p.3). Only the structure changed: the old single paragraph became a list item under a new lead-in. The prior extraction marked the first sentence as modified_existing, but no substantive change exists, so it is downgraded to existing. No base requirement (R-001 to R-117) represents the old 1.2 scope provision, so existing_id is null for both. The new 1.2.2 exclusion of Categories X and Y is a separate clause and is not part of n021.

obligations.text: This UN Regulation does not apply to vehicles of Categories X and Y (vehicles without the ability to be controlled by a driver, as defined in R.E.3).
obligations.reason: New paragraph 1.2.2 adds a scope exclusion for Categories X and Y, vehicles without the ability to be controlled by a driver. The old scope (1.1) limited applicability to Categories M and N2 and had no such exclusion. The old 1.2 was a single paragraph excluding only ACSF/RMF approved under UN R79. It has now been split into 1.2.1, with the same R79 wording, and this new 1.2.2.

clause_reviews.explanation: Only one obligation was found. The footnote and the following '2. Definitions' heading are not obligations. The old 1.2 R79 exclusion is carried by new 1.2.1, which belongs to a different clause. No old requirement matches the Category X/Y exclusion, so it is added with a null existing_id.

obligations.text: DCAS shall be switched to 'OFF' mode upon activation of an ADS feature.
obligations.reason: New paragraph 5.2.3 adds DCAS/ADS interaction. No old clause forces DCAS off when an ADS feature activates. Old 5.5.2.2 covers only driver-initiated off with no automatic transition, and R-054 covers sustained control by other systems, not ADS activation.

obligations.text: DCAS shall not be able to be switched to 'ON' mode whilst an ADS feature is active.
obligations.reason: Separate prohibition on switching DCAS on while an ADS feature is active. Old 5.5.3.2.2 requires only a deliberate driver action for off-to-on and does not block activation during ADS operation, so this is a distinct new obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction's two entries are supported and kept as separate obligations: forced OFF on ADS activation, and blocking ON while ADS is active. Neither has an equivalent base requirement. R-011, R-054 and R-055 concern different subjects (documentation of transitions, other systems' sustained control, driver switch-off). No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: While DCAS or a feature of DCAS is in 'on' mode, the system shall aim to detect the applicable system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Unchanged detection obligation from old 5.3.5.1 sentence 1.

obligations.text: If the system identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded, the system or the applicable feature shall leave the 'active' mode, with the exception of the driver unavailability response.
obligations.reason: Old text required transition into 'stand-by' mode; new text requires leaving 'active' mode and adds an exception for the driver unavailability response.

obligations.text: If the system identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded, the system shall immediately notify the driver in accordance with the strategies described by the manufacturer as outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2 and according to the HMI requirements defined in paragraph 5.5.4.1.
obligations.reason: Notification obligation unchanged from old 5.3.5.1.

obligations.text: If the driver is detected to be disengaged while the system or feature boundary is detected to be exceeded, the system shall continue providing lateral and longitudinal assistance to the extent possible or terminate assistance gradually in a controllable way, as outlined in the safety concept of the vehicle manufacturer.
obligations.reason: New disengaged-driver case with no equivalent in old 5.3.5.1.

obligations.text: The driver state monitoring system shall continue to monitor driver disengagement until the driver is motorically and visually reengaged.
obligations.reason: New monitoring obligation not in old clause.

obligations.text: If the driver remains disengaged, the system shall initiate a driver unavailability response at the latest 10 seconds after it has detected to be beyond a system boundary.
obligations.reason: New 10-second timing obligation not in old clause.

obligations.text: The system shall terminate assistance to the driver provided by the affected feature or the system in a controllable way.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 5.3.5.1.

obligations.text: The assistance termination strategy shall be described by the vehicle manufacturer and assessed according to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 5.3.5.1.

clause_reviews.explanation: Prior inventory kept and linked to base requirements. The notification obligation was bundled with the mode change in the prior output and is now split out as unchanged R-014. R-013 is modified; the three disengaged-driver obligations are new; the termination obligations are unchanged. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: If a DCA is given while performing a system-initiated manoeuvre, the manufacturer shall consider the time required for the driver to direct their gaze to appropriate driving task relevant area(s) after the DCA is given in order to control the vehicle in the current situation when responding to this DCA.
obligations.reason: New 5.3.6.1.2 adds a gaze-direction time consideration for a DCA given during a system-initiated manoeuvre. Old 5.3.6.1.1 covers only reaction time to respond to a DCA and hold the steering control while HORs are withheld, so this scope is new.

obligations.text: If the DCA is given whilst withholding HORs, the time for the driver to direct their gaze to appropriate driving task relevant area(s) shall be considered in addition to the time required by paragraph 5.3.6.1.1.
obligations.reason: This is a separate, additive-time obligation for the case where HORs are withheld. It builds on 5.3.6.1.1 (R-?) without changing it, and applies to a DCA given while performing a system-initiated manoeuvre, which is inherited from the parent sentence.

obligations.text: If a DCA is given while performing a system-initiated manoeuvre, the manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the strategies and the timing with which the assistance is to be provided to the driver until the DCA is confirmed.
obligations.reason: This is a new documentation obligation. No base requirement covers explaining assistance strategies and timing until a DCA is confirmed. R-016 concerns the termination strategy at system boundaries, and R-085 concerns 6.1.1.1.

clause_reviews.explanation: All three prior additions are supported by the source and kept. None is a modification of an existing requirement: old 5.3.6.1.1 (the 1 s reaction-time rule) is unchanged and only referenced. The ‘in the context of a system-initiated manoeuvre’ scope from sentence 1 is carried into the sentence 2 and 3 obligations. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: When the system reaches its boundary conditions set out in paragraph 9.1.3., in the absence of any driver input to the steering control and when any front tyre of the vehicle starts to unintentionally cross a lane marking, the system shall avoid sudden loss of steering support by providing continued assistance to the extent possible as outlined in the safety concept of the vehicle manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action, conditions and scope as the old 5.3.7.1.4 first sentence. The only change is the editorial 'any the front tyre' to 'any front tyre'. No substantive change, and no base requirement represents it.

obligations.text: When the system reaches its boundary conditions set out in paragraph 9.1.3., in the absence of any driver input to the steering control and when any front tyre of the vehicle starts to unintentionally cross a lane marking, the system shall clearly inform the driver about this system status by means of an optical warning signal and additionally by an acoustic or haptic warning signal.
obligations.reason: Identical to the old second sentence of 5.3.7.1.4, with the same conditions inherited from the first sentence. No base requirement represents it.

obligations.text: For vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3, the warning requirement of paragraph 5.3.7.1.4 is deemed fulfilled if the vehicle is equipped with a Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS) fulfilling the technical requirements of UN Regulation No. 130.
obligations.reason: Identical deeming permission in the old 5.3.7.1.4 second paragraph. Unchanged, and no base requirement represents it.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction labelled the first obligation 'modified_existing'. The only change is an editorial wording fix, so it is reclassified as 'existing'. All three items are unchanged from old 5.3.7.1.4 (p.9-10). None of R-001 to R-117 corresponds to them, so existing_id is null and the old source is stated in each reason. The shared conditions are repeated in the warning obligation.

obligations.text: A manoeuvre shall only be initiated if the driver is not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start, and the driver: (a) has commanded the system to perform the manoeuvre for a driver-initiated manoeuvre; or (b) has acknowledged the system's intention as needed for a driver-confirmed manoeuvre; or (c) is given sufficient notice to react for a system-initiated manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Substantive change from old 5.3.7.2.1.1: the old gate was 'driver is not detected to be disengaged'. The new gate is 'not deemed disengaged (per 5.5.4.2.4 and 5.5.4.2.5) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start', which adds a 2-second time qualifier and cross-references to the deeming rules. Conditions (a)-(c) per manoeuvre type are unchanged.

obligations.text: Motoric disengagement may not be considered when HORs are being withheld by the system.
obligations.reason: Unchanged sentence from old 5.3.7.2.1.1. It is represented in base requirement R-021, which bundled it as an exception. It is kept as a separate entry because it is an independent constraint, but it carries no new obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: Both prior obligations are supported and kept. The main rule is modified (R-021): the disengagement criterion changed from 'not detected to be disengaged' to 'not deemed disengaged for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to start', with references to 5.5.4.2.4 and 5.5.4.2.5. The motoric disengagement/HOR-withholding sentence is word-for-word unchanged and is mapped to R-021. No additional obligations were missed in this clause, and no reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall describe in the safety concept the system behaviour in case the driver is detected to be disengaged during a manoeuvre (e.g., aborting the manoeuvre, fully executing a manoeuvre, bringing the vehicle to a safe stop).
obligations.reason: The old 5.3.7.2.4.3 duty (R-028) is carried into the General Requirements in 5.3.7.2.1.13, so it now applies to all manoeuvre types, not only driver-initiated ones. The word 'also' is dropped. The examples change from risk mitigation function, full execution and stop the vehicle, to aborting, fully executing and bringing the vehicle to a safe stop. The duty itself is unchanged, so this is a modification of R-028.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause holds one obligation: the manufacturer's safety-concept description of system behaviour when the driver is detected to be disengaged during a manoeuvre. It matches old R-028 (5.3.7.2.4.3), which was limited to the driver-initiated manoeuvre section. It now sits in 5.3.7.2.1 General Requirements, so its scope widens, and the examples are reworded. It is therefore reported as modified_existing with existing_id R-028, not as an addition. The example list is illustrative (e.g.) and does not create separate obligations.

obligations.text: For feature(s) capable of performing driver-confirmed manoeuvres, the system shall be designed to ensure that the driver has sufficient time to confirm that the system may proceed with the manoeuvre, as appropriate.
obligations.reason: The old 5.3.7.2.3.1 contained the same sufficient-time design obligation, so it is unchanged. The sentence is retained in the new text with only the 'In addition,' lead-in dropped. It applies under the parent 5.3.7.2.3, which covers driver-confirmed manoeuvres.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction marked the sufficient-time obligation as modified_existing against o126. That is wrong, because the sentence is substantively unchanged. It matches R-024, which says the same thing, so it is classed as existing. The change from the old text is the deletion of the first sentence applying 5.5.4.1.8 and its subparagraphs (R-023). That deletion is a removal, which belongs to R-023's decision and not to this obligation, so it is not listed as an obligation here. No new obligation is added: the new text contains only this one sentence, and nothing is bundled.

obligations.text: For features capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Old 5.3.7.2.4.2.1 required 'further strategies' to ensure driver engagement prior to initiation, in addition to the 7-second EOR lockout. New 5.3.7.2.4.2 drops 'In addition, further' and refers to 'The strategies'. The obligation is no longer framed as additional strategies, and the EOR lockout it supplemented is gone.

obligations.text: For features capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the strategies implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of the manoeuvre shall be documented and explained.
obligations.reason: The documentation and explanation duty is retained from old 5.3.7.2.4.2.1 (R-027). It is renumbered to 5.3.7.2.4.2 and the 'further' wording is dropped. It is a separate mandatory action from implementing the strategies, so it is kept as its own entry.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction bundled implementation and documentation into one modified entry. They are independent obligations, so I split them. The implementation duty (R-026) is modified because 'further' and 'in addition' were dropped. The documentation duty (R-027) is substantively unchanged. R-025, the old 7-second EOR lockout, was in old 5.3.7.2.4.2. It is not retained in the new clause text, so it is not listed as an obligation here. The removal is already captured in the existing decisions. No additions are supported, as nothing in the clause is new.

obligations.text: For features capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, a manoeuvre shall only be performed if there is a justifiable reason for it (e.g., pursuing a set destination, following traffic flow, safety-relevant manoeuvres, etc.).
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and scope as old 5.3.7.2.4.4 (R-029). The text is identical and only the paragraph number changed. The parent 5.3.7.2.4 still limits it to system-initiated manoeuvres.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall explain in the documentation the traffic situations where the system may initiate manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: Identical documentation duty to old 5.3.7.2.4.4 second sentence (R-030). It was only renumbered.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a renumbering of old 5.3.7.2.4.4 (R-029 and R-030) with identical wording. The prior extraction cited o139 as the old match. In the base inventory the matching IDs are R-029 for the justifiable-reason gate and R-030 for the documentation duty. There is no substantive change and no reversal or exclusion. The two obligations are kept separate because one is a performance restriction and the other is a documentation duty.

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall not initiate the manoeuvre if the conditions outlined in paragraph 5.3.7.2.3.5 are not met.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and cross-referenced conditions as old 5.3.7.2.4.5 (R-031). Only the paragraph number changed (now 5.3.7.2.4.4, page 13). The parent scope, system-initiated manoeuvres under 5.3.7.2.4, is unchanged, and the referenced conditions (a)-(f) in 5.3.7.2.3.5 are textually unchanged.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a renumbering of old 5.3.7.2.4.5, represented by R-031. The wording is identical, the parent context (general requirements for system-initiated manoeuvres) is unchanged, and the referenced conditions in 5.3.7.2.3.5 are unchanged. It contains one obligation, with no bundled items and no new scope, so no addition or modification is needed.

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres (paragraph 5.3.7.2.4 and subparagraphs), the system shall aim to not initiate a manoeuvre if it would cause other road users to unreasonably or unmanageably decelerate or evade the vehicle as a consequence of the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Wording is identical to old 5.3.7.2.4.6 (R-032), which was renumbered to 5.3.7.2.4.5 on page 13. The actor, 'aim to not initiate' standard, condition and system-initiated scope are unchanged. The related 'shall not propose' rule in 5.3.7.2.3.6 is a separate driver-confirmed obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a renumbering of old 5.3.7.2.4.6 with identical text, so the single obligation is retained as existing and mapped to R-032. It contains no bundled items and no new scope, so nothing is added or modified.

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall aim to not initiate a manoeuvre if it would violate applicable instruction by relevant signage or performance requirements as specified in paragraph 6.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action, scope and constraint as old 5.3.7.2.4.7 (R-033). The clause is only renumbered (old 5.3.7.2.4.7, p.12; new 5.3.7.2.4.6, p.13). It sits under 5.3.7.2.4 'General requirements for system-initiated manoeuvres', so the system-initiated scope is inherited. The 'aim to' wording is unchanged.

clause_reviews.explanation: The new text is word-for-word identical to old 5.3.7.2.4.7 (R-033), which is the system-initiated counterpart. The driver-confirmed variant at 5.3.7.2.3.7 is a separate provision whose scope differs, so it is not the match. Only the paragraph number and page changed. The clause holds one obligation with no bundled items, so no split is needed. No reversal or exclusion applies, and no new obligation was missed.

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres (feature(s) capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres), the system shall not initiate a manoeuvre if it would lead the vehicle to cross lane markings which are not permitted to be crossed.
obligations.reason: The prohibition is identical to old 5.3.7.2.4.8, which is base requirement R-034. The actor, action, scope and 'shall not' strength are unchanged. Only the paragraph number and page changed. The 'propose' variant in 5.3.7.2.3.8 is a separate obligation for driver-confirmed manoeuvres.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a renumbering of old 5.3.7.2.4.8 (R-034), with the same wording and scope. It sits under 5.3.7.2.4, which limits it to features capable of system-initiated manoeuvres, and that parent applicability is kept in the obligation text. The prior extraction matched this to old clause o143, which is the same provision as R-034. No new, modified or split obligations were found. Nothing is reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall aim not to violate appropriate right-of-way rules applicable in the country of operation where relevant to the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Renumbered from old 5.3.7.2.4.9 with identical wording and the same scope (general requirements for system-initiated manoeuvres). The new paragraph 5.3.7.2.4.8 carries the same obligation as old R-035. Paragraph 6.3.8 is a separate, more general right-of-way provision.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a pure renumbering of old 5.3.7.2.4.9 (R-035). Actor (system), action (aim not to violate right-of-way rules), scope (system-initiated manoeuvres, country of operation, where relevant to the manoeuvre) and the soft 'aim' wording are all unchanged. No added obligation is present, and nothing is bundled in the sentence.

obligations.text: A request for the driver to acknowledge that they have read and understood the driver information material outlined in paragraph 5.6 shall be given while the vehicle is in a stopped position.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old 5.3.7.2.4.11 (R-037), renumbered to 5.3.7.2.4.9 under the same parent 5.3.7.2.4 (system-initiated manoeuvres). Wording is identical, so there is no substantive change.

obligations.text: The request for the driver to acknowledge that they have read and understood the driver information material outlined in paragraph 5.6 shall be given at least once every month, except that if the vehicle utilises a means of differentiating between users, this may be extended to 3 months for a given user.
obligations.reason: Same monthly frequency with the user-differentiation extension as old R-038. 'three months' is now written '3 months', which is editorial only.

obligations.text: The request for the driver to acknowledge that they have read and understood the driver information material outlined in paragraph 5.6 shall be given at least once every month, except that if the vehicle can identify that a driver has previously acknowledged this request, it does not need to be given again for that driver.
obligations.reason: Same exemption as old R-039; wording is unchanged and only the paragraph was renumbered.

obligations.text: If the vehicle can identify that the current driver has not acknowledged the request to acknowledge that they have read and understood the driver information material outlined in paragraph 5.6 before, the request shall be given in the current drive cycle.
obligations.reason: Same requirement as old R-040; wording is unchanged and only the paragraph was renumbered.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a renumbering of old 5.3.7.2.4.11 (R-037 to R-040) and sits under the same parent 5.3.7.2.4. The monthly request and the 3-month extension for differentiated users are kept together in one entry (R-038), matching the base inventory. The prior extraction marked the first obligation as modified_existing, but the wording is identical, so it is existing. No new or reversed obligations were found.

obligations.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 5.3.7.2.1.1, a system-initiated manoeuvre may be initiated when it is considered to mitigate the risk of an imminent collision.
obligations.reason: New permission that overrides the manoeuvre-initiation conditions of 5.3.7.2.1.1 (driver not disengaged, sufficient notice) for imminent-collision mitigation. Old 5.3.7.2.4.10 (R-036) was a different highway/HOR gate and has no matching permission.

obligations.text: Following completion of a system-initiated manoeuvre performed to mitigate the risk of an imminent collision, and once the situation is controllable for the driver, a DCA shall be given.
obligations.reason: New mandatory action: a DCA after an imminent-collision mitigation manoeuvre, once the situation is controllable. No old provision contained this.

obligations.text: Following a system-initiated manoeuvre performed to mitigate the risk of an imminent collision, the system shall be disabled according to paragraph 5.5.4.2.8.
obligations.reason: New mandatory action: the system must be disabled per 5.5.4.2.8 after the collision-mitigation manoeuvre. It is separate from the general 30-minute disablement (R-083), which is triggered by insufficient engagement.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior inventory is supported and is kept as three separate entries: the permission, the DCA step and the disablement step. Old 5.3.7.2.4.10 (R-036) required that manoeuvres be initiated only on a highway when not withholding HORs. The new text at this paragraph number does not restate that requirement. The new text is a different provision, so these are treated as additions and not as a modification of R-036. R-036 is not reassigned to this clause; its fate is a matter for the clause where the old gate might have moved.

obligations.text: Where a system-initiated manoeuvre is performed according to paragraph 5.3.7.2.4.10 (to mitigate the risk of an imminent collision), the manufacturer shall describe and justify to the Type Approval Authority the circumstances as to when this happens.
obligations.reason: New documentation and justification duty scoped to the collision-mitigation manoeuvre of 5.3.7.2.4.10. The old 5.3.7.2.4.11 was the driver acknowledgement request (R-037 to R-040), which is a different actor, action and scope and was renumbered to 5.3.7.2.4.9. No old requirement covers this.

obligations.text: Where a system-initiated manoeuvre is performed according to paragraph 5.3.7.2.4.10, the circumstances as to when this happens shall be assessed according to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: Separate obligation: the circumstances of the collision-mitigation manoeuvre are assessed under Annex 3. It is distinct from the describe-and-justify duty. No old equivalent exists; the Annex 3 assessment wording in R-016 and R-053 concerns different subjects.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a new paragraph text under number 5.3.7.2.4.11. The old paragraph with this number (acknowledgement request, R-037 to R-040) is retained as new 5.3.7.2.4.9 and is not affected here. The prior extraction's two additions are supported. They are kept as separate entries: documentation and justification to the TAA, and assessment according to Annex 3. Neither is a modification of an existing requirement, and no reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: For highway or highway-like road operation, the system shall aim to respond to work zones, lane reductions, lane closures, toll stations and end of highways (e.g., by notifying the driver, issuing a DCA, or continuing operation if capable).
obligations.reason: Old 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 (R-041) applied only to 'highway operation'. The new text widens the operating-scope condition to 'highway or highway-like road operation'. The actor (system), the 'aim to respond' action and the listed situations are unchanged, so this is one modified obligation and not a new addition.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause has a single obligation with the alternative response examples kept together. The prior extraction's modified_existing treatment is supported and mapped to base requirement R-041, which holds the old 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 text. The substantive change is the added 'highway-like road' scope. Nothing was reversed, excluded, or split, and nothing is added.

obligations.text: For non-highway operation, if system-initiated manoeuvres can be activated, the system shall aim to respond to relevant situations when the vehicle could be expected to stop, give way or required to change lane.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 first sentence; same actor, scope and condition. Only the paragraph's page position changed.

obligations.text: For non-highway operation, if system-initiated manoeuvres can be activated and the relevant situation is within the system boundaries, the system shall manage it by either: (a) carrying on providing lateral and/or longitudinal assistance; or (b) suggesting a manoeuvre to the driver; or (c) issuing a DCA; or (d) performing a system-initiated manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 list (a)-(d). The alternatives are one obligation and are kept together.

obligations.text: For non-highway operation, if system-initiated manoeuvres can be activated and the relevant situation means that the system is approaching a system boundary, the system shall issue a DCA.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 final sentence; same condition and action.

clause_reviews.explanation: The new clause 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 is word-for-word identical to the old 5.3.7.2.5.3.2. The old text also contained a separate lane-marking recognition sentence, which is now numbered 5.3.7.2.5.3.3 and is covered by R-042. No base requirement represents the non-highway obligations, so each is marked existing with existing_id null. The old source was old paragraph 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 (o152). The three-way split follows the prior inventory, with the shared non-highway and system-initiated manoeuvre conditions repeated in each entry. No change, reversal or exclusion was found.

obligations.text: The system shall be able to recognize lane markings as outlined in Annex 3 of the 01 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 130, as relevant to the countries in which the system can be activated.
obligations.reason: The wording, actor, action, scope and conditions are identical to the old lane-marking recognition obligation, which sat in the old text as a paragraph numbered 5.3.7.2.5.3 appended to the end of 5.3.7.2.5.3.2. In the new text it has its own number, 5.3.7.2.5.3.3, so this is a renumbering and not a substantive change.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause has one obligation. It is a single sentence with one actor, the system, and one action, recognizing lane markings. It has one condition, relevance to the countries of activation, and it makes one reference to Annex 3 of UN R130 01 series. Nothing in it needs splitting. It matches R-042 word for word, and R-042 was already marked unchanged. It sits under the parent 5.3.7.2.5, which covers systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres or withholding of HORs, and under 5.3.7.2.5.3, which covers special provisions regarding system boundaries. Both parents are unchanged in the old and new text. The prior extraction's single 'existing' entry is supported, so no addition or modification is warranted.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres in non-highway environments or during phases of withholding of HORs, where extended testing in Annex 4 includes different vehicle under test (VUT) speeds, this shall cover the maximum operating speed in the applicable test scenarios.
obligations.reason: The clause sets a new test-procedure scope. Extended Annex 4 tests that vary VUT speed must cover the maximum operating speed. The obligation applies to systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres in non-highway environments or while withholding HORs, which is inherited from the parent heading 5.3.7.2.6. The old text has speed-range and speed-limit requirements (5.3.7.4.3 to 5.3.7.4.6) and Annex 4 extended-test lists. None requires extended tests to include the maximum operating speed, and none carries this applicability condition.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction is supported. Old context has no equivalent. The old speed provisions (R-047 and 5.3.7.4.x) govern system behaviour, not extended-test speed coverage. The old Annex 4 extended-test clauses vary speeds but do not require the maximum operating speed. The clause contains one obligation, so no split is needed. The inherited scope from the heading 5.3.7.2.6 is kept in the text. Nothing was reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: The system’s driver unavailability response shall comply with the technical requirements and transitional provisions of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79 with respect to the Risk Mitigation Function (RMF).
obligations.reason: The subject narrows from 'the system' to 'the system’s driver unavailability response'. The R79 04 series RMF reference is unchanged.

obligations.text: In the event that the driver has been determined to be unavailable following a driver disengagement warning escalation sequence as defined in paragraph 5.5.4.2.6., the system shall come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements.
obligations.reason: The trigger is unchanged. The action changes from 'appropriately activate the Risk Mitigation Function in order to come to a safe stop' to 'come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements'.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause has two separate obligations, and both modify old 5.3.7.3.1 (R-043 and R-044). The prior extraction cited old clause o154 for both. They are mapped here to the base requirements R-043 and R-044, with no additions or exclusions. The sentence split matches the base inventory. No bundled items were found.

obligations.text: Where the system is equipped with a driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane change feature, the system shall be capable of performing lane changes during the driver unavailability response, in compliance with the technical requirements for RMF capable of bringing the vehicle to a safe stop outside its own lane of travel of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79, during an intervention on a highway to bring the vehicle towards a target stop area in a slower or emergency lane.
obligations.reason: Old 5.3.7.3.3 (R-045) required the RMF to be capable of performing lane changes on a highway towards a slower or emergency lane. The new text makes the system the actor, limits the capability to the driver unavailability response, and rewords the R79 reference from 'systems with the purpose of' to 'RMF capable of'. The trigger (lane change feature fitted), the highway scope and the target stop area are unchanged. This is a modification of R-045, not a new obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a single obligation, so it is not split. It replaces R-045 (old 5.3.7.3.3, page 13). The prior extraction cited an old ID o156, which is not a base requirement ID, so the old requirement is identified as R-045. No reversal or exclusion applies, and no addition is made because this would duplicate the modification.

obligations.text: A system-initiated manoeuvre may be performed at any time as part of the driver unavailability response in order to mitigate risk, irrespective of the disengagement of the driver or warnings given.
obligations.reason: New permission scoped to the driver unavailability response. Old 5.3.7.3 had no equivalent; old R-021 and 5.3.7.2.4.1 govern initiation and rejection of announced manoeuvres, which is a different scope.

obligations.text: A system-initiated manoeuvre as part of the driver unavailability response shall only be performed after driver reengagement strategies have failed or if there is an imminent risk of collision.
obligations.reason: New restrictive condition on system-initiated manoeuvres within the driver unavailability response. No old provision imposed this gating.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall describe and justify to the Type Approval Authority the circumstances in which a system-initiated manoeuvre is performed as part of the driver unavailability response.
obligations.reason: New documentation and justification duty for this scope. Existing documentation duties such as R-028 and R-030 concern different manoeuvre situations.

clause_reviews.explanation: All three prior obligations were checked against the source and the old context. They are separate (permission, restriction, documentation duty) and are retained as additions. The old driver unavailability response in 5.3.7.3.1 covered only RMF compliance and the safe stop, so none of the three has an old counterpart. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about the status of the system or feature: 'stand-by' mode (if applicable), 'active' mode.
obligations.reason: Item (a) is unchanged from old 5.5.4.1.1(a).

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about the status of an ongoing manoeuvre (e.g., initiation, cancellation or if it will be recommenced after the vehicle is forced to come to a stop during the manoeuvre).
obligations.reason: Item (b) is unchanged from old 5.5.4.1.1(b).

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about the need for the driver to perform a specific action (e.g. apply control, check indirect vision devices).
obligations.reason: Item (c) is unchanged from old 5.5.4.1.1(c).

obligations.text: If while in 'active' mode the system has detected to have reached a currently relevant system boundary, the system shall inform or warn the driver, unless already indicated by (a).
obligations.reason: Item (d) is unchanged from old 5.5.4.1.1(d).

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about a detected upcoming system boundary.
obligations.reason: Item (e) is unchanged from old 5.5.4.1.1(e).

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about detected failures affecting the system or its features, unless the system is in 'off' mode.
obligations.reason: Item (f) is unchanged from old 5.5.4.1.1(f).

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about intended driver-confirmed or system-initiated manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: Item (g) is unchanged from old 5.5.4.1.1(g).

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about the basis for the system being disabled due to insufficient engagement.
obligations.reason: Item (h) is new; the old paragraph ended at (g) and no base requirement covers it.

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about the basis for why a DCA has been issued, if not addressed by the points above or if it follows an engagement request escalation.
obligations.reason: Item (i) is new; the old paragraph ended at (g) and no base requirement covers it.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior single bundled entry for (a)-(g) is split into separate entries, each mapped to its base requirement R-057 to R-063, since the base inventory already holds them separately. Items (h) and (i) are genuinely new additions with no old counterpart.

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall aim to provide the visual information at least 3 seconds ahead of the initiation of a relevant intended manoeuvre or with sufficient notice to allow the driver to comprehend the manoeuvre and the traffic situation, taking into account the complexity of the manoeuvre and amount of other road users present.
obligations.reason: Old R-064 required information ahead of the manoeuvre with sufficient notice. The new text specifies the information as visual and adds an 'at least 3 seconds ahead' target as an alternative to sufficient notice. This is a substantive change to the same obligation.

obligations.text: If there is a risk of imminent collision or the information would conflict with the information about an ongoing manoeuvre, the time may be reduced and the system shall visually inform the driver as far in advance as possible.
obligations.reason: Same exception and same visual-information duty as old R-065. Wording is unchanged, so this is not a new obligation.

obligations.text: Where the notice is less than 3 seconds ahead of initiation, the manufacturer shall provide evidence to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that the timing at which this information is provided ensures an appropriate driver response and that the strategies employed ensure the drivers notice the information without undue delay.
obligations.reason: Old 5.5.4.1.9.2 had no manufacturer evidence duty for short notice, and no base requirement covers it. The duty is triggered by notice under 3 seconds, which is the new threshold, so it is a new obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: R-066 is not carried over: the old last sentence of 5.5.4.1.9.2 required lane change initiation to be announced by another modality unless the driver had observed the visual information. That sentence is absent from the new text, so it is a removal and no obligation is returned for it. Three obligations are returned, one modified, one unchanged and one new.

obligations.text: The system shall offer the driver the possibility to visualize at least a representation of the intended manoeuvre (system messages and signals for system-initiated manoeuvres).
obligations.reason: New paragraph 5.5.4.1.9.4 under System Messages and Signals for System-Initiated Manoeuvres. Old 5.5.4.1.9.1 only applied 5.5.4.1.8 (visual information about a proposed manoeuvre), which has no equivalent offer-to-visualize obligation. Old 5.5.4.1.9.3 (indication of manoeuvre initiation mode) is also different. The old context contained no 5.5.4.1.9.4.

obligations.text: The visualization of the intended manoeuvre shall aim to not cause unnecessary distraction to the driver.
obligations.reason: Separate design constraint (aim-level) on the visualization of the intended manoeuvre in system-initiated manoeuvres; there is no old counterpart. Old 5.5.4.1.8.3 (avoid overreliance or misuse) differs in subject and purpose.

clause_reviews.explanation: Both prior additions are supported. 5.5.4.1.9.4 is a new paragraph with two independent obligations: a mandatory offer of the visualization, and a distraction-avoidance constraint. No existing base requirement (R-057 to R-066 and others) matches. R-063 covers informing about intended manoeuvres, but the visualization possibility is a distinct action. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: The system's warning and escalation strategy shall consider for and prioritize warning strategies of simultaneously activated emergency assistance systems (e.g. AEBS).
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and object as old 5.5.4.2.2.3 under the same parent 5.5.4.2.2, with identical wording. This is a renumbering to 5.5.4.2.2.2 only, so it is not a new obligation.
