clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a verbatim renumbering of old 5.5.4.2.2.3, represented by R-068. It contains a single obligation with no bundled items, and no change in actor, scope, conditions or constraints. No additions or modifications are needed.

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to be visually disengaged when the driver's eye gaze and/or head posture, as relevant, is directed away from any currently driving task relevant area.
obligations.reason: Same definition as old 5.5.4.2.5.2 first paragraph; unchanged.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall specify, in the documentation provided to the Type Approval Authority, an outline of the driving task relevant areas and when they are relevant.
obligations.reason: Same documentation obligation as old 5.5.4.2.5.2; unchanged.

obligations.text: For the purpose of the assessment of visual disengagement, the dashboard and instrument panel may be considered as a driving task relevant area only while manoeuvre relevant information (as detailed in paragraph 5.5.4.1.8.1. or 5.5.4.1.9.4.) is displayed, for a maximum duration of 3 seconds.
obligations.reason: Old text said the dashboard and instrument panel shall not be considered a driving task relevant area. The new text reverses this to a limited permission, only while manoeuvre relevant information is displayed and for at most 3 seconds.

obligations.text: The EOR warning time shall not be extended with the time the driver's gaze is directed towards the dashboard or instrument panel.
obligations.reason: New sentence with no counterpart in the old 5.5.4.2.5.2; it adds a separate constraint on EOR warning timing.

clause_reviews.explanation: The first two obligations are unchanged. The dashboard and instrument panel rule is modified: R-072 is reversed from a blanket exclusion to a limited exception (manoeuvre relevant information, max 3 s). The EOR timing constraint is new and not an old requirement.

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to be visually reengaged following an aversion of eye gaze or head posture if either is re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area, with the exception of the dashboard and the instrument panel, for a sufficient duration depending on the situation.
obligations.reason: Old 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 (R-073) covered 'visually engaged or reengaged' and counted any driving task relevant area. The new text drops 'engaged or' so it covers reengagement only, and excludes the dashboard and instrument panel as re-direction targets.

obligations.text: The duration for which eye gaze or head posture must be re-directed towards a currently driving task relevant area (excluding the dashboard and instrument panel) for the driver to be deemed visually reengaged shall be at least 200 milliseconds.
obligations.reason: The 200 ms minimum is unchanged from R-074. The scope it applies to is now reengagement only and excludes the dashboard and instrument panel.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause has two obligations, and both were already in the inventory as modified existing requirements. I kept them as separate modified_existing entries mapped to R-073 and R-074, and I did not add them as new obligations. The prior extraction matched them to clause o259, not to R-IDs, so I corrected the mapping. The substantive changes are the removal of 'engaged or' and the new dashboard and instrument panel exclusion, which now applies to the sufficient duration and the 200 ms minimum.

obligations.text: The system may withhold HORs when the vehicle is located on a "Highway" or a "Highway-like" road and is operated at a speed up to 130 km/h.
obligations.reason: Old 5.5.4.2.6.5 permitted withholding HORs only on a "Highway"; scope is now widened to "Highway-like" roads. This is a changed permission with no matching base requirement (R-077 covers only the documentation duty).

obligations.text: As outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2., the manufacturer shall describe in detail, as part of the documentation required for section 9, the boundary conditions under which HORs can be withheld (when the vehicle is on a "Highway" or "Highway-like" road at a speed up to 130 km/h).
obligations.reason: The documentation duty is retained but its scope is widened from Highway only to Highway or Highway-like roads, matching the R-077 modification.

obligations.text: When the system is capable of withholding HORs on highway-like roads, it shall aim to avoid frequent fluctuations between being able and not able to withhold HORs (e.g., not operating on discontinuous sections of highway-like roads).
obligations.reason: New requirement for the highway-like road scope; no old equivalent.

obligations.text: When the system is capable of withholding HORs on highway-like roads, the system shall aim to ensure a reasonable duration of being able to withhold HORs by verifying one or more of the following before initiating withholding of HORs: (i) the road ahead is deemed to have the necessary characteristics (as per paragraph 2.28.1.) for at least 500 m, or (ii) the road ahead is deemed to have the necessary characteristics (as per paragraph 2.28.1.) for at least 30 seconds at the vehicle's current speed.
obligations.reason: New road-ahead duration verification; alternatives (i) and (ii) are conditions of one obligation and are kept together.

obligations.text: As an alternative to the 500 m / 30 s road-ahead verification, the system may implement other strategies which can reasonably be expected to result in at least an equivalent duration; the manufacturer shall document such strategies and demonstrate them to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: New permission for alternative strategies, coupled with a documentation and demonstration duty.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall demonstrate the system's ability to safely operate in the presence of cyclists, by avoidance of a collision with a longitudinally travelling cyclist ahead in lane as outlined in Annex 4, paragraph 4.2.5.2.16., taking into account the robustness criteria outlined in Appendix 4 of Annex 3 (applies where the system is capable of withholding HORs on highway-like roads).
obligations.reason: New demonstration obligation; no old equivalent.

obligations.text: When the end of a highway-like road is expected to require a manoeuvre controlled by the driver, an HOR shall aim to be given at least 7 seconds prior to the time the necessary manoeuvre needs to start (where the system is capable of withholding HORs on highway-like roads).
obligations.reason: New timing requirement for highway-like road ends; absent in old text.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior inventory is preserved. The 'Highway' permission is a new scoped permission, and the documentation duty modifies R-077 by widening scope to highway-like roads. Alternatives (i)/(ii) stay in one obligation. The closing lead-in sentence introduces the following subparagraphs and creates no separate obligation; those are covered in their own clauses. Citations use the clause paragraph or its lettered items (a), (b), (c).

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs (while operating in the HOR-withholding mode on a Highway or Highway-like road), the system shall aim to determine whether or not the driver is in an appropriate position to operate the vehicle controls.
obligations.reason: New sub-paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.5.7.1 under the additional monitoring requirements for system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs. No old counterpart exists in the old context or base requirements; the old withholding clauses did not address driver position.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall document the strategy employed for classification and detection of the driver's positions (appropriate position to operate the vehicle controls) for systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs.
obligations.reason: Separate manufacturer documentation duty, split from the assessment duty. New in this scope; no old equivalent.

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority shall assess the strategy documented by the manufacturer for classification and detection of the driver's positions (appropriate position to operate the vehicle controls) for systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs.
obligations.reason: Separate Type Approval Authority assessment action, split from the manufacturer's documentation obligation. New in this scope; no old equivalent.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is entirely new. It sits under new paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.5.7, which applies to systems that perform system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs, so I kept that inherited applicability in each entry. The prior extraction bundled documentation by the manufacturer and assessment by the TAA into one entry. I split them into two entries because they have different actors. No base requirement matches, so every entry is an addition.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs, if the driver is deemed, as per the strategy, not to be in an appropriate position to operate the vehicle controls for 10 seconds, an HOR shall be given.
obligations.reason: New trigger (driver not in an appropriate position for 10 s) producing an HOR, within the HOR-withholding mode with system-initiated manoeuvres. The old HOR rules are tied to motoric disengagement (5.5.4.2.6.1.1) and to boundary conditions (5.5.4.2.6.5.1/.2). None of them covers this trigger, so it is not a restatement.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a single mandatory action (give an HOR) with one condition. It has no alternatives or exceptions to split. It inherits applicability from parent 5.5.4.2.6.5.7, which covers systems performing system-initiated manoeuvres while withholding HORs. The old text has no equivalent: old 5.5.4.2.6.1.1 uses a different trigger (motoric disengagement over 5 s), and no base requirement covers it. The prior addition is therefore supported and kept, with no reversal or exclusion.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs: following an HOR given because the driver was deemed not to be in an appropriate position to operate the vehicle controls for 10 seconds, the system may continue to perform system-initiated manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: New permission in the post-HOR context of the new 5.5.4.2.6.5.7 sub-procedure. No old requirement grants it; R-021 and R-036 address manoeuvre initiation conditions, not continuation after this HOR.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs: following such an HOR, the system shall only resume operating while withholding HORs once the driver has been deemed, as per the strategy, to be in an appropriate position to operate the vehicle controls and not to be motorically disengaged for at least 30 seconds.
obligations.reason: New resumption condition with a 30-second requirement for withholding HORs. No old requirement states it; the old withholding clause 5.5.4.2.6.5 only set road and speed scope and boundary documentation.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs: following such an HOR, the driver shall be informed of the basis for why the system will not resume withholding HORs.
obligations.reason: New driver-information obligation tied to non-resumption of HOR withholding. No old requirement covers it; the old R-057 to R-063 status items do not include it.

clause_reviews.explanation: All three prior obligations are retained as separate independent entries, with inherited applicability from the parent 5.5.4.2.6.5.7 (systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs) added. The paragraph is cited as 5.5.4.2.6.5.7.3, the assigned clause, to match the source. Nothing in the old context carries an equivalent, so each is added. There are no reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: The driver state monitoring system shall have strategies to assess whether the driver is disengaged in the event that no driver input has been determined over prolonged periods (e.g. through a negative determination of driver drowsiness or assessment of changes in gaze direction).
obligations.reason: Old 5.5.4.2.7 required the driver state monitoring system to be equipped with strategies to assess disengagement when no driver input is determined over prolonged periods (R-081). New 5.5.4.2.7.1 keeps the same actor, action and condition. 'Be equipped with' becomes 'have', and the illustrative example list now adds 'assessment of changes in gaze direction'. The example is non-limiting, so the obligation is substantively unchanged.

obligations.text: The driver state monitoring system shall implement appropriate countermeasures in the event that no driver input has been determined over prolonged periods (e.g. through a negative determination of driver drowsiness or assessment of changes in gaze direction).
obligations.reason: Old 5.5.4.2.7 required implementing appropriate countermeasures under the same condition (R-082). This is a separate mandatory action from the assessment strategies, so it is kept as its own entry. The new text widens the illustrative examples of how no driver input is determined to include assessment of changes in gaze direction, which is a modest change in the condition's scope.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction bundled the assessment-strategy duty and the countermeasure duty into one modified_existing entry linked to o283. The old base inventory splits them into R-081 (strategies) and R-082 (countermeasures), so I split them too. R-081 is treated as existing because 'have' versus 'be equipped with' and a non-limiting 'e.g.' example do not change the obligation. R-082 is kept as a modification because the example list in the condition now also covers gaze-direction assessment. This is consistent with the existing decisions, which marked R-081 unchanged and R-082 modified. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: During phases of operation where the system is able to perform system-initiated manoeuvres, the driver state monitoring system shall have additional strategies to assess behaviours which indicate that the driver is consistently engaged with the driving task, including determination of drowsiness.
obligations.reason: New 5.5.4.2.7.2(a) applies to phases where the system can perform system-initiated manoeuvres. The old 5.5.4.2.7 and the new 5.5.4.2.7.1 only require general strategies to assess disengagement when no driver input is determined over prolonged periods (R-081), which is a different trigger and scope.

obligations.text: During phases of operation where the system is able to perform system-initiated manoeuvres, the driver state monitoring system shall have additional strategies to assess that the driver performs changes in eye gaze with a frequency and/or direction appropriate to the current vehicle traffic environment and upcoming manoeuvres, and that these behaviours do not degrade over time.
obligations.reason: New eye-gaze behaviour assessment strategy scoped to system-initiated manoeuvres; no old equivalent.

obligations.text: During phases of operation where the system is able to perform system-initiated manoeuvres, if the driver's behaviours do not indicate consistent engagement with the driving task, system-initiated manoeuvres other than those in situation of imminent collision risk shall not be initiated.
obligations.reason: New prohibition on initiating system-initiated manoeuvres when consistent engagement is not indicated, with an exception for imminent collision risk. Separated from the countermeasure obligation as an independent mandatory action.

obligations.text: During phases of operation where the system is able to perform system-initiated manoeuvres, if the driver's behaviours do not indicate consistent engagement with the driving task, appropriate countermeasures shall be applied as described in the safety concept.
obligations.reason: Independent countermeasure obligation, tied to the safety concept. The old 5.5.4.2.7 countermeasures (R-082) are triggered by a lack of driver input over prolonged periods, not by this condition.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall document the strategies implemented to assess behaviours which indicate that the driver is consistently engaged with the driving task.
obligations.reason: New manufacturer documentation duty scoped to the new consistent-engagement strategies. Separated from the Type Approval Authority assessment as a different actor.

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority shall assess the strategies implemented to assess behaviours which indicate that the driver is consistently engaged with the driving task.
obligations.reason: Separate TAA assessment obligation for the new strategies; different actor from the manufacturer documentation duty.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction bundled the intro and (a), and combined the manufacturer documentation duty with the TAA assessment. I split these by actor and action. The manoeuvre-initiation prohibition and the countermeasure were also separated, with the shared condition repeated. None of these map to R-081/R-082: the old paragraph 5.5.4.2.7 and the new 5.5.4.2.7.1 cover general prolonged no-input disengagement, whereas 5.5.4.2.7.2 is new in its manoeuvre-phase scope, assessed behaviours and consequences.

obligations.text: While the powertrain is active, when the driver is detected to have insufficient engagement, the system shall be disabled for a period of at least 30 minutes. The disablement shall happen once the driver has resumed control of the vehicle, or the vehicle has become stationary.
obligations.reason: The 30-minute disablement while the powertrain is active is carried over from old 5.5.4.2.8.1 (R-083). The new second sentence changes when the disablement takes effect, so this is one modified obligation and not a separate addition.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction split the clause into an existing 30-minute obligation and a new timing sentence. The timing sentence is not independent. It qualifies when the same disablement takes effect: once the driver has resumed control, or the vehicle has become stationary. I therefore merged both sentences into one modified_existing entry on R-083, which already holds the 30-minute disablement obligation. This also avoids duplicating a modification as an addition. The old text had no such timing condition, so the change is substantive. The resumption-of-control and stationary alternatives are kept together as conditions of one obligation. No reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to have insufficient engagement when this leads to one unavailability response initiation. Counting is reset when the system is no longer disabled.
obligations.reason: Criterion (a) is unchanged from the old 5.5.4.2.8.2(a). The reset rule that applies to it is repeated here.

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to have insufficient engagement when this leads to at most 2 DCAs due to prolonged insufficient engagement. Counting is reset when the system is no longer disabled.
obligations.reason: Criterion (b) is unchanged from the old 5.5.4.2.8.2(b). The reset rule that applies to it is repeated here.

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to have insufficient engagement when this leads to at most 3 engagement request escalations, determined over a rolling time window of 30 minutes during the activation of the powertrain.
obligations.reason: Criterion (c) is unchanged from the old 5.5.4.2.8.2(c). The rolling 30-minute window that applies to it is repeated here.

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to have insufficient engagement when this leads to one DCA following a system-initiated manoeuvre performed when the driver is deemed to be disengaged (as per paragraph 5.3.7.2.4.10.). Counting is reset when the system is no longer disabled.
obligations.reason: Criterion (d) is new. It is tied to the new collision-mitigation manoeuvre provision in 5.3.7.2.4.10 and has no old counterpart. The reset rule that applies to it is repeated here.

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to have insufficient engagement when this leads to at most two DCAs which were not preceded by an escalation and not responded to in less than 5 seconds. Counting is reset when the system is no longer disabled.
obligations.reason: Criterion (e) is new and has no old counterpart. The reset rule that applies to it is repeated here.

clause_reviews.explanation: The old 5.5.4.2.8.2 is not represented in the base requirements, so criteria (a) to (c) are marked existing with existing_id null. They match the old paragraph 5.5.4.2.8.2 (a) to (c). Criteria (d) and (e) are new. The prior output bundled the reset and rolling-window rules into one entry. I split them and repeated each rule under the criteria it applies to: the reset applies to (a), (b), (d) and (e), and the rolling window applies to (c). Because no matching base requirement exists, the reset rule for (a) and (b) is existing and not modified_existing. Extending it to (d) and (e) is covered by the new entries for those criteria. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: When the system is disabled due to insufficient engagement by the driver, the system shall only be re-enabled after the driver has confirmed by a deliberate action their understanding of their responsibilities and appropriate use of the system.
obligations.reason: Replaces old 5.5.4.2.8.4 (R-084), which required the system to request, at the latest upon powertrain deactivation, that the driver read the driver information material in paragraph 5.6. The trigger (system disabled due to insufficient engagement) is the same, but the obligation is now a re-enablement gate. The system may be re-enabled only after a deliberate driver action confirming understanding of responsibilities and appropriate use. The powertrain-deactivation timing and the reference to reading paragraph 5.6 material are dropped.

clause_reviews.explanation: Single-sentence clause with one obligation, which is a modification of R-084. The old text was a request to read information material by the latest upon powertrain deactivation. The new text is a re-enablement restriction requiring deliberate driver confirmation. It is not a pure addition, because the clause occupies the same paragraph and has the same trigger. I found no bundled independent steps and no further obligations in the source text. The prior extraction is supported, with the old match given as the base requirement R-084 rather than the clause ID o288.

obligations.text: When there is an approaching vehicle, the system shall be designed to not make the approaching vehicle decelerate at a higher level than 3.0 m/s², in order to ensure that the distance between the two vehicles is never less than that which the DCAS vehicle travels in 1 second.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and values as old 6.2.4.1 first paragraph (R-089); only page changed.

obligations.text: The 6.2.4.1 assessment shall be performed with the assumption that the approaching vehicle begins its deceleration 1.4 seconds after the system starts the lateral movement of the lane change procedure.
obligations.reason: Old 6.2.4.1(a) assumption is unchanged (R-090).

obligations.text: The 6.2.4.1 assessment shall be performed with the assumption that the approaching vehicle begins its deceleration either (i) 0.4 seconds after the system starts the lane change manoeuvre, provided the approaching vehicle was detected by the DCAS vehicle for at least 1.0 seconds immediately before the lane change manoeuvre starts; or (ii) 1.4 seconds after the system starts the lane change manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Old 6.2.4.1(b)(i)/(ii) alternatives are unchanged (R-091); alternatives kept together as one obligation.

obligations.text: At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from the 6.2.4.1 assessment of the approaching vehicle's deceleration.
obligations.reason: New permission absent from old 6.2.4.1, which had no speed-based deviation.

obligations.text: Where the system deviates from the 6.2.4.1 assessment at speeds up to 60 km/h, the manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the distances and timings for an approaching vehicle under which a lane change manoeuvre can be started, and provide evidence of those situations being deemed controllable for other road users.
obligations.reason: New manufacturer explanation and evidence duty tied to the deviation; not in old text.

clause_reviews.explanation: The first three obligations repeat old 6.2.4.1 (R-089, R-090, R-091) unchanged. The final paragraph is new and yields a separate permission and a separate manufacturer obligation. The heading is only an applicability label and is not a separate obligation.

obligations.text: The system shall not suggest a manoeuvre to the driver or perform a system-initiated manoeuvre which intends to cross a solid lane marking that is not permitted to be crossed, unless permitted by the situation as described in paragraph 6.3.9.1(c).
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 6.3.9.4 under the same parent 6.3.9 (navigating around an obstruction). Actor, action, scope and exception are identical. No base requirement R-xxx represents it. R-034 (5.3.7.2.4.8) covers system-initiated manoeuvres in general and has no obstruction scope or 6.3.9.1(c) exception, and R-097 covers the separate 6.3.9.2 enabling condition.

clause_reviews.explanation: The new 6.3.9.4 on page 29 is word-for-word identical to old 6.3.9.4 on page 26. Only the page and the document position changed. The context is unchanged: it still sits under 6.3.9 and 6.3.9.1(c), and 6.3.9.1 is unchanged. The prior extraction's single obligation is supported. There is no base requirement ID for it, so existing_id is null and the old source is old 6.3.9.4. It is a single obligation with a joint suggest-or-perform prohibition and one exception, so it is not split. No modification, addition, reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing a system-initiated left or right turn at an intersection, the provisions of paragraphs 6.3.2. to 6.3.8. shall equally apply when going straight across that intersection (in non-highway environments where the system is able to perform system-initiated manoeuvres).
obligations.reason: New 6.4.1 under 6.4 (additional requirements for system-initiated manoeuvres in non-highway environments) extends 6.3.2-6.3.8 to the straight-across-intersection case for systems capable of system-initiated turns. No old paragraph has this scoped extension. The old 6.3.7 and 6.3.8 (R-035-type right-of-way) apply generally, but the new procedure scope creates a new obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The single prior obligation is supported and kept as an addition. 6.4.1 is a new paragraph in new section 6.4 that extends the scope of 6.3.2-6.3.8 (including the soft 'aim' right-of-way and restricted-lane provisions) to straight crossing at intersections for systems capable of system-initiated turns. It is not a modification of any base requirement. The source has no separable steps, so splitting is not needed. I added the inherited 6.4 non-highway applicability to the text. No reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: In non-highway environments, the system shall only make the vehicle automatically accelerate from standstill if, at the moment of drive off, the driver is not deemed to be visually disengaged as per paragraph 5.5.4.2.5 for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to the drive off.
obligations.reason: New drive-off condition for automatic acceleration from standstill in non-highway environments (6.4 applies to system-initiated manoeuvres in non-highway environments). No old requirement covers automatic drive-off. R-021 covers manoeuvre initiation with a 2 s disengagement qualifier but not drive-off from standstill, so this is added.

obligations.text: In non-highway environments, the system shall only make the vehicle automatically accelerate from standstill if, at the moment of drive off, the system has confirmed there is no risk of collision detected along the drive-off path.
obligations.reason: Separate cumulative drive-off condition (both conditions must be fulfilled) concerning collision risk along the drive-off path in non-highway environments. No old requirement covers it. R-022 only aims to avoid collision during manoeuvres and is a different scope.

clause_reviews.explanation: Clause 6.4.2 (annex path: 6. Additional Specifications for DCAS features > 6.4 > 6.4.2) sets two cumulative conditions for automatic drive-off in non-highway environments. They are kept as two separate entries with the shared scope repeated. The trailing heading '7. Monitoring of DCAS operation' is not an obligation and is excluded. The previous inventory is preserved; only the paragraph citation is corrected to the source clause number 6.4.2, since the list items (a) and (b) are not separate source clauses.

obligations.text: If remedial action addressing DCAS design is to be taken by the manufacturer, the Type Approval Authority shall upload the information received from the manufacturer in English language to the UNECE secure internet database "DETA" without undue delay but no later than 14 days after receipt, to communicate this information to all Type Approval Authorities.
obligations.reason: Same actor (Type Approval Authority), trigger (manufacturer remedial action addressing DCAS design), 14-day limit and DETA upload as old 7.2.2.2. Only editorial differences: 'the English language' became 'English language' and the footnote number changed.

obligations.text: If remedial action addressing DCAS design is to be taken by the manufacturer, the information uploaded to DETA shall be sufficient to understand the incident, the cause of it and the remedial action.
obligations.reason: Same sufficiency requirement as old 7.2.2.2, which is represented separately as R-103. The trigger condition is repeated here. Unchanged apart from editorial differences.

clause_reviews.explanation: New 7.2.2.2 compares word for word with old 7.2.2.2. The only differences are editorial: the article before 'English language', the footnote number, and a trailing quotation mark. The prior inventory matched both obligations to old o349. They map to base requirements R-102 (upload within 14 days) and R-103 (information sufficiency). No substantive change was found in actor, trigger, deadline or scope, so both are existing. The sentence pointing to Annex 6 guidance and the DETA URL footnote are informational and not obligations. The Annex 6 content is unchanged and is covered by other clauses.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall report at least once a year to the Type Approval Authority on the information deemed to be proper evidence of the intended operation collected through the monitoring program and safety of the system in the field, until production is definitively discontinued according to paragraph 14.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action, frequency and end condition as the old 7.2.3.1 first sentence; wording is unchanged.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall report at least the information listed in Table 1 (Information for Periodic Reporting) in the periodic report.
obligations.reason: The obligation to report at least the table information is retained. The table content changes are captured in the separate item entries.

obligations.text: The reported information can be shared in confidence with other Type Approval Authorities on request; the manufacturer shall be notified in this case.
obligations.reason: Unchanged sharing-in-confidence and notification provision of old 7.2.3.1. Old R-105 bundles it with the table reporting duty.

obligations.text: The reported information is not intended to be shared publicly.
obligations.reason: New sentence with no equivalent in old 7.2.3.1. It adds a confidentiality constraint on the information reported.

obligations.text: Additional information beyond the Table 1 information is subject to agreement between the Type Approval Authority and the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Old 7.2.3.1 had the same sentence. R-105 does not represent it, so there is no base requirement ID.

obligations.text: If the system was subject to significant changes relevant to the reported information during the reporting period, the report shall differentiate the changes of the system.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 7.2.3.1.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 1: report the total number of safety-critical occurrences known to the manufacturer (with related hours of operation and distance travelled), differentiated by the DCAS capability at the time (lane keeping; driver-initiated manoeuvres; driver-confirmed manoeuvres; system-initiated manoeuvres), and in each case whether the system was withholding HOR.
obligations.reason: The old item 1 required only the total of safety-critical occurrences. The new text adds differentiation by capability and by HOR withholding. Old table content has no base requirement ID; it is the old Table 1 item 1.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 2: report the number of vehicles equipped with the system (total, with related hours of operation and distance travelled unless specified); 2.a vehicles in which the system was available to be switched ON at any point in the period (if different from 2); 2.b vehicles in which the system was switched ON during the period; 2.c vehicles (of those in 2.a) from which no data was received; 2.d aggregated distance driven by the 2.a vehicles with the system in 'passive' mode; 2.e aggregated distance driven by the 2.a vehicles in 'active' mode.
obligations.reason: The old item 2 covered the number of vehicles and the aggregated distance in passive and active mode. The new text expands this into sub-items 2.a-2.e, adding availability, switched-ON and no-data counts, and restricting distances to the 2.a vehicles.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 3: report the number of events resulting in a driver unavailability response (total, with related hours of operation and distance travelled).
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Table 1 item 3.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 4: report the number of system-initiated deactivations of the system or its features due to 4.a detected system failures; 4.b exceeding system boundaries; 4.c exceeding system or feature boundaries while the driver is detected to be disengaged according to paragraph 5.3.5.1; 4.d other (if applicable).
obligations.reason: The old item 4 had 4.a failures, 4.b boundaries and 4.c other. New category 4.c covers boundary exceedance while the driver is disengaged, and 'Other' is renumbered 4.d.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 5: report the percentage of total distance travelled with a driver-set speed limit above the system-determined speed limit while the system is in 'active' mode.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Table 1 item 5.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 6: report disablement of the system due to insufficient driver engagement: 6.a number of events where the system was disabled due to insufficient engagement according to paragraph 5.5.4.2.8.2; 6.b number of events where the powertrain was deactivated less than 5 minutes after the disablement; 6.c number of events where the system was disabled due to repeated EOR warnings, including the number of warnings and the manufacturer-defined time interval per 5.5.4.2.8.3; 6.d the same for repeated HOR warnings.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Table 1 items 6.a-6.d. The cross-referenced 5.5.4.2.8.2 now has more criteria, so the reported events broaden by reference, but the item text is the same.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 7: report 7.a the number of events where 5 EORs are issued within a 10-minute period while the system is active, and 7.b the same for 5 HORs; once such an event is recorded, counting of EOR/HOR is reset for the purpose of reporting.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Table 1 items 7.a-7.b.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 8 (if applicable), during phases of withholding HORs without driver override of the longitudinal control: 8.a number of events where an upcoming boundary condition is detected and a HOR is given at least 5s in advance; 8.b number of events where a HOR is given but not at least 5s in advance (see 5.5.4.2.6.5.1); 8.c driving distance and time while the system is withholding HORs.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Table 1 items 8.a-8.c.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 9 (if applicable): report the number of started System-Initiated Manoeuvres in the highway environment, with 9.a percentage of driver-aborted System-Initiated Manoeuvres, 9.b percentage of system-aborted System-Initiated Manoeuvres, and 9.c percentage of System-Initiated Manoeuvres as per 5.3.7.2.4.10.
obligations.reason: The old item 9 required only the number of aborted System-Initiated Manoeuvres. The new item reports started manoeuvres in the highway environment, with abort percentages split by driver and system and a new 9.c percentage.

obligations.text: Table 1 item 10 (if applicable): report the number of started System-Initiated Manoeuvres in the non-highway environment, with 10.a percentage of driver-aborted manoeuvres, 10.b percentage of system-aborted manoeuvres, and 10.c percentage of system-initiated manoeuvres as per 5.3.7.2.4.10.
obligations.reason: Separate non-highway reporting item with no equivalent in the old table.

clause_reviews.explanation: Old Table 1 content has no base requirement IDs, so table items are listed with null existing_id. Items with changed content are listed as added because modified_existing needs an old base ID that does not exist. No obligations were removed or excluded. The heading '8. System Validation' was excluded as a heading only.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall provide to the Type Approval Authority at the time of type-approval, together with the Annex 3 documentation package, a yes/no declaration on whether the system continues to provide lateral control assistance, using input other than lane markings to reliably determine the course of the lane, for lane marking(s) listed in UN Regulation No. 130 (operating domain requirement: Highway).
obligations.reason: Table row in paragraph 9.1.8 is a manufacturer data item under the paragraph 9.1 data provision. The wording and scope are unchanged from old 9.1.8, which was renumbered by page only.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall provide to the Type Approval Authority at the time of type-approval, together with the Annex 3 documentation package, a yes/no declaration on whether the system continues to provide lateral control assistance, using input other than lane markings, for a lane marked with only a single marking (operating domain requirement: Non-Highway).
obligations.reason: Separate table row with a distinct situation and Non-Highway domain. It is unchanged from the same row in old 9.1.8 and falls under the paragraph 9.1 data provision.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall provide to the Type Approval Authority at the time of type-approval, together with the Annex 3 documentation package, a yes/no declaration on whether the system continues to provide lateral control assistance, using input other than lane markings, when road edges are the input (operating domain requirement: Non-Highway).
obligations.reason: Separate table row with a distinct situation. It is unchanged from the same row in old 9.1.8 and falls under the paragraph 9.1 data provision.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall provide to the Type Approval Authority at the time of type-approval, together with the Annex 3 documentation package, a yes/no declaration on whether the system continues to provide lateral control assistance, using input other than lane markings, when the lane is demarked by something other than a lane marking (parked cars, curb, construction infrastructure) (operating domain requirement: Non-Highway).
obligations.reason: Separate table row with a distinct situation. It is unchanged from the same row in old 9.1.8 and falls under the paragraph 9.1 data provision.

clause_reviews.explanation: Paragraph 9.1.8 and its four table rows are unchanged from old 9.1.8, apart from page position and formatting. Each row is kept as its own entry and mapped to R-107, the general paragraph 9.1 data-provision requirement. R-107 is the closest base requirement because no base requirement covers 9.1.8 specifically. The heading of section 10 is not an obligation and is excluded. No additions were found.

obligations.text: For the purpose of ensuring the software of the System can be identified, the vehicle manufacturer shall implement an R171SWIN.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 10.1 first sentence (page 31); same actor and object. Represented by R-108.

obligations.text: If the R171SWIN is not held on the vehicle, the vehicle manufacturer shall declare the software version(s) of the vehicle or single ECUs, with the connection to the relevant type approvals, to the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old 10.1 second sentence (R-109). The only change is correction of the typos 'R1XXSWIN' to 'R171SWIN' and 'ay' to 'may', which is editorial. The condition, actor and recipient are unchanged, so this is existing and not a modification.

obligations.text: The R171SWIN may be held on the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Permission in old 10.1 that the R171SWIN may be held on the vehicle. It is a separate permission, and the new text keeps it unchanged. It has no separate base requirement, so it is mapped to the closest old requirement R-109, which covers the alternative case.

clause_reviews.explanation: Clause 10.1 is unchanged in substance. The only differences are the typo corrections R1XXSWIN to R171SWIN and 'ay' to 'may'. The prior extraction labelled the second item modified_existing, which is not supported because the correction is editorial. The inventory splits the permission to hold the R171SWIN on the vehicle from the conditional declaration duty. No additions were made. Both mandatory duties map to R-108 and R-109. The permission has no distinct base ID and shares the R-109 context.

obligations.text: Production is not considered definitively discontinued if the vehicle manufacturer intends to obtain further approvals for software updates for vehicles already registered in the market.
obligations.reason: Same provision as old 14.2 (o384). The only change is the spelling 'definitely' to 'definitively', with no change to actor, scope or conditions. The old provision has no corresponding base requirement ID in the inventory. R-104 refers to production being 'definitively discontinued according to paragraph 14', but it is a separate reporting obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: Clause 14.2 is unchanged in substance from old 14.2 (page 33). The heading for section 15 that follows it is not an obligation and is excluded. No new obligation was found. There is no matching base requirement ID, so the entry is existing with existing_id null.

obligations.text: As from the official date of entry into force of the 01 series of amendments, no Contracting Party applying this Regulation shall refuse to grant or refuse to accept type approvals under this Regulation as amended by the 01 series of amendments.
obligations.reason: Old paragraph 16.1 carried identical wording on the same actor and scope (01 series). It is renumbered 16.1.1 under the new sub-heading 'Transitional Provisions applicable to the 01 series of amendments'. The obligation is unchanged.

clause_reviews.explanation: Clause 16.1.1 is word-for-word the old 16.1 and is only renumbered under the new 01-series sub-heading. The old paragraph has no corresponding base requirement, so existing_id is null. Nothing in the clause adds a separate obligation. The 02-series transitional provisions are in separate clauses (16.2.x).

obligations.text: As from 1 September 2027, Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall not be obliged to accept type approvals issued to the original version (00 series of amendments) of this Regulation, first issued after 1 September 2027.
obligations.reason: Clause is the old 16.2 renumbered to 16.1.2 under the new heading for the 01 series transitional provisions. The actor, date, 00-series scope and permission not to accept are all unchanged. No base requirement (R-...) represents this old provision, so existing_id is null.

clause_reviews.explanation: One permission (relief from the obligation to accept) is in the clause. It matches old paragraph 16.2 (o387) word for word. The only change is the renumbering and the new parent heading 'Transitional Provisions applicable to the 01 series of amendments'. That heading just groups the clause and does not alter its scope, since it already concerned the 00 series versus the 01 series. No R-xxx base requirement covers it, so existing_id is null. No new obligation is added and nothing is reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: Until 1 September 2030, Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall accept type approvals issued to the original version (00 series of amendments) of this Regulation, first issued before 1 September 2027.
obligations.reason: Same actor (Contracting Parties), action (accept 00 series type approvals), scope (first issued before 1 September 2027) and end date (1 September 2030) as old 16.3. The text is unchanged and was only renumbered to 16.1.3 under the new heading for the 01 series transitional provisions. This is an unchanged relocation, not a modification.

clause_reviews.explanation: Old 16.3 (o388) is the equivalent provision, and it has no corresponding base requirement R-xxx, so existing_id is null. The prior extraction labelled this modified_existing and pointed to a clause ID, which is not valid for existing_id. The wording is identical, and the only change is the paragraph number and its placement under the new 16.1 heading on the 01 series transitional provisions. The new 16.1 heading restates that the provision applies to the 01 series, which was already implicit, so I treat it as existing, not modified. No additional obligations are bundled in this clause, and nothing was reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: As from 1 September 2030, Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall not be obliged to accept type approvals issued to the original version (00 series of amendments) of this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Unchanged permission: the actor, date and scope (00 series approvals) match old 16.4. Only the numbering and placement changed, to 16.1.4 under the sub-heading for the 01 series transitional provisions. The 2030 cut-off is not the new 2032 or 2029 cut-offs for the 02 series, which are in separate clauses.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a renumbered copy of old 16.4. Actor, date (1 Sep 2030), scope (00 series) and the permissive nature are identical, so there is no substantive change. The prior 'modified_existing' label is rejected, and no base requirement R-xxx covers the old 16.4 transitional provision, so existing_id is null. The old source is paragraph 16.4 on page 33 (o389). It also creates no new obligation, because it only relieves Contracting Parties of a duty to accept.

obligations.text: Notwithstanding the transitional provisions above, Contracting Parties who start to apply this Regulation after the date of entry into force of the most recent series of amendments are not obliged to accept type approvals which were granted in accordance with the original version (00 series of amendments) of this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Old 16.5 has the same actor, condition, scope and permission (new Contracting Parties need not accept 00 series approvals). The clause is renumbered to 16.1.5 and sits under the 01 series transitional heading. The wording is unchanged. No base requirement R-xxx represents old 16.5, so existing_id is null. The prior extraction's 'modified_existing' label overstated the change, since it is only a renumbering.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction marked this as modified_existing with old_match o390. Comparison with old 16.5 shows identical text, so this is an unchanged existing provision that was renumbered. The actor (manufacturer) and action (explain) are new in this scope. Old context covers misuse safeguards, HMI messages and test tolerances, which have different objects. No base requirement covers it.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause is a single mandatory manufacturer explanation, so one obligation is retained. It applies only to systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres, inherited from parent heading 5 and 5.1. The prior addition is supported. No old base requirement (R-001 to R-117) has the same actor, action or scope, so it is not a modification or an existing item. No reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the manufacturer shall provide evidence of the driver's ability to control system operation.
obligations.reason: New controllability evidence obligation in Annex 3 Appendix 2, within the section on additional aspects for systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres (parent heading 5 and 5.2 'Evidence of controllability'). No old Annex 3 Appendix 2 clause or base requirement requires this evidence. R-001 and R-003 are general design requirements, and R-115 covers capability evidence only. The scope is therefore new.

clause_reviews.explanation: Single obligation. The clause is a manufacturer evidence duty. The system-initiated-manoeuvre scope is inherited from parent heading 5, so it is kept in the text. It was checked against the old context (5.1.4, 5.5.3.x, 2.3.8 and the others), and none contains an equivalent controllability-evidence obligation. The prior extraction is retained as an addition. There is no reversal or exclusion.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the manufacturer's evidence of controllability of system operation (Annex 3, Appendix 2, paragraphs 5.2.1 and 5.2.2) shall include situations where the driver is cancelling a manoeuvre before it is started.
obligations.reason: Parent 5.2 and 5.2.1 require evidence of the driver's ability to control system operation for systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres. 5.2.2 sets the minimum scope of that evidence, and this bullet covers driver cancellation before the manoeuvre starts. No old base requirement imposes controllability evidence for driver cancellation. R-024 and R-025 concern confirmation time and the EOR lockout, which have a different actor and object.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manouvres, the manufacturer's evidence of controllability of system operation (Annex 3, Appendix 2, paragraphs 5.2.1 and 5.2.2) shall include situations where the driver is aborting an ongoing manouvre.
obligations.reason: This is a separate operating case from cancelling before the start. It is a distinct evidence scenario under the same inherited scope of system-initiated manoeuvres. No old base requirement covers evidence of controllability when the driver aborts an ongoing manoeuvre.

clause_reviews.explanation: Both prior obligations are supported by the source and are kept as two separate entries, one per bullet. The inherited applicability from parent 5.2 and 5.2.1 is repeated in each entry. No old base requirement is equivalent, so both stay as additions. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the manufacturer shall provide evidence of its system validation, including the overall validation strategy and the results of its execution.
obligations.reason: New Annex 3 Appendix 2 para 5 is scoped to systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres, and 5.3.1 sits under that scope. It requires validation evidence consisting of the validation strategy and the results of its execution. No old provision requires validation evidence. Old Annex 3 Appendix 1 4.1 only covers verification of function and the list of tests, and the old R-115 capability evidence is a different scope. This is therefore a new obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction is supported. The clause contains one documentation obligation, with the strategy and the results as parts of a single evidence duty, so no split is needed. The scope inherited from the parent heading, 'systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres', is preserved. No base requirement matches: R-115 concerns capability evidence for the declaration, R-117 concerns demonstrating no unreasonable switching of control strategy, and R-107 concerns the data package. None covers validation strategy and results. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: For systems capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the system validation evidence provided by the manufacturer (including the overall validation strategy and results of its execution) shall include at least relevant real world driving test results.
obligations.reason: New content requirement for the validation evidence in the Annex 3 Appendix 2 additional assessment for systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres (parent 5 and 5.3.1). No old provision requires real world driving test results as part of validation evidence.

clause_reviews.explanation: Clause 5.3.2 is a single mandatory content requirement, so one obligation is returned. It inherits its scope from parent 5 (systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres) and 5.3.1 (system validation evidence). The old context contains no equivalent requirement for real world driving test results. The nearest base requirement, R-115, covers general capability evidence via documentation and has a different object and scope, so it is not an equivalent. The prior addition is supported and preserved. No exclusions or reversals apply.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall declare the system's ability to safely perform other system-initiated manoeuvres, or to respond to the target in non-highway environments without driver intervention, alternatively indicating 'Not Applicable'.
obligations.reason: The old declaration also covered driver-initiated manoeuvres; the new text is limited to system-initiated manoeuvres. The obligation to declare is retained with narrowed scope.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'Pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT in an intersection' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.11.1), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: The row is retained from the old table, but it now sits under the system-initiated-only heading.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'Bicycle target crossing into the path of the VUT in an intersection' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.12.1), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: The row is retained from the old table, but it now sits under the system-initiated-only heading.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'VUT turns across a path of an oncoming vehicle' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.13.1), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: The row is retained from the old table, but it now sits under the system-initiated-only heading.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'VUT crosses the straight path of a vehicle target in an intersection' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.14.1), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: The row is retained from the old table, but it now sits under the system-initiated-only heading.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'System-initiated manoeuvring around an obstruction in the lane' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.15), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: The row is retained from the old table, but it now sits under the system-initiated-only heading.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'Longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.16), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: This scenario row is new and was not in the old Appendix 4 paragraph 4 table.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'Cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.17), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: This scenario row is new and was not in the old Appendix 4 paragraph 4 table.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'Pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.18), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: This scenario row is new and was not in the old Appendix 4 paragraph 4 table.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'VUT crosses the straight path of the vehicle target in a partially obstructed intersection' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.19), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: This scenario row is new and was not in the old Appendix 4 paragraph 4 table.

obligations.text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'VUT turns across a path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.20), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
obligations.reason: This scenario row is new and was not in the old Appendix 4 paragraph 4 table.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior inventory is preserved. The general declaration is modified: the old text covered driver-initiated or system-initiated manoeuvres, the new text only system-initiated manoeuvres. R-113 is used as the closest base requirement (the Appendix 4 capability declaration). The first five scenario rows were in the old table, and the old paragraph had no matching base requirement, so they are marked existing with null id. The last five rows are new scenarios and are added. Each row is kept as a separate entry, and the 'Not Applicable' condition and the non-highway/no-driver-intervention scope are repeated in each.

obligations.text: All relevant base tests in Annex 4 shall be performed or witnessed by the Type Approval Authority or the Technical Service acting on its behalf during the approval process.
obligations.reason: Old Annex 4 / 1 required all tests in the annex to be performed or witnessed. The new text limits this to the relevant base tests, so the scope of the same obligation changes.

obligations.text: At least one extended test associated with each applicable base test shall be performed or witnessed during the approval process.
obligations.reason: Extended tests are new. The old Annex 4 / 1 had no equivalent obligation.

obligations.text: Further extended tests shall be performed or witnessed during the approval process at the request of the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: New TAA-request provision for further extended tests.

obligations.text: For those extended tests that are not performed during the approval process, the manufacturer shall provide evidence of the required system behaviour in those scenarios.
obligations.reason: New manufacturer evidence obligation for extended tests not performed.

obligations.text: During the assessment according to Annex 3, the Type Approval Authority may identify scenarios of particular relevance with regard to safety risk.
obligations.reason: New TAA permission.

obligations.text: An identified scenario with particular safety relevance may replace a base or extended test scenario only if the manufacturer provides satisfactory evidence of test performance of the replaced scenario.
obligations.reason: New conditional replacement permission.

obligations.text: The rationale for replacing a base or extended test and a detailed description of the identified scenario applied shall be documented in the test report.
obligations.reason: New documentation obligation tied to scenario replacement.

obligations.text: The specific test parameters for track tests shall be selected by the Type Approval Authority based on the declaration made by the manufacturer and shall be recorded in the test report in such a manner that allows traceability and repeatability of the test setup.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and scope as the old Annex 4 / 1 sentence. No base requirement represents it.

obligations.text: Pass- and fail-criteria for tests are derived solely from the technical requirements in paragraphs 5. and 6. of this UN Regulation and correspondence with the declarations made according to Appendix 4 to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Annex 4 / 1. No base requirement represents it.

obligations.text: The tests specified in Annex 4 are intended as a minimum set of tests. The Type Approval Authority may perform additional tests and compare the measured results against the requirements in paragraphs 5. and 6., or the contents of the Audit according to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Annex 4 / 1. No base requirement represents it.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction is supported and kept as 10 obligations. The old match o589 is a clause ID, not a base requirement ID. No R-ID covers the old Annex 4 / 1 provisions, so the unchanged provisions are marked existing with existing_id null, and the changed base-test scope is also marked existing with null. The old provision is Annex 4 / 1, which required all tests in the annex to be performed or witnessed. The scope change to relevant base tests is substantive, but it cannot be tied to a provided R-ID. The extended-test, scenario-replacement and test-report provisions are new.

obligations.text: The requirements and system aspects listed in Table A4/1 shall be tested during the physical tests; the relevant requirements or system aspects shall be chosen based on the system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and scope as old Annex 4 / 4.1.1. Only the table reference changed (table A4/1 to table 1) and the pages moved.

obligations.text: Scenarios with the aim of testing a given requirement or aspect shall be created and described in agreement with the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Annex 4 / 4.1.1.

obligations.text: Each requirement or aspect shall be assessed at least through track testing or public road verification.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Annex 4 / 4.1.1.

obligations.text: A given scenario may be used to assess different requirements / aspects of the system.
obligations.reason: Unchanged permission from old Annex 4 / 4.1.1. It is separated from the mandatory obligations.

obligations.text: Test scenarios shall be created depending on the system preconditions for activation and system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Annex 4 / 4.1.1.

obligations.text: For Table A4/1 items marked with an asterisk (functional requirements, driver unavailability response, failure response, DCAS operation/driver interaction/driver information, lane change, driver-confirmed lane changes), scenarios and test procedures shall be agreed between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Table A4/1 footnote content is identical in the old Annex 4 / 4.1.1. It is not a change.

clause_reviews.explanation: The new 4.1.1 matches old 4.1.1 in wording. Only the table label and pages changed, and Table A4/1 mappings are identical. None of the listed base requirements (R-001 to R-117) corresponds to this test-scope provision, so existing_id is null with the old source being Annex 4 / 4.1.1. No new obligations were found. The citation for the table-footnote entry is corrected to the assigned clause paragraph, Annex 4 / 4.1.1, on page 62.

obligations.text: For systems where identical initial conditions (e.g., path or positioning) of the vehicle in a given scenario may not always result in a repeatable outcome (e.g. using non-rule-based algorithms), the manufacturer shall explain this deviation to the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: New paragraph imposing a manufacturer explanation duty for non-repeatable systems. No old requirement in the provided base or old context covers it. Annex 4 3.1.6.2 repeat-test rules and 3.1.6.1 TAA-defined parameter combinations address different matters.

obligations.text: For systems where identical initial conditions (e.g., path or positioning) of the vehicle in a given scenario may not always result in a repeatable outcome (e.g. using non-rule-based algorithms), the manufacturer shall agree with the Type Approval Authority on the ranges of different test parameterization that do not modify the objective of the test scenario and diverge from other requirements of this regulation.
obligations.reason: Separate mandatory action: agreement with the TAA on parameterization ranges. It is distinct from the explanation step, and old 3.1.6.1 gives the TAA unilateral definition of test parameter combinations, so this is not an equivalent.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior single obligation bundled two independent mandatory steps (explain the deviation to the TAA, and agree on parameterization ranges), so I split them and repeated the shared condition. No equivalent old requirement exists in the inventory (R-001 to R-117), and the old context lacks this scope, so both are additions with null existing_id. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: In the lane positioning base test with a test speed and radius provoking a higher lateral acceleration than the declared maximum lateral acceleration + 0.3 m/s2, the VUT speed shall remain in the range declared by the manufacturer in paragraphs 9.1.1. and 9.1.2. of this UN Regulation.
obligations.reason: Old 4.2.5.1.1.1.2 (p.59) has identical wording, so this is unchanged. Only the page changed, from 59 to 65. No base requirement (R-xxx) represents Annex 4 test-procedure steps.

obligations.text: In the lane positioning base test exceeding the declared maximum lateral acceleration, the test shall be carried out for each speed range declared by the manufacturer in paragraphs 9.1.1. and 9.1.2. separately, or within contiguous speed ranges where the declared maximum lateral acceleration is identical.
obligations.reason: Identical to the old 4.2.5.1.1.1.2 second paragraph (p.59), so this is unchanged. No base requirement represents it.

obligations.text: In the lane positioning base test exceeding the declared maximum lateral acceleration, the VUT shall be driven without any force applied by the driver on the steering control (e.g. by removing the hands from the steering control) at a constant speed on a curved track with lane markings at each side.
obligations.reason: Identical to the old 4.2.5.1.1.1.2 third paragraph (p.59), so this is unchanged. No base requirement represents it.

obligations.text: In the lane positioning base test exceeding the declared maximum lateral acceleration, the Type Approval Authority shall define a test speed and a radius which would provoke a higher acceleration than the declared maximum lateral acceleration + 0.3 m/s2 (e.g. by travelling with a higher speed through a curve with a given radius).
obligations.reason: Identical to the old 4.2.5.1.1.1.2 fourth paragraph (p.59), so this is unchanged. The prior extraction labelled it modified_existing, but no substantive change exists, so it is existing.

clause_reviews.explanation: The new clause n677 repeats old 4.2.5.1.1.1.2 word for word, and only the page moved from 59 to 65. All four steps are retained as unchanged. The fourth step was wrongly marked modified_existing in the prior extraction. The base requirements list contains no Annex 4 test-procedure items, so the existing_id values are null and the old source is the same paragraph on page 59. No additions, reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: In the Extended Testing for a stationary vehicle ahead on a straight section of road, the test shall be executed at least with a stationary vehicle of a different type or category.
obligations.reason: Same scoped case as old 4.2.5.2.1.3.1(a); the wording is unchanged.

obligations.text: In the Extended Testing for a stationary vehicle ahead on a straight section of road, the test shall be executed at least with a stationary vehicle positioned at a larger offset to the VUT's centerline.
obligations.reason: Same scoped case as old 4.2.5.2.1.3.1(b); only the spelling changed from centreline to centerline.

obligations.text: In the Extended Testing for a stationary vehicle ahead on a straight section of road, for systems able to operate in non-highway conditions, the test shall be executed at least with a stationary vehicle facing towards the VUT.
obligations.reason: Same scoped case and condition as old 4.2.5.2.1.3.1(c); unchanged.

clause_reviews.explanation: The new clause repeats old Annex 4 / 4.2.5.2.1.3.1 (a)-(c), with the same scenario scope and the same non-highway condition on (c). The only difference is centreline becoming centerline. No base requirement corresponds to these Annex 4 test-procedure items (R-116 and R-117 are generic Appendix 4 requirements), so each is an unchanged old provision with existing_id null. No additions or reversals were found.

obligations.text: In the bicycle intersection base test, the bicycle target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the VUT's direction of travel at a constant speed of 15 km/h +0/-1 km/h, starting not before the functional part of the test has started.
obligations.reason: Identical to the old 4.2.5.2.12.1.1 text on target path, speed and start timing; no change in actor, action or scope.

obligations.text: In the bicycle intersection base test, during the acceleration phase of the bicycle target prior to the functional part of the test, the bicycle target shall be obstructed.
obligations.reason: Identical to the old 4.2.5.2.12.1.1 sentence; unchanged.

obligations.text: In the bicycle intersection base test, the bicycle target's positioning shall be coordinated with the VUT so that the impact point of the bicycle target on the front of the VUT is on the longitudinal centreline, with an offset of not more than 0.2 m, if the VUT would remain at the prescribed test speed throughout the functional part of the test and does not brake.
obligations.reason: The old text already had the 0.2 m limit and the 'if VUT remains at test speed and does not brake' condition. The new wording drops 'of the VUT' and 'with a tolerance of' (the old text had 'longitudinal centreline offset'), an editorial change with no substantive effect. The 0.2 m limit is retained.

clause_reviews.explanation: Compared the new 4.2.5.2.12.1.1 with the old 4.2.5.2.12.1.1 and with parallel bicycle crossing test 4.2.5.2.10.1.1 in the old context. The three separable steps (target path and speed, obstruction during acceleration, positioning with 0.2 m limit) are all present in the old text. The only wording difference is the editorial change in the centreline and offset phrase. There is no base requirement (R-...) for these Annex 4 test details, so existing_id is null for all three. The existing source was the old 4.2.5.2.12.1.1 (previously o723). No additions or modifications are supported.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle in an intersection (4.2.5.2.13.1), the target vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h, depending on the declared system boundaries.
obligations.reason: The old text has an identical sentence only at 4.2.5.2.14.1.2, which is the separate scenario where the VUT crosses the straight path of a vehicle target. It is flagged missing_parent_clause. In the new text the sentence sits under 4.2.5.2.13.1 for the turning scenario. The speed limit for the target is therefore a separately scoped test-procedure obligation for the turning base test. There is no base requirement equivalent, so it is added.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior submitted addition is supported and kept, with the scenario scope stated. The old context has the same wording only under 4.2.5.2.14.1.2, a different scenario (crossing, not turning). It is a new scoped test parameter, not a relocation. No existing base requirement (R-001 to R-117) covers it. Nothing was reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: In the crossing vehicle target base test (VUT crosses the straight path of the vehicle target in an intersection), the VUT shall approach the impact point with another vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) target in an initial straight line in an intersection from either the near side or far side direction, to collide the side of the target vehicle at 25 per cent along the length of the target with the centre front of the VUT.
obligations.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.14.1.1 sentence is carried over word for word, so there is no substantive change. The old text appears on page 71, where it is run together with 4.2.5.2.14.1.2. Under the new text this is a standalone paragraph on page 77.

clause_reviews.explanation: The new clause 4.2.5.2.14.1.1 is identical to the first sentence of old 4.2.5.2.14.1.1 (old page 71). Actor (the VUT), action, scope (near or far side, 25 per cent along the target length, centre front of the VUT), the vehicle target type and the parent base test for crossing vehicle targets are all unchanged. The sentence is a single obligation with alternative near-side and far-side directions, which stay together. The old text also contains 4.2.5.2.14.1.2 (target speed up to 60 km/h, VUT expected to give right of way), but the new text has that as a separate clause, so it is not part of this assignment. No base requirement (R-001 to R-117) represents this old test procedure, so existing_id is null. The old provision is the first sentence of Annex 4 / 4.2.5.2.14.1.1 (old o734). The prior extraction's 'existing' disposition is therefore supported. Nothing was added, modified, reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target in an intersection, the target shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h, depending on the declared system boundaries.
obligations.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.14.1.2 (old page 70, run together with 4.2.5.2.14.1.1 on page 71) had the same obligation in the same crossing-vehicle base test. It is unchanged in actor, action, scope and conditions. It has no matching base requirement because R-001 to R-117 are the main regulation requirements.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target in an intersection, the VUT is expected to give right of way to the crossing target vehicle.
obligations.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.14.1.2 on page 71 contained the same sentence. The sentence now appears in its own paragraph, but the scope and the expected outcome are the same. It has no matching base requirement.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause has two separate obligations: the target approach speed of up to 60 km/h and the VUT right-of-way expectation. Both are unchanged from the old crossing-vehicle base test, so neither is novel. The old text sat in the same scenario, 4.2.5.2.14, and the only differences are page and paragraph placement. The base requirements hold only main-text requirements, so there is no R-ID for either obligation. The clause adds no new scope and nothing is reversed or excluded. The new 4.2.5.2.19.1.2 and 4.2.5.2.13.1.2 carry similar wording for different scenarios and are not part of this clause.

obligations.text: In the extended test for a VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target in an intersection (4.2.5.2.14.2), the test shall be executed at least with different target vehicle types or categories, different overlaps, and different lane positions of the VUT and target vehicle.
obligations.reason: Same scoped extended-test variation list as old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1 in the same crossing-vehicle intersection scenario. Only minor wording differences (singular 'target vehicle'), so there is no substantive change.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause repeats old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1 (old o736) with the same actor, action, scope and conditions. It is a variation list under the unobstructed-intersection extended test, and the old parent context is unchanged. No base requirement R-xxx represents it, so existing_id is null. The only difference is 'vehicles' becoming 'vehicle', which is editorial. The three items (a)-(c) are alternative variations of one obligation, so they stay together. This is not a modification and not an addition, because the new partially obstructed scenario 4.2.5.2.19.2.1 is a separate clause.

obligations.text: In the base test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a longitudinally moving target and any lateral movement navigating around the target, if applicable.
obligations.reason: New base test scenario (longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, 4.2.5.2.16). The old 4.2.5.2.8.1 covers a stationary bicycle target, which is a different test scope, so this is a separately scoped test obligation. The wording is repeated but the procedure scope is new. The Type Approval Authority conducts or witnesses it under 4.2.5 for the declared operating domains.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction is supported as a single obligation. The clause is one sentence and has no bundled independent steps, permissions or alternative conditions to split. The old 4.2.5.2.8.1 base test for a stationary bicycle target is not represented in base_requirements, so no existing R-ID applies. The 'if applicable' qualifier on lateral movement is kept inside the single obligation. Nothing was reversed or excluded.
