obligations.text: In the base test for the longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the bicycle target shall be positioned within the driving path of the VUT facing away from the subject vehicle.
obligations.reason: New test scenario 4.2.5.2.16 (longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane) introduces its own positioning requirement for the target. Wording repeats the stationary bicycle test in 4.2.5.2.8.1.1, but that is a separate procedure with a different scope, so this is a distinct obligation scoped to the new moving-bicycle base test.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause has a single mandatory test set-up action: positioning the bicycle target in the VUT driving path facing away. The old context contains identical wording only for the stationary bicycle test (4.2.5.2.8.1.1), a different procedure. The new moving-bicycle scenario 4.2.5.2.16 applies the requirement to a new test, so it is a new obligation rather than an existing or modified one. No base requirement corresponds to it, and nothing in the prior extraction needed reversal or exclusion.

obligations.text: In the base test for the longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the VUT shall approach the impact point with the cyclist target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test.
obligations.reason: Repeated wording from the stationary bicycle test (4.2.5.2.8.1.2) now applies to the newly introduced longitudinally moving bicycle target scenario (4.2.5.2.16). The new procedure scope creates a separately applicable obligation, so it is not a modification or duplicate of an old requirement.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause contains one independent test-procedure obligation, with no separate permissions or exceptions to split out. The old context has near-identical wording only for the stationary bicycle (4.2.5.2.8.1.2) and pedestrian (4.2.5.2.7.1.2) scenarios. Those cover different targets and procedures, and no base requirement represents the moving-bicycle scenario, so the prior addition is supported and retained. Nothing was reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: In the base test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.16.1), the bicycle target shall travel with a constant speed of 20 (+1/-1) km/h.
obligations.reason: The clause sets a specific bicycle target speed and tolerance for the newly introduced longitudinally moving bicycle base test. The old context has no equivalent: the 15 km/h crossing bicycle speeds in 4.2.5.2.10.1.1 and 4.2.5.2.12.1.1 apply to different scenarios and have different tolerances.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior single obligation is retained as an addition. The scenario 4.2.5.2.16 is new, so its constant 20 (+1/-1) km/h test condition is a new obligation, even though similar bicycle-speed wording exists for other scenarios. No existing requirement (R-001 to R-117) covers it, and it is not a modification of any of them. The clause contains one independent obligation, so there is nothing to split.

obligations.text: Annex 4 / 4.2.5 / 4.2.5.2 / 4.2.5.2.16 / 4.2.5.2.16.2 Extended testing for the longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane: the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a bicycle.
obligations.reason: The clause is a new extended-test obligation for the new scenario 4.2.5.2.16 (longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane). The old context has similar extended-test wording only for other scenarios (stationary pedestrian, stationary bicycle, crossing bicycle). The scenario scope differs, so this is not a relocation of any old obligation. The old requirements R-116 and R-117 are generic Appendix 4 control-strategy provisions and are not scenario-specific Annex 4 extended tests, so they are not modified by this clause.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction was reviewed and the single addition is supported. The clause is a single mandatory extended-test requirement with no bundled items, so no split is needed. It is not a modification of R-116 or R-117 because those are generic. No obligation was reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: In the extended test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the test shall be executed at least with a bicycle target positioned with different offsets, up to the target being outside of the driving path of the VUT.
obligations.reason: The offset variation resembles stationary bicycle 4.2.5.2.8.2.1(a). This clause belongs to the new longitudinally moving bicycle scenario (4.2.5.2.16), which has no old counterpart, so it is a separately scoped procedure.

obligations.text: In the extended test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the test shall be executed at least with a different speed of the VUT.
obligations.reason: The VUT speed variation exists in the old stationary bicycle test, but the moving bicycle scenario is new. This is a separately scoped test variation.

obligations.text: In the extended test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the test shall be executed at least with a different speed of the bicycle target within the range of 10-25 km/h.
obligations.reason: The bicycle target speed range of 10-25 km/h has no counterpart in the old text. It applies only to the new moving bicycle scenario.

clause_reviews.explanation: The source clause lists three independent minimum test variations (a)-(c) for the new moving bicycle extended test. The old context has no 4.2.5.2.16 scenario, and the stationary bicycle clause 4.2.5.2.8.2.1 has different scope and items. All three prior additions are supported, kept as separate additions, and not matched to base requirements. R-116 and R-117 are generic control-strategy obligations and do not cover these specific test conditions. No reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: Base Test: the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a cut-out of the lead M1 category vehicle when other vehicles are fully or partially blocking the lane.
obligations.reason: New scenario 4.2.5.2.17 'Cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle'. The old 4.2.5.2.5.1 base test covers cut-out of the lead M1 vehicle without blocking vehicles. The blocking-vehicle condition extends the test scope, so this is a separate, newly scoped test obligation and not a renumbering.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause contains a single mandatory test obligation, which the prior extraction captured correctly. It is not a modification of the old 4.2.5.2.5.1 cut-out test, because the old test has no interfering or blocking vehicles. The old 4.2.5.2.5.1 test continues in its own scenario, and no base requirement (R-001 to R-117) corresponds to it. The prior inventory is preserved with no reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: In the base test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle (other vehicles fully or partially blocking the lane), the vehicle cutting out shall perform a full lane change (e.g., 3.5 m lateral displacement) into the adjacent lane to avoid the stationary vehicle target, with the measurement behind the stationary vehicle target indicating the start of the lane change and the measurement in front of the stationary vehicle target indicating the end of the lane change.
obligations.reason: The wording repeats 4.2.5.2.5.1.1 (cut-out base test). It now applies to the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17 (cut-out with an interfering/blocking vehicle), a separately scoped test procedure under the new base test 4.2.5.2.17.1. The old procedure remains for its own scenario, so this is a new obligation, not a relocation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior addition is supported and kept. The clause repeats the wording of old 4.2.5.2.5.1.1 (no base requirement exists for it). It sits under the new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17.1, so the test scope is new. Nothing in it needs splitting: the lane change and the start and end measurement points are one procedure step. No reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: In the base test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the indicated TTC is defined as the TTC of the lead vehicle to the target at the moment the lead vehicle starts the lane change.
obligations.reason: The wording is identical to old 4.2.5.2.5.1.2 (cut-out without interfering vehicle). It now sits under the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17 (cut-out with an interfering vehicle), so it applies to a new procedure scope. It is a separately scoped obligation, not a relocation. No base requirement (R-...) covers it.

obligations.text: In the base test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the lead vehicle shall not use indicators during the lane change manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: This is a separate test-procedure restriction (second sentence). It has the same wording as old 4.2.5.2.5.1.2, but it applies to the new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17. No base requirement covers it.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior two-obligation inventory is retained. The clause has two independent elements: the TTC definition and the no-indicators restriction. Both repeat old wording from 4.2.5.2.5.1.2 (the cut-out test without an interfering vehicle). They apply to the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17, so they stay separate additions. The old paragraph still exists in its own scenario, so they are not modifications. No base R-xxx requirement represents the old provision, so existing_id is null. Nothing is reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: In the cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle base test (4.2.5.2.17.1), the cutting out vehicle shall not deviate from its defined path by more than ±0.2 m.
obligations.reason: The wording matches old 4.2.5.2.5.1.3, but it now sits under the new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17. That is a new test procedure scope, so it creates a separately scoped obligation. The old cut-out test continues in its own scenario.

obligations.text: In the cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle base test (4.2.5.2.17.1), the cut-out at TTC = 3 s shall be run with VUT set speed 70 km/h, lead vehicle (M1 category) speed 50 km/h, lane change lateral acceleration of the SOV 1.5 m/s2, lane change length 44 m and radius of turning segment 130 m.
obligations.reason: The parameter table is repeated from old 4.2.5.2.5.1.3, but it now applies to the new interfering-vehicle scenario. It is a separate test-parameter obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction is supported and kept. The sentence and the table are separate obligations, so they stay as two entries. No existing R-xxx base requirement covers Annex 4 test-procedure parameters for this scenario. The old equivalent, 4.2.5.2.5.1.3, has no base requirement ID in the inventory. The new scope, with blocking vehicles, justifies treating both as added. There are no reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: In the base test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the blocking vehicle in the adjacent lane shall drive under conditions where the VUT is prevented from changing lanes, specifically where the conditions of paragraph 6.2.4.1. are not met.
obligations.reason: New blocking-vehicle set-up in the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17. The old context has no equivalent. The old cut-out test 4.2.5.2.5.1 and the 6.2.4.1 lane-change conditions are not the same obligation.

obligations.text: During the cut-out of the lead vehicle in the interfering vehicle base test, the blocking vehicle in the adjacent lane shall, as one trajectory case, continue with the same constant speed. The shared condition is that the blocking vehicle drives so that the VUT is prevented from changing lanes (conditions of paragraph 6.2.4.1. not met).
obligations.reason: Independent blocking trajectory (a). The shared blocking condition is repeated because the trajectories are split into separate cases.

obligations.text: During the cut-out of the lead vehicle in the interfering vehicle base test, the blocking vehicle in the adjacent lane shall, as another trajectory case, brake with the same deceleration as the VUT, blocking the way of the lane change, until the VUT stops or passes the static target. The shared condition is that the blocking vehicle drives so that the VUT is prevented from changing lanes (conditions of paragraph 6.2.4.1. not met).
obligations.reason: Independent blocking trajectory (b). The shared blocking condition is repeated because the trajectories are split into separate cases.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction's three obligations are supported and retained. Each is new because the interfering-vehicle scenario has no old equivalent. The old context holds only the plain cut-out test (4.2.5.2.5.1.x) and the 6.2.4.1 assessment. Neither sets up blocking vehicle behaviour. No existing requirement matches, so none is modified or marked existing. The shared blocking condition is repeated in the (a) and (b) entries. The (a) and (b) trajectories are alternative test cases, so they stay separate. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: Extended Testing for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle: the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a cut-out of the lead vehicle.
obligations.reason: Clause 4.2.5.2.17.2 sits under the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17 (cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, p.80). It repeats the wording of old 4.2.5.2.5.2, but that clause applies to the separate cut-out scenario 4.2.5.2.5. The new test scope is therefore a separate, independently applicable test obligation. It is not shown to be a renumbering, and the old clause remains in the new text.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior single obligation is supported and is retained as an addition. The old context has the same wording only for scenario 4.2.5.2.5 (cut-out without an interfering vehicle). The new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17 is new scope, so the extended test is a new obligation rather than an existing or modified one. R-116 and R-117 are general Appendix 4 duties about control-strategy switching and demonstration. They are not equivalent to this scenario-specific Annex 4 test requirement, so I did not map it to them. The clause contains a single mandatory step, so no splitting is needed. Nothing was reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle (blocking vehicles fully or partially blocking the lane), the test shall be executed at least with a stationary vehicle target of a different type or category, including cyclist and pedestrian (if the system is designed to drive in non-highway roads).
obligations.reason: Applies to the new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17.2. The similar old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1(a) covers cut-out without an interfering vehicle and had no cyclist/pedestrian target or non-highway condition. This is a separate scoped obligation.

obligations.text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the test shall be executed at least with the cut-out occurring at less than 3 seconds TTC of the lead vehicle.
obligations.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1(b) wording is repeated, but under the new interfering-vehicle procedure scope, so it is a separate obligation.

obligations.text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the test shall be executed at least with different speeds of the VUT and lead vehicle.
obligations.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1(c) wording is repeated, but under the new interfering-vehicle procedure scope, so it is a separate obligation.

obligations.text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the test shall be executed at least with different lateral acceleration of the lead vehicle.
obligations.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1(d) wording is repeated, but under the new interfering-vehicle procedure scope, so it is a separate obligation.

obligations.text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the test shall be executed at least with impassable objects.
obligations.reason: This test condition has no counterpart in the old cut-out extended test list.

clause_reviews.explanation: Prior extraction preserved. Five independent test conditions in the new interfering-vehicle extended test each scoped to the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17.2. They were checked against the old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1 list; scope differs, so they are treated as new rather than existing. No matching R-ID, since R-116/R-117 are general control-strategy requirements in Appendix 4 and do not cover this scenario's specific test conditions. Nothing was reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: Base Test for pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre: the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a crossing pedestrian target, while another vehicle obstructs the lane of travel and the perception of the pedestrian target.
obligations.reason: New scenario 4.2.5.2.18 (drive around manoeuvre) with an obstructing vehicle and obstructed perception. The old crossing-pedestrian base test (4.2.5.2.9.1) covers a plain crossing pedestrian without obstruction, so its scope differs. No old R-xxx requirement represents it, and the changed scope makes this a distinct obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior single obligation is supported and retained. The clause is one base-test mandate with no bundled independent steps. The old 4.2.5.2.9.1 crossing pedestrian test has no base requirement ID and a different scope (no obstructing vehicle, no drive around), so it is added as new rather than existing. No reversal or exclusion was applied.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for a pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1), a static target shall be placed in front of the VUT with 50% overlap towards the edge of the road.
obligations.reason: Test set-up for the new 4.2.5.2.18 scenario. The old 4.2.5.2.15.1.2 has the same static target placement, but it sits in a different scenario (adjacent-lane moving vehicle target, synchronised arrival). The scoped obligation is therefore new.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for a pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1), the VUT shall travel at least 30 km/h toward the static target with system-initiated manoeuvring activated.
obligations.reason: Speed and activation condition for the new scenario. It is a separate procedural step from the target placement. The old 4.2.5.2.15.1.2 and 4.2.5.2.15.1.3 conditions apply to a different scenario with a moving vehicle target.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for a pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1), the VUT shall avoid collision with the target if performing a drive around manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Pass criterion for the new scenario. It is conditional on a drive around manoeuvre being performed. The old 4.2.5.2.15.1.3 requires avoiding collision with the targets in a different scenario, so equivalence is not established.

clause_reviews.explanation: The three prior obligations are kept as separate independent entries: the target placement, the VUT speed and activation condition, and the collision-avoidance criterion. All are scoped to the new pedestrian-crossing drive-around scenario. The wording is similar to old 4.2.5.2.15.1.x, but that clause covers a different scenario, and no base requirement (R-001 to R-117) corresponds to these test-procedure details. They are therefore added, with existing_id null. No exclusions or reversals.

obligations.text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1.2), the pedestrian target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the VUT's direction of travel at a constant speed of 5 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h from a maximum of 1 m from the front of the static target.
obligations.reason: New drive-around scenario (4.2.5.2.18). The pedestrian starts within 1 m of the static target's front, and the old 4.2.5.2.9.1.3 'starting not before the functional part of the test' wording and its separate scenario scope are absent. It is a separately scoped test-procedure obligation, not a continuation of the old crossing-pedestrian clause.

obligations.text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1.2), the pedestrian target's positioning shall be coordinated with the VUT so that the impact point of the pedestrian target on the front of the VUT is on the longitudinal centreline of the VUT if the VUT would remain at the speed it has when reaching the rear of the static target and does not brake.
obligations.reason: The reference speed is the VUT speed on reaching the rear of the static target, rather than the prescribed test speed. No 0.2 m tolerance is stated, unlike old 4.2.5.2.9.1.3. This is a separate coordination obligation for the new scenario.

clause_reviews.explanation: Both prior obligations are supported by the source and are retained as separate entries: the pedestrian travel and speed requirement, and the positioning coordination requirement. The old comparable clauses (4.2.5.2.9.1.3 for pedestrian, 4.2.5.2.10.1.1 for bicycle) cover different scenarios and have different start, reference-speed and tolerance wording, so these are added rather than existing or modified. No base requirement R-xxx corresponds to this test-procedure detail. No obligations were reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: Extended testing for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18): the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a crossing pedestrian target.
obligations.reason: Same wording as old 4.2.5.2.9.2 (plain crossing pedestrian), but the new clause applies to a separately introduced scenario, 4.2.5.2.18 (drive around manoeuvre with an obstructing static target). The new procedure scope creates a new extended-test obligation rather than a relocation. R-116/R-117 are the general control-strategy and demonstration duties in Appendix 4 and do not cover this scenario-specific test.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause holds one independent obligation: the extended test for the new drive around pedestrian-crossing scenario. The old text in 4.2.5.2.9.2 has identical wording but a different scope (no obstructing vehicle, no drive around), so I kept it as an addition. There is no modification of an existing requirement and no reversal or exclusion. The prior extraction is retained, with the paragraph path completed.

obligations.text: In the extended test for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (4.2.5.2.18.2), the test shall be executed at least with a static and pedestrian target of a different type and/or size.
obligations.reason: Old 4.2.5.2.9.2.1(a) only varied pedestrian size, in a plain crossing scenario. This variation covers both the static target and the pedestrian target, and applies to the newly introduced drive around scenario 4.2.5.2.18.

obligations.text: In the extended test for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (4.2.5.2.18.2), the test shall be executed at least with a pedestrian target moving at a different, but constant speed.
obligations.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.9.2.1(b), but the scope is the newly introduced drive around scenario 4.2.5.2.18, so it is a separate obligation.

obligations.text: In the extended test for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (4.2.5.2.18.2), the test shall be executed at least with a different angle of the pedestrian target path to the VUT path.
obligations.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.9.2.1(c), but the scope is the newly introduced drive around scenario 4.2.5.2.18, so it is a separate obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction of three separate obligations is supported. Items (a)-(c) are independent test variations and are kept separate. The old context has no drive around scenario (4.2.5.2.18), so none of the three maps to an existing base requirement. The old plain crossing-pedestrian test 4.2.5.2.9.2.1 has no matching base requirement and is a different scenario, so each item is a new scoped obligation.

obligations.text: In the partially obstructed intersection scenario (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target, Annex 4 / 4.2.5.2.19), the Base Test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system to recognize and offer right of way for a crossing vehicle target driving straight in an intersection.
obligations.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.14.1 (the unobstructed intersection Base Test), but the new paragraph sits under the newly introduced partially obstructed intersection scenario 4.2.5.2.19. It is therefore a separately applicable test obligation, not a renumbering of the old one. No base requirement (R-001 to R-117) covers it, so it is added.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause has one obligation: the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection. Old 4.2.5.2.14.1 has identical wording but belongs to the unobstructed intersection scenario, so the new scenario scope makes this a new obligation. The prior extraction is supported and is kept as one entry. The clause contains no further independent steps, permissions or exceptions to split out. The clause is annex test text with no matching base requirement, so existing_id is null.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the VUT shall approach the impact point with another vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) target in an initial straight line in an intersection from the near side direction only, to collide the side of the target vehicle at 25 per cent along the length of the target with the centre front of the VUT.
obligations.reason: The paragraph sits under the new partially obstructed intersection scenario 4.2.5.2.19. It restricts the approach direction to the near side, whereas the old 4.2.5.2.14.1.1 (unobstructed crossing) allows either near side or far side. This is a separately scoped test setup obligation, not a renumbering. No base requirement R-### corresponds to it.

clause_reviews.explanation: The single prior addition is supported and retained. The clause is one test-setup obligation with no separable independent steps: approach geometry, near-side direction and the 25 per cent impact point form one setup. The old 4.2.5.2.14.1.1 wording is similar but covers the near or far side in the unobstructed scenario, so the near-side-only scope in the new procedure creates a new obligation. No existing R-ID matches, and no base requirement is modified or reversed by this clause.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target), the target shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h, depending on the declared system boundaries.
obligations.reason: The parameter is the same as in the unobstructed intersection test (4.2.5.2.14.1.2). It is repeated here under the new partially obstructed intersection procedure (4.2.5.2.19), so it is a separately applicable test parameter.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target), the VUT is expected to give right of way to the crossing target.
obligations.reason: The expected outcome is the same as in the unobstructed intersection test (4.2.5.2.14.1.2). It is repeated here as a separate pass expectation under the new partially obstructed scenario (4.2.5.2.19).

clause_reviews.explanation: The old context contains the same wording only in 4.2.5.2.14.1.2, which covers the unobstructed intersection. The old 4.2.5.2.19 scenario did not exist, and no base requirement (R-001 to R-117) covers these test parameters. The two sentences are independent items, a target speed parameter and a right-of-way expectation, so they are kept as two separate additions. The prior extraction is retained. No reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target in a partially obstructed intersection (Annex 4 / 4.2.5.2.19.1), a static target shall be placed in the opposite direction of travel at the same side of the intersection, such that it obstructs the view of the coming moving target but does not interfere with the path of the VUT.
obligations.reason: The view-obstructing static target set-up is new and applies only to the newly introduced partially obstructed intersection scenario (4.2.5.2.19). No old clause sets up a static target that obstructs the view of a moving target in an intersection test, so the prior addition is supported.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction is retained as one added obligation. The source paragraph states a single test set-up requirement, so there is nothing to split. The old context contains no equivalent static view-obstructing target requirement. The nearby old straight-line and drive-around set-ups (4.2.5.2.15.1.x) place a static target for a different purpose, and none corresponds to a view obstruction in an intersection. No base requirement R-xxx matches it, so existing_id is null. There are no rejected existing or modified_existing obligations to review, and no reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: In the partially obstructed intersection scenario (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target), the extended test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a crossing vehicle target driving straight in an intersection.
obligations.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.14.2, but that clause is scoped to the unobstructed intersection scenario. This one sits under new scenario 4.2.5.2.19 (partially obstructed intersection), so it is a separately scoped extended-test obligation and not a relocation. No old requirement in the base inventory covers it. R-116 and R-117 are general Appendix 4 control-strategy statements, not this scenario-specific test.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction is supported. There is a single obligation, with no bundled items. The new test scope (partially obstructed intersection, 4.2.5.2.19) creates a new obligation despite repeated wording from 4.2.5.2.14.2. It is not a duplicate of any base requirement, so it stays an addition with existing_id null. No reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different target vehicle types or categories.
obligations.reason: Separately scoped extended-test variation for the new partially obstructed intersection scenario (4.2.5.2.19.2). The old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1(a) applies to the unobstructed intersection scenario only.

obligations.text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different overlaps.
obligations.reason: Independent variation item for the new partially obstructed intersection scenario. The old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1(b) is scoped to the unobstructed scenario.

obligations.text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different lane positions of the VUT and the moving target vehicle.
obligations.reason: Independent variation item for the new partially obstructed intersection scenario. The old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1(c) is scoped to the unobstructed scenario.

obligations.text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different positions of the static target.
obligations.reason: New variation item with no counterpart in the old unobstructed-intersection list. It relates to the static view-obstructing target introduced in 4.2.5.2.19.1.3.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior single bundled obligation is split into four independent test-variation obligations, one per item (a)-(d), each repeating the shared lead-in and the partially obstructed intersection scope. None is a modification of an existing R-requirement. The base requirements do not represent the old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1 list, and the scenario scope is new. There are no reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist, the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection with multiple targets.
obligations.reason: Paragraph 4.2.5.2.20.1 is a new test scenario (4.2.5.2.20, oncoming vehicle plus cyclist). The old 4.2.5.2.13.1 base test covered a single oncoming vehicle target with no cyclist. The multiple-target scope is a separate procedure obligation, even though the wording is largely repeated.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior single obligation is supported and kept. The clause holds one independent mandatory base-test requirement, so there is nothing to split. It is not a modification of old 4.2.5.2.13.1, because the multiple-target scope is new. No old base requirement (R-...) corresponds to it, so existing_id is null. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (multiple targets), the VUT shall approach the impact point with another vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) target in an initial straight line followed by a turn in an intersection to cross the front edges of the target vehicle, with a lateral position giving a 50 per cent overlap of the width of the VUT.
obligations.reason: The wording repeats the old oncoming-vehicle turning test (4.2.5.2.13.1.1), but it sits under the newly introduced multiple-target oncoming vehicle and cyclist test (4.2.5.2.20.1). That new procedure scope creates a separately applicable test obligation, and no base requirement represents it.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction supports one obligation: the clause is a single test-setup step with one actor (the VUT), one action (approach in a straight line, then turn) and one constraint (50 per cent overlap), so it is not split. No base requirement R-001 to R-117 covers Annex 4 test setups for this scenario, and the old 4.2.5.2.13.1.1 has no corresponding R-ID, so existing_id is null. The text is a repeat of old wording, but the new multiple-target scope makes it a new obligation. No reversal or exclusion applies.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (multiple targets), the first target (the oncoming vehicle target) shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h.
obligations.reason: The clause sits in a newly introduced multi-target scenario (4.2.5.2.20) and sets a speed limit for the first target. Similar wording in 4.2.5.2.14.1.2 / R-series Annex 4 clauses applies to different scenarios, and the new clause has no declared-system-boundaries qualifier. It is therefore a separately scoped new obligation.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior extraction is supported. No base requirement R-001 to R-117 covers a test-target approach speed for a multi-target oncoming vehicle and cyclist test. The old 4.2.5.2.14.1.2 text, 'target shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h, depending on the declared system boundaries', is for the crossing vehicle scenario and is not an equivalent of this clause. The clause contains a single obligation, so there is nothing to split and no reversal or exclusion.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (multiple targets), the cyclist target shall approach at 20 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h from a maximum of 1 m from the road edge.
obligations.reason: New cyclist target speed, tolerance and start-position parameters for the multi-target turning scenario; no old clause has a cyclist target in this scenario.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (multiple targets), the cyclist target's positioning shall be coordinated with the moving target so that the cyclist target reaches the centreline of the road two seconds after the rear of the moving target passes the same virtual centreline.
obligations.reason: Separate timing-coordination obligation between the cyclist and the moving vehicle target; no old counterpart exists in any scenario.

clause_reviews.explanation: The clause contains two independent test-procedure obligations: the cyclist speed and start position, and the cyclist timing coordination. I kept both prior obligations. The old context has no cyclist target in a turning-across-oncoming-vehicle test. Similar old clauses cover pedestrian or bicycle crossing tests with different speeds, positioning and scope. So both are new and not modifications of existing requirements. No base requirement matches, and nothing was excluded or reversed.

obligations.text: In the Extended testing for the scenario in which the VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20), the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection.
obligations.reason: Identical wording exists under the separate scenario 4.2.5.2.13.2 (oncoming vehicle turn, no cyclist). The new clause sits under the new 4.2.5.2.20 scenario (oncoming vehicle and cyclist, multiple targets), so it is a separately applicable extended-test obligation. It is not a relocation of the old one, and the old 4.2.5.2.13.2 remains in the new text. No equivalent R-ID exists, because R-116 and R-117 are general control-strategy requirements in Appendix 4 of Annex 3 and not scenario-specific extended test procedures.

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior single obligation is retained as an addition. The clause is one extended-testing demonstration requirement with no bundled independent steps. Its scope is the new oncoming vehicle and cyclist scenario, so the repeated wording does not make it an existing obligation. No reversals or exclusions.

obligations.text: For the extended test in Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist; demonstrating that the system does not unreasonably change its control strategy for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection), the test shall be executed at least with different target vehicle types or categories.
obligations.reason: New scenario 4.2.5.2.20 (oncoming vehicle and cyclist). The same wording in the old 4.2.5.2.13.2.1(a) applies to a different scenario without a cyclist, so this is a separately scoped obligation.

obligations.text: For the extended test in Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the test shall be executed at least with different overlaps.
obligations.reason: Separately scoped test variation for the new oncoming vehicle and cyclist scenario. The old 'different overlaps' items belong to other scenarios (4.2.5.2.13 and 4.2.5.2.14).

obligations.text: For the extended test in Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the test shall be executed at least with different lane positions of the vehicles and target.
obligations.reason: Separately scoped test variation for the new scenario. The old lane-position items apply to other scenarios (4.2.5.2.13 and 4.2.5.2.14).

clause_reviews.explanation: The prior inventory is supported and complete: each of items (a)-(c) is a separate test variation. No bundled items were found. No base requirement (R-001 to R-117) covers these scenario-specific extended test variations, so existing_id is null and all three are additions. Nothing was reversed or excluded.

obligations.text: The simulation models and simulation tools used in the overall M&S toolchain should be investigated in terms of their impact in case of a safety error in the final product.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Annex 5 / 3.5.5.1 (same context under 3.5.5 Criticality assessment). No base requirement (R-...) represents it, because the base inventory contains no Annex 5 obligations.

obligations.text: To derive how critical the simulated data is, the criticality assessment should consider the following parameters: (a) the consequences on human safety, e.g. severity classes in ISO 26262; (b) the degree to which the M&S toolchain results influence the DCAS.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old Annex 5 / 3.5.5.1 (a)-(b); the only difference is the grammatical fix 'influence's' to 'influence'. No base requirement represents it.

clause_reviews.explanation: The new 3.5.5.1 is identical to the old one except for the grammatical correction 'influence's' to 'influence'. The ISO 26262 sentence is background explanation and imposes no obligation, so it is excluded. Both obligations are unchanged. No R-xxx base requirement covers Annex 5, so existing_id is null for both. They are kept as two separate obligations: the investigation duty and the criticality parameters.

old_reviews.reason: No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none needed resolving. Old 5.2.2 (p.7) and new 5.2.2 (p.8) are word for word identical: transitions between DCAS and other assistance or automation systems, prioritization, and suppression or deactivation of other assistance systems intended to ensure safe and nominal operation must be described in detail in the documentation presented to the Type Approval Authority. Only the page changed. The heading of 5.2 now adds 'and ADS', and the new 5.2.3 requires DCAS to switch to 'OFF' on ADS activation and to stay unable to switch to 'ON' while an ADS feature is active. The new 5.2.3 is a separate functional obligation and is not folded into R-011. It does not alter the documentation duty. The 'other automation systems' wording in 5.2.2 was already present, so the ADS heading change leaves the scope of R-011 as it was. The neighboring 5.2.1 is unchanged and still covers AEBS non-suppression, which is a different obligation. Annex 3 Appendix 2 2.3.4 (old p.46, new p.51) is identical and still points back to 5.2.2 as a documentation checklist item. Paragraphs 3.2.1 and 5.3.5.x are unchanged and are separate obligations. The retrieved corpus shows no deletion or weakening of 5.2.2, so the obligation is retained.

Old R-012 (UN R171 5.3.5.1, p.8) requires that, while DCAS or a DCAS feature is in 'on' mode, the system aims to detect the applicable system boundaries. The new 5.3.5.1 (p.9) opens with an identical first sentence: 'The system shall aim to detect the applicable system boundaries when DCAS or a feature of DCAS is in 'on' mode.' The obligation, trigger (on mode) and aim-level strength are the same. Only the later sentences changed: leaving 'active' mode instead of transitioning to 'stand-by', the driver-disengaged handling, the 10-second driver unavailability response and gradual termination. These are separate obligations (boundary-exceeded response, driver unavailability) and are not the detection duty in R-012, so they are not folded into this ID. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve (handoffs list is empty). The definitions of 'on mode' (2.15), 'stand-by' and 'active' (2.15.1, 2.15.2) are textually the same in the new context, apart from a minor wording tweak in 2.15.2.1 ('a DCAS feature'), so the dependencies do not change the meaning. Neighboring clauses 5.3.1 (detection capabilities documentation) and 5.3.5.1.1 are unchanged. The old context had 5.3.5.1 on p.8 and the new one has it on p.9, which is only a pagination shift. The evidence was a full review of the supplied old and new context; the requirement was matched by its identical wording, not by absence from the retrieved candidates.

old_reviews.new_text: If the system identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded while DCAS or a DCAS feature is in 'on' mode, the system or the applicable feature shall leave the 'active' mode, with the exception of the driver unavailability response, and shall immediately notify the driver in accordance with the manufacturer's strategies (paragraph 5.3.5.2) and the HMI requirements of paragraph 5.5.4.1.
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff (R-013, modified_existing) resolved as modified. The old 5.3.5.1 required the system to transition into 'stand-by' mode when a boundary was exceeded. The new 5.3.5.1 (page 9) requires the system or applicable feature to leave 'active' mode, with an exception for the driver unavailability response. This changes the target mode and adds the exception, so the old obligation is replaced rather than unchanged. Evidence: the new clause applies when DCAS or a feature is in 'on' mode, and the old text was a direct counterpart of the same sentence. Neighboring 5.3.5.1.1 and 5.5.3.3.3 still reference 'stand-by' transitions, but they are separate obligations and do not restore the old rule. The new clause's additional rules on disengaged-driver behaviour, the 10 s driver unavailability response and assistance termination are separate obligations. They are not folded into R-013; only the boundary-exceeded mode-exit obligation is carried here. The 'stand-by' wording is no longer mandated for this trigger, so the change is substantive.

old_reviews.new_text: If the DCAS identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded while DCAS or a DCAS feature is in 'on' mode, then the system or the applicable feature shall leave the 'active' mode, with the exception of the driver unavailability response, and shall immediately notify the driver in accordance with the strategies described by the manufacturer as outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2. and according to the HMI requirements defined in paragraph 5.5.4.1.
old_reviews.reason: No Track B handoffs were supplied, so there is nothing to resolve. The old requirement was the immediate driver notification when a boundary is exceeded, with references to 5.3.5.2 and 5.5.4.1. The new 5.3.5.1 (p.9) keeps this obligation and both references, so the obligation is not removed. The previous 'unchanged' decision is not fully accurate, because the trigger and condition wording changed. The old text had no 'leave active mode' wording. The new text says that the system or feature shall leave 'active' mode, except for the driver unavailability response, and then notify the driver. The old text in this ID did not include the mode transition, which was old 'transition into stand-by'. The new text changes the applicability of the notification, so the requirement is modified to carry the new exception wording. The newly added driver-disengaged continued assistance and the 10-second driver unavailability response are separate obligations and are not folded into R-014. The dependencies 5.3.5.2 and 5.5.4.1 are text-identical in the new context. 5.5.4.1.1(d) still has the boundary-reached notification. A full review of the retrieved context found no other clause that removes the notification.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. R-015 requires the DCAS, when it identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded, to terminate assistance from the affected feature or system in a controllable way. New 5.3.5.1 (p.9) keeps this obligation verbatim: 'The system shall terminate assistance to the driver provided by the affected feature or the system in a controllable way. The assistance termination strategy shall be described by the vehicle manufacturer and assessed according to Annex 3.' The sentence remains in the boundary-exceeded paragraph, so its trigger is unchanged. The new text changes the preceding mode-handling sentence. The system or feature must now leave 'active' mode, except for the driver unavailability response, instead of transitioning into 'stand-by'. It also adds driver-disengagement provisions: continued assistance or gradual controllable termination, continued monitoring of driver disengagement, and a driver unavailability response within 10 seconds. These are separate obligations (mode transition, notification, driver-disengaged handling, driver unavailability response). They do not replace or narrow the old termination duty, and I did not fold them into R-015. The disengaged-driver sentence mentions controllable termination as one option, but the general termination sentence is still present and applies. Neighboring clauses 5.3.5.1.1, 5.3.5.4, 5.3.5.5 and 5.3.6, plus the Annex 3 references, are textually the same apart from page shifts. The definitions of active and stand-by mode are also unchanged. No dependency change alters the old obligation, so it stays unchanged.

Old R-016 requires the manufacturer to describe the assistance termination strategy for when the DCAS identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded, and requires it to be assessed according to Annex 3. The new 5.3.5.1 (p.9) keeps the same sentence word for word: 'The assistance termination strategy shall be described by the vehicle manufacturer and assessed according to Annex 3.' The preceding sentence ('shall terminate assistance ... in a controllable way') is also kept. There are no handoffs to resolve. The new text adds separate obligations: leaving 'active' mode instead of going to 'stand-by', the driver-disengaged case with continued or gradual termination, and the 10-second driver unavailability response. These are different obligations. They do not change the manufacturer's description and Annex 3 assessment duty, so I did not fold them into R-016. Neighbouring clauses 5.3.5.1.1, 5.3.5.2.2, 5.3.5.3, 5.3.5.4 and 5.3.5.5 are unchanged in substance. Table 1 item 4.c in 7.2.3.1 is a reporting item and is also a different obligation. Annex 3 itself was not supplied, so I could not check it. The reference is unchanged and the lexical match is direct, so the obligation remains in force.

old_reviews.new_text: A manoeuvre shall only be initiated if the driver is not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start, and the driver: (a) has commanded the system to perform the manoeuvre for a driver-initiated manoeuvre; or (b) has acknowledged the system's intention as needed for a driver-confirmed manoeuvre; or (c) is given sufficient notice to react for a system-initiated manoeuvre. Motoric disengagement may not be considered when HORs are being withheld by the system.
old_reviews.reason: Handoff resolved as modified (modified_existing, R-021). The same obligation, paragraph 5.3.7.2.1.1, is in both versions (old p.10, new p.11), so it is not a new procedure and not removed. The old gate was 'driver is not detected to be disengaged'. The new text uses 'not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start'. That adds a 2-second time qualifier and a changed criterion with cross-references to the deeming rules. Conditions (a)-(c) by manoeuvre type are unchanged. The final sentence, that motoric disengagement may not be considered when HORs are withheld, is retained in the new clause, and the previous decision's new_text kept it as well. The handoff obligation text omitted this sentence, but the clause text includes it, so it is retained here as an applicability condition. Neighbouring clauses 5.3.7.2.1.2 (detection range) and 5.5.4.2.5.x (visual disengagement) are different obligations and are not substituted. 5.5.4.2.4 does not appear in the supplied new context. This is not evidence of removal, since the clause itself still cites it.

Old 5.3.7.2.3.1 (p.10) stated that the requirements in 5.5.4.1.8 and subparagraphs shall apply, in addition to a driver-confirmation-time obligation. New 5.3.7.2.3.1 (p.12) retains only the sentence that the system shall be designed to ensure the driver has sufficient time to confirm that the system may proceed with the manoeuvre. The explicit reference to 5.5.4.1.8 is deleted. The 5.3.7.2.3 chapeau (new p.12) only says that paragraph and its subparagraphs apply to features capable of driver-confirmed manoeuvres. It does not mention 5.5.4.1.8. The sibling 5.3.7.2.3.2 only requires a specific signal per 5.5.4.1, which is a different and broader reference and not an application of 5.5.4.1.8. 5.5.4.1.9.1 (new p.19) says 5.5.4.1.8 applies equally to system-initiated manoeuvres, which is a different context and a different obligation. Annex 3 Appendix 2 item 2.1.7 only requires documentation of timings and strategy, not application of 5.5.4.1.8. The 5.5.4.1.8 text itself is unchanged, and its heading is for driver-confirmed manoeuvres, but it is only a standalone clause and no longer cross-referenced from 5.3.7.2.3.1. No handoffs were supplied, so there were none to resolve. The retrieved candidates show no clause in the new version that carries the old obligation, so the requirement is removed. Any residual applicability of 5.5.4.1.8 rests on its own heading and not on this requirement.

Old R-024 (5.3.7.2.3.1, p.10) required the system to be designed so the driver has sufficient time to confirm that the system may proceed with the manoeuvre, as appropriate. New 5.3.7.2.3.1 (p.12) states the same obligation: 'The system shall be designed to ensure that the driver has sufficient time to confirm that the system may proceed with the manoeuvre, as appropriate.' It applies under the same condition, driver-confirmed manoeuvres per 5.3.7.2.3 (p.12). The only change is the deletion of the first sentence, which applied paragraph 5.5.4.1.8 and subparagraphs, and the 'In addition,' lead-in. R-024's text only covers the sufficient-time sentence, so dropping the cross-reference does not change it. The neighbouring clauses are unchanged: 5.3.7.2.3.2 to 5.3.7.2.3.4 (confirmation signal, no initiation without confirmation, justifiable reason) and the separate system-initiated clause 5.3.7.2.4.1 (time to reject), which is a different obligation and was not substituted. No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so none need resolving. The 5.5.4.1.8 reference text is not in the supplied new context, so any obligation there is outside R-024 and would need separate review. The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed.

Old R-025 (old 5.3.7.2.4.2, p.11) prohibited initiating a manoeuvre if the system had presented an EOR in the 7 seconds before initiation. No handoffs were supplied, so there is nothing further to resolve. In the new corpus, 5.3.7.2.4.2 (p.12) reads only 'The strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of the manoeuvre, which shall be documented and explained.' This corresponds to old 5.3.7.2.4.2.1, a separate documentation/strategy obligation, and it must not replace the old lockout. The neighbouring new clauses give no equivalent: 5.3.7.2.4.1 covers driver rejection of a manoeuvre, 5.3.7.2.4.3 covers justifiable reason, 5.3.7.2.4.9 covers the driver acknowledgement of information material, and 5.3.7.2.4.10 covers collision-mitigation manoeuvres. 5.5.4.2.6.3.1 (DCA within 5 seconds after EOR escalation) is a different obligation. Table 1 reporting (7.2.3.1) mentions EORs only for reporting. The 7-second EOR figure and any link between EOR presentation and blocking manoeuvre initiation do not appear in the supplied new context. This conclusion rests on that context covering the manoeuvre clauses and neighbouring HMI and reporting clauses, not on absence from retrieved candidates alone. The previous removal decision is confirmed.

old_reviews.new_text: For features capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of the manoeuvre, and these strategies shall be documented and explained.
old_reviews.reason: Handoff (R-026, modified_existing, new 5.3.7.2.4.2): resolved as modified. Old 5.3.7.2.4.2.1 required 'further strategies' in addition to the 7-second EOR lockout in old 5.3.7.2.4.2. New 5.3.7.2.4.2 (page 12) reads 'The strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of the manoeuvre, which shall be documented and explained.' The core obligation (driver engagement strategies before initiation, documented and explained) is retained, but the 'In addition, further' framing is dropped. Applicability is carried over from 5.3.7.2.4, which limits its subparagraphs to features capable of system-initiated manoeuvres (new context, page 12). The 7-second EOR lockout is not in the supplied new context. The retrieved new neighbouring clauses (5.3.7.2.1.1, 5.5.4.2.7.2, 5.5.4.2.8) address different obligations: a 2-second disengagement condition, additional driver-state monitoring, and disablement. These are not substituted for the old obligation. Absence of the lockout from the retrieved candidates is not proof of its removal, and I do not rely on it. The old ID R-026 concerned only the further-strategies obligation, so it remains and is modified rather than removed. The 'documented and explained' element is made explicit in new_text because the old clause had it and the new clause keeps it.

old_reviews.new_text: The strategies implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of a manoeuvre shall be documented and explained. This applies to features capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres.
old_reviews.reason: The previous 'unchanged' decision is revised. The documentation and explanation obligation is retained in new 5.3.7.2.4.2 (page 12, within 5.3.7.2.4, which applies to system-initiated manoeuvres). However, the old text was framed as 'further' strategies, 'in addition' to the 7-second EOR (emergency-or-override request) prohibition in old 5.3.7.2.4.2. The new 5.3.7.2.4.2 no longer contains that prohibition and no longer says 'further'. Neighbouring clauses 5.3.7.2.4.1 and 5.3.7.2.4.3 do not restate it. The new text therefore refers to 'the strategies', with no stated baseline, and the new paragraph states the obligation on its own. The documentation obligation itself is not lost, so this is not a removal, and the 7-second rule is a separate obligation that is not folded into R-027. No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so none need resolving. The lexical search of the supplied new context found no replacement for the 7-second EOR rule. That absence only covers the retrieved excerpts, so I do not treat it as proof of removal for any other requirement. The related new clause Annex 3 Appendix 2 5.1.3 (driver engagement influencing manoeuvre execution) is a different obligation and is not substituted for R-027.

old_reviews.new_text: The manufacturer shall describe in the safety concept the system behaviour in case the driver is detected to be disengaged during a manoeuvre (e.g., aborting the manoeuvre, fully executing a manoeuvre, bringing the vehicle to a safe stop). This applies to all manoeuvres covered by the General Requirements for manoeuvres, not only system-initiated ones.
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff resolved as modified (modified_existing, R-028). The supplied clause 5.3.7.2.1.13 (page 11) restates the old 5.3.7.2.4.3 duty almost verbatim: describe in the safety concept the system behaviour when the driver is detected disengaged during a manoeuvre. The clause sits under 5.3.7.2.1 General Requirements, so its scope is wider than the old duty, which sat under 5.3.7.2.4 (system-initiated manoeuvres). The word 'also' is dropped. The examples change from risk mitigation function, full execution and stop the vehicle to aborting, fully executing and safe stop. The duty is the same and is not replaced by a different obligation, so it is modified, not removed. The new 5.3.7.2.4.x numbering contains no counterpart, which is consistent with relocation. Related provisions are different obligations and do not substitute for R-028: 5.3.5.1 covers disengagement beyond a system boundary, 5.5.3.4.1.5 and 5.3.6.2 cover controllability. The new_text preserves the carried-over duty and adds the wider applicability.

Old R-029 (UN R171, 5.3.7.2.4.4, p.11) requires that a manoeuvre is only performed if there is a justifiable reason, with examples: pursuing a set destination, following traffic flow, safety-relevant manoeuvres. The new text at 5.3.7.2.4.3 (p.13) contains the same obligation with the same examples, inside the same 5.3.7.2.4 section (general requirements for system-initiated manoeuvres). Only the paragraph number and page changed. The extra sentence on documenting traffic situations is in both versions, so it is not a change. The neighbouring clauses 5.3.7.2.3.4 (a manoeuvre is only proposed if there is a justifiable reason) and 5.3.7.2.4.5 (do not initiate if it would cause unreasonable deceleration of other road users) are different obligations and do not replace or alter R-029. Their presence or absence does not affect this requirement. No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so there is nothing further to resolve. The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed.

Old R-030 (UN R171 5.3.7.2.4.4, page 11) requires the manufacturer to explain in the documentation the traffic situations where the system may initiate manoeuvres. The new context contains the same obligation in 5.3.7.2.4.3 (page 13): 'A manoeuvre shall only be performed if there is a justifiable reason... The manufacturer shall explain in the documentation the traffic situations where the system may initiate manoeuvres.' The sentence is identical and the applicability is unchanged, since it sits under 5.3.7.2.4, which applies to features capable of system-initiated manoeuvres. Only the paragraph number and page changed, because new 5.3.7.2.4.2 was inserted. There were no Track B handoffs to resolve (handoffs list is empty). The neighbouring new clauses are different obligations and were not substituted: 5.3.7.2.4.2 (driver engagement strategies documented), 5.3.7.2.4.5 (not initiating manoeuvres that cause unreasonable deceleration or evasion by other road users), and Annex 3 Appendix 2 5.1.3 (explaining how situation understanding and driver engagement influence manoeuvre execution). None of them replaces or removes the traffic-situation documentation duty. The obligation is retained, so it is unchanged with null new_text and source fields.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The old R-031 (old 5.3.7.2.4.5, page 11) says the system shall not initiate the manoeuvre if the conditions in 5.3.7.2.3.5 are not met. The new version has the identical sentence at 5.3.7.2.4.4 (page 13), so only the paragraph number changed. The referenced 5.3.7.2.3.5 is now on page 12. Conditions (a)-(f) are word-for-word the same as in the old text: target area clear, reason still exists, stable control after the manoeuvre, completion before standstill, target within system boundaries, driver gaze. The scope is unchanged, since 5.3.7.2.4 still applies to features capable of system-initiated manoeuvres. The neighbouring clauses changed but do not alter this obligation. Old 5.3.7.2.4.4 (justifiable reason) is now 5.3.7.2.4.3. The old 5.3.7.2.4.6 to 5.3.7.2.4.8 clauses (road-user deceleration, signage, lane markings) are renumbered 5.3.7.2.4.5 to 5.3.7.2.4.7. Old 5.3.7.2.4.9 (right-of-way) is now 5.3.7.2.4.8. Old 5.3.7.2.4.10 (highway only) is not among the retrieved new paragraphs, but it is a different obligation and does not affect R-031. The new 5.3.7.2.4.9 (driver acknowledgement of information material) is a separate, newly introduced procedure and is not folded into R-031. The old 5.3.7.2.3.1 text no longer references 5.5.4.1.8, but that concerns driver-confirmed manoeuvres and not this requirement. The old requirement remains in force with no substantive change.

Old R-032 (5.3.7.2.4.6, page 12) requires that the system aim not to initiate a manoeuvre if it would cause other road users to unreasonably or unmanageably decelerate or evade the vehicle. In the new text this clause is 5.3.7.2.4.5 on page 13, with identical wording: same 'shall aim to not initiate' strength, same trigger (unreasonable or unmanageable deceleration or evasion by other road users as a consequence of the manoeuvre), and same scope (system-initiated manoeuvres under 5.3.7.2.4). Only the paragraph number and page changed. Neighbouring clauses were checked and none replaces or alters it. 5.3.7.2.3.6 is a separate obligation: a firm 'shall not propose' with a 'knowingly' qualifier, applying to driver-initiated manoeuvres. 5.3.7.2.4.4 (formerly 5.3.7.2.4.5) is the conditions check against 5.3.7.2.3.5. 6.2.4 and 6.2.4.1 are lane-change-specific and unchanged in substance, and a new sentence in 6.2.4.1 about speeds up to 60 km/h applies only to the approaching-vehicle assessment, not to this general obligation. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve. The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed, and new_text and the source fields are null.

Old R-033 (5.3.7.2.4.7, p.12): system shall aim to not initiate a manoeuvre if it would violate applicable signage instruction or performance requirements in paragraph 6. New context 5.3.7.2.4.6 (p.13) has identical wording, including 'shall aim to', 'initiate', and the paragraph 6 reference; only the number shifted from .7 to .6 because old 5.3.7.2.4.4 (justifiable reason/documentation) is absent in the supplied new context. That removal does not alter this obligation. Neighbouring new clauses are different obligations: 5.3.7.2.4.7 (shall not cross prohibited lane markings), 5.3.7.2.4.5 (road users' deceleration) and 6.3.9.4 (solid lane markings); none was substituted for R-033. The 5.3.7.2.3.7 proposal-stage clause is a separate obligation and still present. No handoffs were supplied, so none to resolve. The unchanged decision rests on the identical text found, not on absence from retrieved candidates. Paragraph 6 itself was not supplied in either version, so only the reference was compared, and it is unchanged. Hence unchanged, with null new_text and source fields.

Old R-034 (UN R171 5.3.7.2.4.8, page 12) says the system shall not initiate a manoeuvre if it would lead the vehicle to cross lane markings that are not permitted to be crossed. The new text at 5.3.7.2.4.7 (page 13) is word-for-word identical, so the obligation, strength ("shall not") and conditions are the same. Only the paragraph number and page changed, because new 5.3.7.2.4.4 through 5.3.7.2.4.9 are renumbered; the old 5.3.7.2.4.7 and 5.3.7.2.4.8 were a signage clause and the lane-marking clause, and the old 5.3.7.2.4.9 is now 5.3.7.2.4.8. Neighbouring clauses are unchanged in substance: the signage clause (new 5.3.7.2.4.6) still uses "aim to" language, and the right-of-way clause is also unchanged. The new 5.3.7.2.3.8 (page 12) applies to proposing a manoeuvre, which is a separate obligation, and it does not replace the initiation clause. Related clause 6.3.9.4 (page 29) is also textually unchanged; it covers suggesting or performing a manoeuvre across a solid marking, with an exception for 6.3.9.1(c). It is a related but different obligation, so it was not substituted for R-034. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve (the handoff list is empty). The old and new contexts contain no removal, so the requirement stays. A paragraph renumbering is not a substantive change and does not require modification. Since the decision is unchanged, new_text and the source fields are null.

The old obligation (old 5.3.7.2.4.9, page 12) is that the system shall aim not to violate appropriate right-of-way rules applicable in the country of operation where relevant to the manoeuvre. In the new corpus, 5.3.7.2.4.8 (page 13) has identical wording, so the obligation, 'aim' strength, country-of-operation scope and manoeuvre-relevance condition are all preserved. Only the paragraph number moved, because old 5.3.7.2.4.2/4.2.1 were removed and the numbering shifted. The new 5.3.7.2.4.9 (page 13) is a different obligation about driver acknowledgement of driver information material, so it must not be substituted for R-035. Neighboring clauses show the same renumbering: old 4.6/4.7/4.8 became new 4.5/4.6/4.7 with unchanged text. Related clauses 6.3.8 (aim to respect right-of-way rules), 6.3.3 and the Annex 4 right-of-way test text are unchanged or are separate obligations and do not alter R-035. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve (handoffs list is empty). The previous unchanged decision is confirmed, and new_text and the source fields stay null.

Old R-036 (5.3.7.2.4.10) restricted initiating a manoeuvre to when the vehicle is on a highway (including slip roads) and the system is not withholding HORs. The supplied new context has no counterpart. New 5.3.7.2.4.10 is a different obligation: a system-initiated manoeuvre may be initiated, notwithstanding 5.3.7.2.1.1, to mitigate an imminent collision, followed by a DCA and disabling per 5.5.4.2.8. It does not carry the old road-type/HOR gate and must not be substituted for it. Neighbouring clauses 5.3.7.2.4.1, .4, .5, .6 and .9 cover driver rejection, conditions, other road users, signage and the acknowledgement request. 5.3.7.2.1.1 only keeps the driver-disengagement and motoric-disengagement conditions. None restates a highway or highway-slip-road restriction or a not-withholding-HORs condition on manoeuvre initiation. Annex 1 items 6.4 and 6.4.1 only declare whether the system can withhold HORs, and on highway-like roads. They are declarations, not manoeuvre-initiation restrictions. The previous decision's 5.5.4.2.6.5 text and the 'highway-like road' wording were not found in the supplied new context. 5.5.4.2.6.5 would govern withholding HORs, which is a different obligation from restricting manoeuvre initiation, so it cannot support a modification. The previous 'modified' text added highway-like roads and a speed limit that the old text did not contain, so it is unsupported. Retrieval is limited to the supplied excerpts, so absence is not proof of removal in the full regulation, but nothing supplied supports a replacement obligation. No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so none need resolving. Decision: removed.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none needed resolving. Old 5.3.7.2.4.11 (page 12) says the acknowledgement request is given while the vehicle is in a stopped position. New 5.3.7.2.4.9 (page 13) carries the same obligation in the same wording: a request to acknowledge reading and understanding the driver information material in paragraph 5.6, given while stopped. Only the paragraph number changed. The only wording difference is '3 months' replacing 'three months' in the user-differentiation extension, which does not affect this obligation. The new 5.3.7.2.4.11 (page 13) is a different obligation, covering the description and justification of collision-mitigation manoeuvres. It was not substituted for the old one. The new 5.3.7.2.4.10 is also a different obligation. The 5.6 dependency has the same list of information aspects (a)-(j) and the same non-misleading clause in old and new text. The only difference is page layout, so no review-triggering change exists. The related 5.5.4.2.8.4 did change, but it is a separate obligation about re-enabling the system after disablement, not this requirement. The requirement is therefore unchanged apart from the renumbering.

Old 5.3.7.2.4.11 required a request to acknowledge the driver information material in paragraph 5.6 at least once every month, extendable to three months per user if the vehicle differentiates between users. New 5.3.7.2.4.9 (page 13) has the same obligation: stopped-position request, at least monthly, extendable to '3 months' for a given user where users are differentiated, with the same rules on prior acknowledgement and new drivers. The only change is 'three months' becoming '3 months', which is formatting. New 5.3.7.2.4.11 is a different, unrelated provision on collision-mitigation manoeuvres. It is not a substitute and must not be conflated with this requirement. The old paragraph 5.6 content and the new 5.6 content (a)-(j) are textually identical, so the referenced material is unchanged. No handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The renumbering from 5.3.7.2.4.11 to 5.3.7.2.4.9 was confirmed by explicit text match in the new corpus, not by absence from retrieved candidates. The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed.

Old R-039 (5.3.7.2.4.11) required a request to acknowledge the paragraph 5.6 driver information material at least monthly, except that it need not be repeated for a driver the vehicle can identify as having already acknowledged it. New 5.3.7.2.4.9 (page 13) keeps this obligation: the request is given at least once every month, and if the vehicle can identify that a driver has previously acknowledged it, it need not be given again for that driver. The only differences are the paragraph number (5.3.7.2.4.11 to 5.3.7.2.4.9) and the writing of '3 months' instead of 'three months'. The new text still contains the stopped-position condition, the 3-month extension for differentiated users and the current-drive-cycle rule for unacknowledged drivers, all of which were already in the old paragraph. The new 5.3.7.2.4.11 now covers a different obligation (describing and justifying imminent-collision manoeuvres to the Type Approval Authority) and must not be substituted for R-039. The 5.6 content list is also unchanged apart from pagination. No Track B handoffs were supplied, so there is none to resolve. The old paragraph's content is present in the new text, so the earlier decision of unchanged stands.

The old R-040 obligation is in old 5.3.7.2.4.11: if the vehicle can identify that the current driver has not previously acknowledged the request to acknowledge reading and understanding the driver information material in paragraph 5.6, the request shall be given in the current drive cycle. The new text carries this over in 5.3.7.2.4.9 (page 13) with the same substance. It keeps the same trigger (the vehicle can identify that the current driver has not acknowledged before) and the same obligation (give the request in the current drive cycle). The surrounding clauses are also the same: the request is given while stopped, at least monthly, extendable to 3 months per user where users are differentiated, and not repeated for a driver who has already acknowledged. The only difference is "three months" becoming "3 months", which is editorial. The paragraph number changed from 5.3.7.2.4.11 to 5.3.7.2.4.9. The new 5.3.7.2.4.11 is a different obligation about describing and justifying imminent-collision manoeuvres to the Type Approval Authority. The new 5.3.7.2.4.10 concerns imminent-collision manoeuvres, and the old 5.3.7.2.4.10 on highway and HOR conditions has no counterpart in the new text. Neither affects this requirement. Paragraph 5.6, the referenced driver information material, still exists in the new text with the same content. The related new 5.5.4.2.8.4 (re-enabling after insufficient engagement) and Annex 3 3.4.5 (information strategy) are different obligations and do not replace it. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve. Retrieval found the carried-over clause directly, so the decision does not rest on absence from candidates. The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed. The source fields are null because the decision is unchanged.

old_reviews.new_text: For highway or highway-like road operation, the system shall aim to respond to work zones, lane reductions, lane closures, toll stations and end of highways (e.g., by notifying the driver, issuing a DCA, or continuing operation if capable).
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff (existing_id R-041, disposition modified_existing) resolved as modified. Evidence: old 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 (page 12) read 'For highway operation, the system shall aim to respond to work zones, lane reductions, lane closures, toll stations and end of highways (e.g., ...)'. New 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 (page 13) reads 'For highway or highway-like road operation, ...' with the same actor, 'aim to respond' action, listed situations and example responses. The only change is the wider applicability condition, so this is the same obligation with a changed scope and not a new one. Neighboring clauses checked: new 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 (non-highway operation, system-initiated manoeuvres) is a different obligation and was not substituted. New 5.3.7.2.5.3.3 (lane marking recognition) is separate. New 5.5.4.2.6.5 (HOR withholding on highway-like roads, HOR timing at end of a highway-like road) covers a different obligation and does not replace or remove R-041. Dependency or neighbor changes elsewhere, such as 5.3.5.1 on system boundary response, do not alter R-041 and need no change. The previous modified decision is confirmed. Because the new clause is present verbatim in the supplied new context, the decision rests on direct evidence and not on absence from retrieval results.

The old requirement (old 5.3.7.2.5.3, page 13, a duplicate-numbered line that follows 5.3.7.2.5.3.2) says the system shall recognize lane markings as outlined in Annex 3 of the 01 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 130, as relevant to the countries in which the system can be activated. New 5.3.7.2.5.3.3 (page 14) has the same obligation word for word: the same R130 Annex 3 reference, the same 01-or-later series condition and the same country-of-activation condition. The clause was renumbered from the duplicate-numbered 5.3.7.2.5.3 to 5.3.7.2.5.3.3 and still sits under 5.3.7.2.5.3 (special provisions regarding system boundaries). Neighboring clauses: new 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 now covers 'highway or highway-like road operation', and 5.3.7.3.1 has been reworded. Neither changes the lane-marking recognition obligation or its applicability. 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 is unchanged. The new 5.3.7.2.6 is a separate heading for non-highway or HOR-withholding systems and has no lane-marking text in the retrieved context, so it neither replaces nor narrows R-042. No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none needed resolving. The R130 reference in 5.3.7.1.4 concerns LDWS fulfilment of the warning requirement for M2, M3, N2 and N3 vehicles. It is a different obligation and was not used as a substitute. The retrieved context contains no removal or modification of R-042, so the prior decision of unchanged is confirmed. A new source is not cited because the decision is unchanged.

old_reviews.new_text: The system's driver unavailability response shall comply with the technical requirements and transitional provisions of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79 with respect to the Risk Mitigation Function (RMF).
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff resolved as modified. The old R-043 required that 'the system' comply with the R79 04 series RMF requirements and transitional provisions. Supplied new paragraph 5.3.7.3.1 (page 14) still carries the same obligation and the same R79 04 or later series reference.
