However, its subject is now 'The system's driver unavailability response', which narrows what must comply. The handoff text matches the clause text. The clause's second sentence (safe stop in accordance with RMF requirements after driver unavailability following the 5.5.4.2.6 escalation sequence) restates the trigger and is a related obligation that is not added to this ID. Neighboring clauses 5.3.7.3.2, 5.3.7.3.3 and 5.3.7.3.4 are separate obligations (target stop area selection, lane-change capability, system-initiated manoeuvres) and are not folded into R-043. The corpus evidence is limited to the supplied new_context: the paragraph is present with the same number in the new text, so the requirement is not removed, and the wording change means it is not unchanged. The previous decision is confirmed.

old_reviews.new_text: In the event that the driver has been determined to be unavailable following a driver disengagement warning escalation sequence as defined in paragraph 5.5.4.2.6., the system shall come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements.
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff (R-044, modified_existing, 5.3.7.3.1, p.14): resolved as modified. The supplied new clause 5.3.7.3.1 (p.14) keeps the same trigger: the driver determined unavailable following the 5.5.4.2.6 warning escalation sequence. The obligation changes from 'appropriately activate the Risk Mitigation Function in order to come to a safe stop' to 'come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements'. The clause now also says the system's driver unavailability response shall comply with UN R79 04 series RMF requirements. That sentence only continues the existing compliance wording, which is not part of the old R-044 text, so I did not fold it in. Neighbouring clauses were checked and do not replace this obligation. 5.3.7.3.2 (target stop area) is unchanged and is a different obligation. 5.3.7.3.3 (lane changes during the response) and 5.3.7.3.4 (system-initiated manoeuvre) are newly introduced separate procedures, so they stay outside R-044. 5.5.4.2.6.4.1 (initiate the response within 10 s) and 5.3.5.1 (response within 10 s beyond a boundary) are timing or trigger obligations, not the stopping obligation. The old clause is still present in a revised form, so this is a modification, not a removal.

old_reviews.new_text: Where the system is equipped with a driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane change feature, the system shall be capable of performing lane changes during the driver unavailability response, in compliance with the technical requirements for RMF capable of bringing the vehicle to a safe stop outside its own lane of travel of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79, during an intervention on a highway to bring the vehicle towards a target stop area in a slower or emergency lane.
old_reviews.reason: Handoff resolved as modified_existing: new 5.3.7.3.3 (page 14) is the direct successor of old 5.3.7.3.3 (R-045). Same paragraph number, same trigger (driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane change feature fitted), same highway scope, same target (slower or emergency lane) and same UN R79 04 series reference. Changes: the actor is now 'the system' rather than 'the RMF'; the capability is expressly limited to 'during the driver unavailability response'; and the R79 wording changes from 'systems with the purpose of' to 'RMF capable of'. Neighbouring clauses 5.3.7.3.1 (RMF compliance), 5.3.7.3.2 (target stop area) and the new 5.3.7.3.4 (system-initiated manoeuvre) are separate obligations and do not replace the lane-change capability; they are not folded into R-045. The prior modified decision is confirmed; the text matches the new clause, so this is not a removal or a new obligation.

No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so there is nothing to resolve. The old requirement R-050 (old 5.4.2.1, p.14) says that if a failure affects the entire system, the system switches to 'off' mode upon termination of assistance. New 5.4.2.1 (p.16) has identical wording on the same obligation, with the same condition (failure affecting the entire system) and the same consequence (switch to 'off' mode upon termination of assistance). Only the page numbers changed. The neighboring clauses are also textually identical between old and new: 5.4.2 (terminate assistance safely, gradually reduce, inform the driver), 5.4.2.2 (optical indication unless in 'off' mode), 5.4.1, 5.4.3, 5.4.4 and 5.4.5. The related deactivation clauses 5.5.3.3.1 to 5.5.3.3.3 and the Annex 3 definitions of failure and fault (2.12 to 2.14) are unchanged, only repaginated. The only difference found is the pagination shift, so no dependency change requires modification. The new text does not add or remove any applicability condition or obligation. The obligation is still present in the new corpus, so the unchanged decision rests on direct textual evidence and not on absence from retrieval. The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The old R-051 obligation (UN R171 5.4.2.1, p.14) requires that, if a failure affects the entire system, at least an optical failure warning signal is provided to the driver for an appropriate duration. New 5.4.2.1 (p.16) is word-for-word identical: 'If a failure affects the entire system, the system shall switch to off mode upon termination of assistance and provide at least an optical failure warning signal to the driver for an appropriate duration.' The old requirement's condition (failure affecting the entire system), actor (system), signal (at least optical failure warning) and duration (appropriate) all remain. The only difference is the page number (14 to 16), which reflects pagination, not substance. Neighboring clauses are also unchanged. 5.4.2 and 5.4.1 are identical in old and new. 5.4.2.2 (optical signal for a failure unless the system is in off mode) is a separate obligation and is not substituted for R-051. 5.3.7.4.7.1 (optical signal when speed exceeds the limit) is unrelated and also unchanged. The 'off' mode switching wording is part of the same sentence in the old 5.4.2.1 and was already in scope. The dependency on 5.5.4.1 referenced in 5.4.2 is not itself a changed obligation. No retrieved candidate shows a removal, split or relocation. The evidence covers the full 5.4 section in both versions, so the obligation is retained as-is.

Old 5.4.4.2 (p.15) and new 5.4.4.2 (p.16) are word-for-word identical: if the system can provide continued assistance after a failure disabling a given feature, the manufacturer shall describe which features can operate independently of one another, assessed according to Annex 3. The obligation, its condition and its scope are unchanged; only the page number shifted. Neighbouring clauses 5.4.4 and 5.4.4.1 and the sibling clauses 5.4.1 to 5.4.3 and 5.4.5 are also textually identical, so no neighbouring change alters this duty. The explicit Annex 3 reference points to Appendix 2 item 2.3.7 (outline of continued assistance after a feature failure, citing paragraph 5.4.4), which is identical in old (p.47) and new (p.51) apart from a trailing full stop. Annex 3 clauses 3.2.3, 3.2.4 and 3.3 are likewise identical. The only substantive new text in the retrieved context is the added 6.2.4.1 paragraph on lane changes at speeds up to 60 km/h, which concerns a different obligation and does not touch R-052. There were no Track B handoffs to resolve (handoffs list is empty). The retrieved candidates show no removal or modification, and the identical old and new clause text supports unchanged.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so there is nothing further to resolve. Old 5.4.4.2 (p.15) and new 5.4.4.2 (p.16) are textually identical. Both say that if the system can provide continued assistance after a failure disables a given feature, the manufacturer shall describe which features can operate independently, and that this shall be assessed according to Annex 3. The explicit Annex 3 reference is unchanged. Annex 3 Appendix 2 para 2.3.7, which outlines continued assistance after a feature failure and cites 5.4.4, is unchanged apart from added punctuation and new pagination (p.47 to p.51). The neighbouring clauses 5.4.4 and 5.4.4.1 and the rest of 5.4 (5.4.1 to 5.4.5) are identical except for the page shift. Annexes 3.2.x and 8.1 are also unchanged. New 7.2.3.1 adds reporting items and new 5.3.7.2.5.3.x adds non-highway provisions, but neither alters or replaces this obligation, and no separate procedure was folded into R-053. The retrieved context shows no removal or modification, so the old obligation continues unchanged.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. Old 5.5.2.3 (p.15) and new 5.5.2.3 (p.17) read identically: while the system is in 'active' mode, no system other than DCAS may provide sustained longitudinal and lateral control assistance, unless an emergency safety system intervention is deemed necessary as specified in paragraph 5. 2. The only dependency change is the title of the referenced paragraph 5.2, which now reads 'DCAS interaction with other vehicle assistance systems and ADS'. I reviewed it as a dependency change and did not modify the requirement automatically. New 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 are word-for-word identical to the old text, apart from page shifts. The emergency-system exception and the AEBS non-suppression rule are therefore unchanged. The added 'and ADS' is a title-level scope label. It adds no new obligation and does not alter the prohibition on other systems providing sustained control. Neighbouring clauses 5.5.2.1, 5.5.2.2 and 5.5.2.4 and the mode definitions 2.15 to 2.15.2 are also unchanged. The retrieved candidates show no removal or relocation, and the clause is present in the new corpus with the same obligation. The old requirement's mode, other-system prohibition and emergency exception conditions all remain.

No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so none needed resolving. Old 5.5.4.1.1(a) (p.17) requires the system to inform or warn the driver about the status of the system or feature: 'stand-by' mode (if applicable), 'active' mode. New 5.5.4.1.1(a) (p.19) is word-for-word identical, with the same lead-in 'The system shall inform or warn the driver about:' and no new applicability conditions. Neighboring clauses are consistent. The mode definitions 2.14, 2.15 and 2.15.1 and the mode clauses 5.5.2.1 and 5.5.3.3.3 are unchanged, so the stand-by and active states keep their meaning. Items (b) to (g) are unchanged. New items (h), disabling due to insufficient engagement, and (i), the basis for a DCA, are separate obligations about different information and do not alter the status-indication duty. They must not be folded into R-057. The shift in page numbers (p.17 to p.19) is only pagination. Other changes in the new text, such as 5.5.4.1.9.2 and the new 5.5.4.1.9.4, concern manoeuvre notice timing and visualization, not mode status. The obligation is retained as is, so new_text and source fields are null.

Old 5.5.4.1.1(b) (p.17) requires the system to inform or warn the driver about the status of an ongoing manoeuvre (e.g., initiation, cancellation, or recommencement after the vehicle is forced to stop). New 5.5.4.1.1(b) (p.19) has identical wording, with the same lead-in 'The system shall inform or warn the driver about:'. Items (h) and (i) are newly added, separate obligations (insufficient engagement basis, DCA basis). They do not alter (b) and are not folded into R-058. Neighbouring clause 5.5.4.1.2 (unambiguous, timely messages) is unchanged. Related clause 5.3.7.2.1.9 (visual warning if the vehicle is unexpectedly forced to stationary during a planned manoeuvre) is textually identical in old and new, so it gives no reason to modify R-058. 5.3.7.2.1.1 changed (a 2-second driver disengagement condition was added), but it governs manoeuvre initiation conditions, not driver information about manoeuvre status, so this dependency change does not require modifying R-058. No handoffs were supplied to resolve. The obligation remains present in the new text, so no removal is warranted.

No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so there is nothing further to resolve. The old obligation in 5.5.4.1.1(c) (p.17) is that the system informs or warns the driver of the need for the driver to perform a specific action (e.g. apply control, check indirect vision devices). The new text in 5.5.4.1.1(c) (p.19) is word for word identical, with the same lead-in 'The system shall inform or warn the driver about:' and no added conditions or exceptions. The new items (h) (basis for disablement due to insufficient engagement) and (i) (basis for why a DCA was issued) are separate information obligations. They are not a change to (c), so they are not folded into R-059. The neighbouring clause 5.5.4.1.2 (messages unambiguous, timely, not confusing) is identical in both versions. Clauses 5.3.5.5, 5.4.5 and 5.5.4.2.6.5.1/2 are also identical in text, and they are separate obligations whose page shifts do not change R-059. No other retrieved clause replaces or removes the driver-action notification obligation. The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed.

Old R-060 is item (d) of 5.5.4.1.1 (p.17): when in 'active' mode the system has detected it reached a currently relevant system boundary, it shall inform or warn the driver, unless already indicated by (a) (system/feature status). New 5.5.4.1.1 (p.19) contains item (d) with identical wording, including the 'unless already indicated by (a)' exception, and item (a) is also unchanged. No handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. Neighboring clauses are unchanged in substance: 5.5.4.1.2 (unambiguous, timely messages), 5.3.5.5 (approaching a boundary, lead time, only repagined to p.9), and the definition of 'active mode' in 2.15.1. The new items (h) (basis for disablement due to insufficient engagement) and (i) (basis for a DCA) are separate obligations and do not alter or replace the boundary-reached obligation. The new 5.5.4.2.8.3/5.5.4.2.8.4 and 5.6 concern insufficient engagement and driver information materials, which are different obligations. The page and numbering shifts reflect repagination only. The obligation, its trigger and its exception are all unchanged.

Old 5.5.4.1.1 (p.17) item (e) 'A detected upcoming system boundary' is retained verbatim in new 5.5.4.1.1 (p.19) under the same lead-in 'The system shall inform or warn the driver about'. The obligation is identical in scope and condition: detected upcoming boundary leads to driver information or warning. New items (h) (basis for disablement due to insufficient engagement) and (i) (basis for a DCA being issued) are separate, different obligations and are not folded into R-061. Neighboring clauses are also unchanged: 5.3.5.5 (inform driver on approaching boundary of active feature with sufficient lead time), 5.5.4.1.2 (messages unambiguous and timely) and 5.5.4.2.6.5.1 (HOR at latest 5 s before boundary). They differ in page numbers only, so there is no dependency change requiring modification. There are no Track B handoffs (handoffs list is empty), so none needed resolving. Retrieval of the new text shows direct evidence of retention, so this is not an inference from absence.

No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so none need resolving. The old obligation is 5.5.4.1.1 item (f): if the system is not in 'off' mode, it informs or warns the driver about detected failures affecting the system or its features. In the new text, 5.5.4.1.1(f) (p.19) reads identically: 'Detected failures affecting the system or its features, unless the system is in 'off' mode', under the unchanged lead-in 'The system shall inform or warn the driver about'. Applicability condition (not in 'off' mode) and scope (system or its features) are unchanged. New items (h) (basis for disabling due to insufficient engagement) and (i) (basis for a DCA) are separately introduced obligations and do not alter (f). Neighbouring clauses are also unchanged in substance, only renumbered by page: 5.4.2.2 (optical failure signal unless off), 5.4.2.1, 5.4.5 and 5.5.4.1.2. The change to 5.5.4.1.9.2 concerns manoeuvre notice timing, not failure information. The 5.2 heading now mentions ADS, which does not affect this obligation. The requirement persists, so removal is not supported.

Old R-063 derives from item (g) of 5.5.4.1.1 (old p.17): the system shall inform or warn the driver about intended driver-confirmed or system-initiated manoeuvres. The new corpus carries 5.5.4.1.1 (now p.19) with the same lead-in 'The system shall inform or warn the driver about:' and item (g) 'Intended driver-confirmed or system-initiated manoeuvres;' verbatim, with no added conditions, so scope and applicability are unchanged. The only changes to the clause are new items (h) (basis for disabling due to insufficient engagement) and (i) (basis for a DCA), which are separate obligations and do not alter (g) or fold into R-063. Neighbouring clauses were checked and none replaces the old obligation. The new 5.5.4.1.9.2 adds a 3-second visual notice and an evidence rule, and new 5.5.4.1.9.4 adds an intended-manoeuvre visualisation. Both are separate timing or visualisation procedures. 5.5.4.1.9.3 is unchanged. These are related but different obligations and should not be substituted for R-063. Annex 4 test clauses 4.2.5.1.3 and 4.3.3 are unchanged in text, and the Annex 3 Appendix 2 controllability evidence is separate. No handoffs were supplied, so there are none to resolve. The page shift (17 to 19) is only a relocation. The evidence is the verbatim retention of (g) in new 5.5.4.1.1, so unchanged is correct.

old_reviews.new_text: The system shall aim to provide the visual information at least 3 seconds ahead of the initiation of a relevant intended manoeuvre, or with sufficient notice to allow the driver to comprehend the manoeuvre and the traffic situation, taking into account the complexity of the manoeuvre and the amount of other road users present. If there is a risk of imminent collision or the information would conflict with information about an ongoing manoeuvre, the time may be reduced and the system shall visually inform the driver as far in advance as possible. Where the notice is less than 3 seconds ahead of initiation, the manufacturer shall provide evidence to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that the timing ensures an appropriate driver response and that the strategies employed ensure the driver notices the information without undue delay.
old_reviews.reason: Handoff (modified_existing, R-064, 5.5.4.1.9.2) resolved as modified. Evidence: old 5.5.4.1.9.2 (p.18) required information ahead of a relevant intended manoeuvre with sufficient notice. New 5.5.4.1.9.2 (p.20) is the same paragraph and obligation, now specifying the information as visual and adding an 'at least 3 seconds ahead' target as an alternative to sufficient notice. It adds a condition: where notice is under 3 seconds, the manufacturer must give the Type Approval Authority evidence of appropriate driver response and timely noticing. The reduced-time exception for imminent collision or conflict with ongoing-manoeuvre information is retained. The old sentence requiring another modality for lane-change announcement is absent from the new 5.5.4.1.9.2 text. It is a separate obligation, not the R-064 timing obligation, so it is not folded into R-064. Full-corpus context showed no other clause replacing the timing obligation; neighbouring 5.5.4.1.9.1 and 5.5.4.1.9.3 are unchanged and cover different obligations. Annex 3 defines 'shall aim to' as a non-absolute obligation, so the aim wording is kept. 6.2.7 (3 seconds of indication to other road users) is a different obligation and was not substituted. The previous modified decision is confirmed.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so there is nothing further to resolve. The old R-065 obligation is that when there is a risk of imminent collision or the information would conflict with information about an ongoing manoeuvre, the system visually informs the driver as far in advance as possible, and the time may be reduced. New 5.5.4.1.9.2 (p.20) keeps this sentence word for word: 'If there is a risk of imminent collision or it would conflict with the information about an ongoing manoeuvre, the time may be reduced and system shall visually inform the driver as far in advance as possible.' The conditions (imminent collision or conflict with ongoing-manoeuvre information), the visual modality and the 'as far in advance as possible' standard are all unchanged. What changed in the new paragraph is separate: the first sentence now sets a 3-second target for visual information, and a new final sentence requires evidence to the Type Approval Authority when notice is under 3 seconds. The old lane-change second paragraph (announcement by another modality) is not in the new 5.5.4.1.9.2 text supplied. Those are different obligations and are not substituted for R-065. The neighbouring clauses 5.5.4.1.9.1 and 5.5.4.1.9.3 and the references to 5.5.4.1.8 are unchanged, and no other supplied new clause alters or replaces this obligation. The new paragraph is on p.20 and was located directly by its paragraph number and lexical match, not inferred from absence in the retrieved candidates. The decision is unchanged, so new_text and source fields are null.

Old 5.5.4.1.9.2 (p.18) ended with: 'In addition, the initiation of a lane change procedure shall be announced by another modality unless the system has assessed that the driver has observed the visual information.' New 5.5.4.1.9.2 (p.20) replaces this: it requires visual information at least 3 seconds ahead (or sufficient notice), allows reduced time for imminent collision or conflict, and requires manufacturer evidence if notice is under 3 seconds. The sentence on a lane-change announcement by another modality is no longer there. The retrieval covered neighbouring clauses 5.5.4.1.1, 5.5.4.1.8.3, 5.5.4.1.9, 5.5.4.1.9.1, 5.5.4.1.9.3, 6.2.7, 6.2.8, 6.2.9, 6.3.9.3, 6.3.9.4 and Annex 4 lane-change tests. None of them imposes the same obligation. 5.5.4.1.1(b),(g) only require informing the driver, without a different modality or the observed-visual-information exception. 6.2.7 concerns indicating the lane change to other road users, not the driver. 6.2.8 covers an optical plus acoustic or haptic signal only when the lane change is suppressed, which is a different trigger. 6.2.9 appears only as a heading, with no text supplied. The 3-second evidence provision in new 5.5.4.1.9.2 is a related but different obligation (visual timing, not a second modality), so it does not replace R-066. There are no Track B handoffs (handoffs is empty), so none need resolving. The removal rests on the supplied text being absent, not on a missing retrieval hit. This holds only for the supplied new context, in which 6.2.9 has no body text. The earlier removal decision is confirmed.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The old requirement is 5.5.4.2.2.1 (p.18): the warning shall guide the driver on the required actions to support appropriate engagement in the driving task. The new context has 5.5.4.2.2.1 on p.20 with identical wording, in the same parent 5.5.4.2.2 (General Requirements for Driver Disengagement Warnings). The obligation, its subject (the warning), its applicability and its parent heading are all unchanged; only the page number moved. Neighbouring clauses: old 5.5.4.2.2.3 (prioritising warnings of emergency assistance systems such as AEBS) appears as new 5.5.4.2.2.2. This is a renumbering of a different obligation and does not alter R-067. Cross-references 5.1.1 (driver remains engaged, per 5.5.4.2) and 5.1.2 (demonstrated by 5.5.4) are identical in old and new. The 5.5.4.2 introduction is also identical. New 5.5.4.1.9.4 (manoeuvre visualisation) is a different driver-information provision and is not a substitute. No removal or modification is supported, so new_text and source fields are null.

The old requirement (5.5.4.2.2.3, p.18) states that the warning and escalation strategy shall consider for and prioritize warning strategies of simultaneously activated emergency assistance systems (e.g. AEBS). The new text at 5.5.4.2.2.2 (p.20), under the same heading 5.5.4.2.2 'General Requirements for Driver Disengagement Warnings', is word-for-word identical. Only the paragraph number and page changed, because the new version dropped or renumbered a sibling clause. Neighbouring clauses are also unchanged: 5.5.4.2.2.1 (warning guides driver), 5.5.4.2.3 (Types of Warnings), 5.5.4.1.4 (prioritization of parallel messages by urgency), and 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 (DCAS must not suppress AEBS longitudinal functionality). No applicability condition, scope or obligation was altered. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve (handoffs list is empty). The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed. No new source is cited because the decision is unchanged.

Old 5.5.4.2.3.2.1 (p.19) requires an EOR to be a continual visual information combined with at least one other modality, clear and easily perceptible, unless it can be ensured the driver has observed the visual information. The new corpus has 5.5.4.2.3.2.1 (p.21) with identical wording, under the same parent 5.5.4.2.3.2 (Eyes On Request), so the obligation, its applicability and the exception are unchanged. Only the page changed (19 to 21). Neighboring clauses are consistent: 5.5.4.2.3.2.2 (EOR confirmation) is unchanged and 5.5.4.2.6.2.3 (escalated EOR containing acoustic and/or haptic information) is a separate escalation obligation, not a replacement. No handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The new clause 5.5.4.2.6.2.2 (immediate EOR on renewed visual disengagement) is a different obligation and is not folded into R-069. Because the new text is identical, null new_text and source fields apply.

No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so there is nothing further to resolve. R-070 is the first sentence of 5.5.4.2.5.2: the driver is deemed visually disengaged when eye gaze and/or head posture, as relevant, is directed away from any currently driving task relevant area. Para 5.5.4.2.5.2 on new p.21 repeats this sentence verbatim. The dashboard/instrument panel treatment changed in a later sentence: it was previously not a relevant area, and now may be one only while manoeuvre-relevant information is displayed, for at most 3 seconds. A new sentence also says the EOR warning time is not extended by dashboard gaze. These are separate obligations on the scope of the relevant area and on EOR timing. They do not change the disengagement definition in R-070, and I did not fold them into R-070. Neighbouring clauses are consistent with this: 5.5.4.2.5.1 (detection based on eye gaze, with head posture optional) is identical. 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 (reengagement, at least 200 ms) is reworded to exclude the dashboard and instrument panel, which is a separate reengagement obligation. The EOR clauses 5.5.4.2.6.2.1 and 5.5.4.2.6.2.2 are unchanged in substance, and they depend on the disengagement definition, which is still the same. The dependency changes in the dashboard exception and in 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 were reviewed, and they do not alter the text or the applicability of R-070. The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed.

Old 5.5.4.2.5.2 (p.19) required the manufacturer to specify, in the documentation provided to the Type Approval Authority, an outline of the driving task relevant areas and when they are relevant. New 5.5.4.2.5.2 (p.21) contains the same sentence word for word. Only the dashboard and instrument panel sentence changed: it was previously excluded as a relevant area, and is now allowed as a relevant area for up to 3 seconds while manoeuvre information is displayed. A new sentence says the EOR warning time shall not be extended by gaze time on the dashboard. These changes affect how visual disengagement is assessed, not the documentation duty. The related Annex 3 Appendix 2 para 2.1.1.4 (old p.45, new p.50) is also unchanged and still requires the outline of the relevant areas and their limits. It cross-refers to 5.5.4.2.5.2. The neighbouring 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 was revised on reengagement, and 5.5.4.2.5.2.2 (sufficient duration outline) is unchanged. Neither replaces or removes the obligation in R-071. No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none needed resolving. The obligation remains in the new text, so it is not removed, and the unchanged decision stands.

old_reviews.new_text: For the purpose of the assessment of visual disengagement, the dashboard and instrument panel may be considered as a driving task relevant area only while manoeuvre relevant information (as detailed in paragraph 5.5.4.1.8.1. or 5.5.4.1.9.4.) is displayed, for a maximum duration of 3 seconds. The EOR warning time shall not be extended with the time the driver's gaze is directed towards the dashboard or instrument panel.
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff (modified_existing, R-072, para 5.5.4.2.5.2, p.21): resolved as modified. The old text (p.19) said the dashboard and instrument panel shall not be considered a driving task relevant area. The supplied new para 5.5.4.2.5.2 (p.21) reverses this to a limited permission: they may be considered relevant only while manoeuvre relevant information (per 5.5.4.1.8.1 or 5.5.4.1.9.4) is displayed, for at most 3 seconds. The same paragraph adds that the EOR warning time shall not be extended by gaze time on the dashboard or instrument panel. This sentence is part of the same clause and limits the same permission, so it is kept in the updated obligation. The references 5.5.4.1.8.1 (visual information on a proposed manoeuvre) and 5.5.4.1.9.4 (visualization of the intended manoeuvre) still exist in the new context, so the dependency is intact. Neighbouring clause 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 (reengagement, which excludes the dashboard and instrument panel) is a separate obligation and is not folded into R-072. The old requirement is therefore not unchanged or removed.

old_reviews.new_text: The driver shall be deemed to be visually reengaged following an aversion of eye gaze or head posture if either is re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area, with the exception of the dashboard and the instrument panel, for a sufficient duration depending on the situation.
old_reviews.reason: Handoff resolved as modified (modified_existing, R-073). Evidence: old 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 (p.19) covered 'visually engaged or reengaged' and counted any currently driving task relevant area. New 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 (p.21) says only 'visually reengaged following an aversion', so 'engaged or' is dropped. It also excludes the dashboard and instrument panel as re-direction targets. The same obligation is retained at the same ID, so this is not removed or unchanged. The 200 ms minimum was already in the old clause and is not part of R-073's old text, so it is not added here. Neighbouring clauses were checked and do not replace this obligation. New 5.5.4.2.5.2 (p.21) lets the dashboard and instrument panel count as relevant areas for disengagement only while manoeuvre information is shown, for up to 3 s. That is a separate disengagement-assessment obligation, not a substitute for the reengagement exception, and it is not folded into R-073. 5.5.4.2.5.2.2 on the sufficient duration is unchanged.

old_reviews.new_text: The duration for which the driver's eye gaze or head posture must be re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area, with the exception of the dashboard and the instrument panel, for the driver to be deemed visually reengaged following an aversion of eye gaze or head posture shall be at least 200 milliseconds.
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff (R-074, modified_existing) resolved as modified. In the new text, paragraph 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 (page 21) keeps the 200 ms minimum, but the clause now covers reengagement only. The old wording 'engaged or reengaged' is gone, and the target area now excludes the dashboard and instrument panel. The old clause (page 19) had no such exclusion. Neighbouring clauses are consistent. New 5.5.4.2.5.2 allows the dashboard and instrument panel as a relevant area only for the visual disengagement assessment, and only while manoeuvre information is displayed for up to 3 seconds. Under 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 they still cannot count for reengagement. 5.5.4.2.5.2.2 (sufficient duration specified by the manufacturer) is a separate obligation and is unchanged. The 200 ms obligation is retained, not removed, and the modification stays within the same obligation. This agrees with the previous decision.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The old requirement (UN R171 5.5.4.2.6.2.3, page 20) says that on continued visual disengagement the EOR is escalated at the latest 3 seconds after the initial EOR, per the warning strategy, with increased intensity. The new context has 5.5.4.2.6.2.3 on page 22 with identical wording for that obligation: 'In the event of continued visual disengagement, the EOR shall be escalated at the latest 3 seconds after the initial EOR according to the warning strategy with increased intensity.' The 3-second limit, the trigger and the increased-intensity condition are all unchanged. The second sentence, that the escalated EOR always contains acoustic and/or haptic information, was already in the old text and is not part of R-075. Neighboring clauses are also unchanged: 5.5.4.2.6.2.1 (EOR at 5 s of visual disengagement above 10 km/h), 5.5.4.2.6.2.2 (immediate EOR on re-disengagement), 5.5.4.2.6.3.1 (DCA within 5 s after EOR escalation) and 5.5.4.2.6.4.1 (driver unavailability response). The lead-in 5.5.4.2.6 is identical, with the same permission to skip, delay or suppress warning stages. The only differences in the new corpus are the page numbers, the added HOR-withholding text in 5.5.4.2.6.5 (highway-like roads), and a punctuation fix in 5.5.4.2.6.2.2. None of these changes the EOR escalation obligation. No explicit reference or dependency change affects R-075, so the requirement stays unchanged.

Old 5.5.4.2.6.2.3 (page 20) and new 5.5.4.2.6.2.3 (page 22) are word for word identical: 'In the event of continued visual disengagement, the EOR shall be escalated at the latest 3 seconds after the initial EOR according to the warning strategy with increased intensity. The escalated EOR shall always contain acoustic and/or haptic information.' The obligation and its condition (continued visual disengagement, escalated EOR, acoustic and/or haptic content) are preserved. Neighboring clauses are also unchanged apart from page shifts: 5.5.4.2.6.2.1 (EOR after 5 s of visual disengagement above 10 km/h), 5.5.4.2.6.2.2 (immediate EOR on renewed disengagement) and the 5.5.4.2.6 preamble (stages may be skipped, combined, suppressed or delayed). The only new numbering is 5.5.4.2.2.2, which replaces old 5.5.4.2.2.3 and has identical text, and it does not affect this requirement. The references 5.5.4.1.3 and 5.5.4.1.4 are unchanged. No handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The unchanged decision rests on the identical clause text, not on any absence from retrieval.

old_reviews.new_text: The manufacturer shall describe in detail, as part of the documentation required for section 9 and as outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2., the boundary conditions under which HORs can be withheld when the vehicle is located on a "Highway" or a "Highway-like" road (as defined in paragraph 2.28.1.) and is operated at a speed up to 130 km/h.
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff resolved as modified: new paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.5 (pages 22-23) keeps the documentation duty, cross-referenced to 5.3.5.2 and section 9, and the old text is not removed. The withholding scope widens from "Highway" only to "Highway" or "Highway-like" road at up to 130 km/h. Paragraph 2.28.1 defines "Highway-like road" as a non-highway section with at least two lanes per direction, a speed limit of at least 80 km/h, no prohibition of pedestrians and cyclists, a physical separation and no at-grade crossings or intersections. The retrieved 5.3.5.2 is unchanged in substance, so the cross-reference still holds. The new clause's extra duties are separate obligations and are not folded into R-077: the 500 m / 30 s road-ahead verification and the documentation of equivalent strategies, the cyclist demonstration, and the 7-second HOR before the end of a highway-like road. The old paragraph's page-20 text is superseded, and the updated source is page 22, paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.5.

old_reviews.new_text: While the system is in the mode of operation in which HORs are withheld (on a "Highway" or a "Highway-like" road at speeds up to 130 km/h), if the system has the ability to suppress accelerator input in order to avoid exceeding the system boundaries, the driver shall be able to override this suppression of accelerator input.
old_reviews.reason: The old R-078 (5.5.4.2.6.5.3) is retained in the new text at 5.5.4.2.6.5.3, page 23, with identical wording, so the core obligation is unchanged. The previous decision treated the clause in isolation. Neighbouring context shows the parent paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.5 changed. Old text: HOR withholding on a "Highway" only. New text: "Highway" or "Highway-like" road, up to 130 km/h, and the lead-in now says the subparagraphs apply "regardless if operated on a highway or a highway-like road". The subparagraph's applicability scope therefore widened through its parent. This is a dependency change that was reviewed and not modified automatically. The obligation itself (driver override of accelerator suppression) is unchanged, but its applicability condition is now broader, so the requirement is restated with the updated scope. No handoffs were supplied, so none needed resolving. The related 5.5.3.4.1.3 (accelerator override of longitudinal assistance) is a different obligation and was not substituted. I found no evidence of removal.

Old R-079 (UN R171 5.5.4.2.6.5.4, p.21) requires an EOR at the latest when the driver has been visually disengaged for the relevant time in the table (3.5 s at 130 km/h, 5.0 s at 10-60 km/h), notwithstanding 5.5.4.2.6.2.1. The new 5.5.4.2.6.5.4 (p.23) has identical text, the identical table and the same linear interpolation for 60-130 km/h. The referenced 5.5.4.2.6.2.1 (5 s EOR at speeds above 10 km/h) is also unchanged (p.22). No handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The new lead-in 5.5.4.2.6.5 extends withholding of HORs to 'Highway-like' roads and adds conditions (a)-(c). It also states that the subparagraphs apply 'regardless if operated on a highway or a highway-like road'. This widens the scope in which the unchanged EOR timing applies but does not alter the EOR obligation, so it is a dependency change reviewed here, not a modification. Neighboring clauses 5.5.4.2.6.5.5 (EOR on no gaze deviation) and 5.5.4.2.6.2.2/.3 are separate obligations and were not substituted. Evidence was found by matching the paragraph number and text in the new context, so retrieval is positive and no removal question arises.

Old 5.5.4.2.6.5.4 (page 21) and new 5.5.4.2.6.5.4 (page 23) contain the same sentence: for vehicle speeds between 60 and 130 km/h, a linear interpolation shall be used to calculate the corresponding EOR timing. The table is identical in both versions (130 km/h = 3.5 s; 10 to 60 km/h = 5.0 s). The parent 5.5.4.2.6.5 (Withholding of HORs) was extended in the new text to cover highway-like roads, with added conditions (a) to (c). The new text also says the subparagraphs apply regardless of whether the vehicle is on a highway or a highway-like road. These changes widen the scope of the mode but do not change the interpolation obligation or its 60 to 130 km/h range. The neighboring clauses 5.5.4.2.6.5.1, .3 and .5 are also unchanged, apart from the page renumbering. The definition of EOR in 2.33 is identical. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve (handoffs list is empty). The retrieved candidates show no explicit references that alter the obligation. Because the parent condition changed, I reviewed the dependency, and it does not require modifying this requirement.

Old 5.5.4.2.7 required that the driver state monitoring system be equipped with strategies to assess driver disengagement when no driver input has been determined over prolonged periods (e.g. negative drowsiness determination), and implement appropriate countermeasures. New 5.5.4.2.7.1 (page 24) has the same obligation, same trigger (no driver input over prolonged periods) and same scope, with countermeasures retained. 'Be equipped with' became 'have', which is wording only. The added example 'or assessment of changes in gaze direction' is a non-limiting e.g. and does not alter the obligation. No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none needed resolution. The new 5.5.4.2.7.2 is a separately introduced obligation, with its own applicability (phases where system-initiated manoeuvres are possible) and its own consistent-engagement assessments, consequences and documentation. It is not folded into R-081 and does not substitute for it. Neighboring clauses 5.5.4.2.1.1, 5.5.4.2.5 and 5.5.4.2.8 changed in other ways, but they are different obligations and do not change R-081. The old requirement is therefore retained unchanged, based on the matching new clause 5.5.4.2.7.1 rather than on absence from retrieval.

old_reviews.new_text: The driver state monitoring system shall implement appropriate countermeasures in the event that no driver input has been determined over prolonged periods (e.g. through a negative determination of driver drowsiness or assessment of changes in gaze direction).
old_reviews.reason: Old 5.5.4.2.7 (p.21) required countermeasures when no driver input is determined over prolonged periods, with drowsiness as the example. New 5.5.4.2.7.1 (p.24) keeps that obligation: 'and implement appropriate countermeasures' under the same condition. The only change is that the example list now includes 'assessment of changes in gaze direction', a modest widening of the illustrative scope. The handoff disposition is modified_existing for R-082, and I agree with it. The countermeasure obligation is kept separate from the assessment-strategies obligation, which the prior decision folded into the same text; this text is limited to the countermeasure duty. Neighboring 5.5.4.2.7.2 (system-initiated manoeuvres, drowsiness and gaze-change assessment, countermeasures per the safety concept) and 5.5.4.2.8 (disablement after insufficient engagement) are different obligations with different conditions, so they do not replace R-082 and are not folded into it. The reference paragraph numbers and the dependencies in 5.3.5.1 are unaffected by this requirement. The retrieved clause evidence confirms that the obligation is retained, so removal is not warranted.

old_reviews.new_text: While the powertrain is active, when the driver is detected to have insufficient engagement, the system shall be disabled for a period of at least 30 minutes. The disablement shall happen once the driver has resumed control of the vehicle, or the vehicle has become stationary.
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff (modified_existing, R-083, new 5.5.4.2.8.1, page 24) resolved as modified. Old 5.5.4.2.8.1 (page 21) required the system to be disabled for at least 30 minutes whilst the powertrain is active when the driver is detected to have insufficient engagement. The new 5.5.4.2.8.1 (page 24) keeps that obligation with the same applicability conditions (powertrain active, insufficient engagement detected, at least 30 minutes), so it is the same obligation and not a separate addition or a new ID. It adds the sentence: 'The disablement shall happen once the driver has resumed control of the vehicle, or the vehicle has become stationary.' This changes when the disablement takes effect. Neighboring clauses 5.5.4.2.8.2 (page 24) and 5.5.4.2.8.3 only define what counts as insufficient engagement (new items (d) and (e) were added to the criteria). They are related but different obligations, so they are not substituted for R-083 and are not folded into it. The 5.5.4.2.8.4 and 5.5.4.1.1(h) information obligations are likewise separate. The dependency change in 5.5.4.2.8.2 needs its own review and does not by itself modify R-083. The new text is found in the supplied new source, so there is no ground for removal or for leaving the requirement unchanged.

old_reviews.new_text: When the system is disabled due to insufficient engagement by the driver, the system shall only be re-enabled after the driver has confirmed by a deliberate action their understanding of their responsibilities and appropriate use of the system.
old_reviews.reason: Track B handoff (modified_existing, R-084, 5.5.4.2.8.4, page 24) resolved as modified. Evidence: the old 5.5.4.2.8.4 (page 21) required the system, at the latest upon powertrain deactivation, to request that the driver read the paragraph 5.6 driver information material when disabled for insufficient engagement. The supplied new clause 5.5.4.2.8.4 (page 24) has the same trigger (system disabled due to insufficient engagement) but a different obligation: re-enablement is permitted only after the driver confirms by a deliberate action their understanding of their responsibilities and appropriate use. The powertrain-deactivation timing and the request to read 5.6 material are not in the new clause. Neighbouring clauses 5.5.4.2.8.1 (disablement of at least 30 minutes, now with timing after the driver resumes control or the vehicle is stationary) and 5.5.4.2.8.3 (repeated EOR/HOR) set the disablement trigger and definition, not this obligation. New 5.6 still lists information content, but contains no request-to-read obligation, so it cannot substitute for the old one. The same-ID modification is the only candidate, and the old obligation does not survive unchanged elsewhere. Annex 3 / 3.5.7 (old context), a documented information strategy encouraging review of materials, is a separate documentation obligation and is not the old requirement. The handoff is therefore confirmed as modified, not unchanged or removed.

No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. The old R-088 comes from paragraph 6.2.4 (page 23 in the old text). The new context has paragraph 6.2.4 on page 26 with identical wording: a lane change manoeuvre shall only be started if a vehicle in the target lane is not forced to unmanageably decelerate due to the lane change. The obligation, the 'shall' strength and the conditions are the same. Neighbouring clauses 6.2.4.1 to 6.2.4.4 are the quantitative assessment rules. New text appears only in 6.2.4.1: a deviation allowed up to 60 km/h, with the manufacturer explaining the distances and timings and providing evidence. That text is a separate provision in a different paragraph, so it is not folded into R-088, and it does not change the 6.2.4 obligation. The 5.3.7.2.3.6 and 5.3.7.2.4.5 clauses cover manoeuvre proposal or initiation and use different wording ('shall not propose' or 'shall aim to not initiate'), so they are related but different obligations and do not replace R-088. The Annex 3 Appendix 2 item 4.3 on evidence is documentation and does not alter the obligation. Definitions 2.10 to 2.12 are unchanged apart from page numbers and a minor wording tweak in 2.11 that does not affect meaning. The old text and the new text both contain 6.2.4 in full, so the requirement is unchanged rather than missing or removed.

old_reviews.new_text: When there is an approaching vehicle during a lane change, the DCAS system shall be designed to not make the approaching vehicle decelerate at a higher level than 3.0 m/s² in order to ensure that the distance between the two vehicles is never less than that which the DCAS vehicle travels in 1 second, assessed assuming the approaching vehicle begins its deceleration 1.4 s after the system starts the lateral movement of the lane change and either 0.4 s after the lane change manoeuvre starts (if the approaching vehicle was detected for at least 1.0 s immediately before the manoeuvre starts) or 1.4 s after the manoeuvre starts. At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from this assessment; in that case the manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the distances and timings for an approaching vehicle under which a lane change can be started, and provide evidence that those situations are deemed controllable for other road users.
old_reviews.reason: The previous 'unchanged' decision is not supported. The 3.0 m/s² and 1-second-distance sentence in 6.2.4.1 is verbatim identical in old and new text. However, the new 6.2.4.1 (pages 26-27) adds a sentence: 'At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from this assessment', with manufacturer explanation and evidence obligations. This sentence sits inside the same paragraph and directly modifies how the old obligation is assessed and applied, so it is a change to the applicability and conditions of R-089, not a separate procedure. The old text states the obligation without exception, and the new text introduces an exception for speeds up to 60 km/h with documentation duties. The neighbouring clauses 6.2.4, 6.2.4.2, 6.2.4.3 and 6.2.4.4 are textually unchanged. They still refer to 6.2.4.1, so they need no separate modification. No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs list is empty), so none needed resolution. The new_text keeps the original obligation and adds the 60 km/h deviation condition, citing new paragraph 6.2.4.1.

old_reviews.new_text: The DCAS shall perform the assessment of the approaching vehicle's deceleration with the assumption that the approaching vehicle begins its deceleration 1.4 seconds after the system starts the lateral movement of the lane change procedure. At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from this assessment; in these cases the manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the distances and timings for an approaching vehicle under which a lane change manoeuvre can be started, and provide evidence that those situations are deemed controllable for other road users.
old_reviews.reason: No Track B handoffs were supplied, so none need resolving. Old and new 6.2.4.1(a) are verbatim identical: 1.4 s after the start of lateral movement. However, the new 6.2.4.1 adds a closing paragraph, absent in the old text, that lets the system deviate from this assessment at speeds up to 60 km/h. It is conditional on the manufacturer explaining distances and timings to the Type Approval Authority and providing controllability evidence. That paragraph qualifies the assessment this requirement mandates, so the old unconditional wording is no longer accurate, and the previous 'unchanged' decision is overturned. The 1.4 s assumption itself is retained and is not replaced by the neighbouring 6.2.4.1(b) timings. The neighbouring clauses 6.2.4.2 to 6.2.4.4 are textually unchanged and refer to 6.2.4.1, so they do not alter the obligation. The new text is cited from the supplied new 6.2.4.1, spanning pages 26-27.

old_reviews.new_text: The assessment of the approaching vehicle's deceleration shall be performed with the assumptions that the approaching vehicle begins its deceleration either: (i) 0.4 seconds after the system starts the lane change manoeuvre, provided that the approaching vehicle was detected by the DCAS vehicle for a duration of at least 1.0 seconds immediately before the lane change manoeuvre starts; or (ii) 1.4 seconds after the system starts the lane change manoeuvre. At speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from this assessment; in these cases the manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the distances and timings for an approaching vehicle under which a lane change manoeuvre can be started, and provide evidence of those situations being deemed controllable for other road users.
old_reviews.reason: Reassessed against the new 6.2.4.1 (new pages 26-27), with neighboring clauses 6.2.4, 6.2.4.2 to 6.2.4.4 and 6.2.5 checked. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve. The previous 'unchanged' decision treated the 60 km/h deviation sentence as separate, but it is an exception that qualifies this very assessment. The 0.4 s and 1.4 s timing assumptions and the 1.0 s detection condition are verbatim identical to the old text. The new text adds a speed-based applicability condition: at speeds up to 60 km/h the system may deviate from the assessment. When it does, the manufacturer must explain to the Type Approval Authority the distances and timings under which a lane change can start, and provide evidence that those situations are controllable for other road users. Leaving the old text unchanged would state the assessment as unconditional, which no longer matches the source, so the requirement is modified. The 6.2.4.2 assessment refers back to 6.2.4.1 and so inherits the same assumptions, and 6.2.5 requires demonstration of the 6.2.4 implementation. Neither neighboring clause replaces this obligation. The Annex 4 lane-change tests are unchanged in substance, with only page shifts. The old requirement was not removed, because the new 6.2.4.1(b) still carries it.

Reassessed R-104 (old 7.2.3.1, p.27) against the new 7.2.3.1 (new pp.30-32). The new text keeps the same first sentence word for word: the manufacturer shall report at least once a year to the Type Approval Authority on the information deemed proper evidence of the intended operation collected through the monitoring program and safety of the system in the field, until production is definitively discontinued according to paragraph 14. Frequency, addressee, subject matter and end condition are unchanged. The neighbouring clauses 7.1.1, 7.1.2 and 7.2.3 are also identical, so the dependencies of the monitoring program have not changed. The new sentence 'The information is not intended to be shared publicly' is a separate confidentiality statement and does not alter the annual reporting duty. Table 1 changed: items 1, 2, 4, 9 and new 10 were expanded or split. Those changes concern the minimum content that must be reported, which falls under the separate sentence 'shall report at least the information listed in the table below'. They are not part of R-104's obligation, so I did not fold them into this ID. No Track B handoffs were supplied (handoffs is empty), so none needed resolution. The old requirement was found directly in the new text, so removal is not in question.

The old requirement in 7.2.3.1 (p. 27) says that if the system was subject to significant changes relevant to the reported information during the reporting period, the report shall differentiate the changes of the system. The new 7.2.3.1 (pp. 30-32) keeps this sentence word for word: "In the event that the system was subject to significant changes relevant to the reported information during the reporting period, the report shall differentiate the changes of the system." The condition (significant changes relevant to the reported information, during the reporting period) and the obligation (differentiate the changes of the system in the report) are the same. The new 7.2.3.1 adds the sentence "The information is not intended to be shared publicly", and Table 1 is expanded, for example item 1 is differentiated by DCAS capability, item 2 is split into 2.a-2.e, and items 9 and 10 are added. These changes sit beside the obligation and do not replace it. The Table 1 item 1 differentiation by capability covers a different obligation, which is the content of the occurrence reporting. It does not replace the general duty to differentiate system changes. There are no Track B handoffs to resolve (the handoffs list is empty). The neighbouring clauses 7.1.2, 7.2 and 7.2.3 are textually identical, so the old and new texts give no reason to change the requirement. The new text keeps the same periodic reporting scope, so the requirement is unchanged.

Old R-108 derives from paragraph 10.1: the vehicle manufacturer shall implement an R171SWIN so the System software can be identified. New paragraph 10.1 (page 35) contains the same first sentence, word for word in substance: 'For the purpose of ensuring the software of the System can be identified, an R171SWIN shall be implemented by the vehicle manufacturer.' The only differences are in the second sentence (optional holding on the vehicle or declaration to the Type Approval Authority), where typos are fixed ('ay' to 'may', 'R1XXSWIN' to 'R171SWIN'). Those fixes do not touch the implementation obligation, and the declaration alternative applies only if the R171SWIN is not held on the vehicle. Neighbouring and referenced clauses were checked: new 2.21 defines R171SWIN as a manufacturer-defined identifier for type-approval-relevant software of the Electronic Control System, which supports the obligation but does not create a different one. The heading of section 10 now reads 'software identification and updating', and 10.2 (UN R156 compliance) is a separate obligation that is textually unchanged, so neither changes R-108. Annex 1 items 16.1 and 16.2 are information-document entries that are unchanged apart from page shifts. There were no Track B handoffs to resolve (handoffs list is empty). The previous decision of unchanged is confirmed, so new_text and source fields are null.

R-113 is the Appendix 4 lead-in: the manufacturer shall declare the capability of the system and its features according to the paragraph 6 classification based on the following criteria. The new Appendix 4 text (page 52) repeats this sentence verbatim and adds that the declaration serves as reference for the Annex 4 base tests. The old requirement is still present and unchanged. Annex 3 / 3.2.4 (page 39) still requires a declaration in the Appendix 4 model, and Annex 4 / 1 refers to the declaration made under Appendix 4. The Track B handoff proposed modifying R-113 to narrow it to system-initiated manoeuvres and non-highway responses, and I resolve it as not modifying R-113. The handoff clause, Annex 3 / Appendix 4 / 4 (pages 57-58), is a specific declaration item within the criteria table. Its tables ask, for each scenario, whether the system can avoid a collision and under what preconditions. It does not replace the general lead-in obligation, which still applies to all of Appendix 4, including sections 1, 2, 2.1, 3 and 5. The claim that old section 4 also covered driver-initiated manoeuvres is not shown here, because no old-context clause for section 4 was supplied. Narrowing a sub-item is therefore a separate or related obligation, and folding it into R-113 would substitute a different obligation for the old one. Any change to section 4 should be tracked under its own requirement ID. Section 5 of the new Appendix 4 (page 58) still covers driver-initiated manoeuvres, which also argues against narrowing the general lead-in. No evidence indicates the lead-in was removed or reworded, so the decision is unchanged with null new_text and null source fields.
